items.title: REEMERGÊNCIA DE DOENÇAS PREVIAMENTE CONTROLADAS: FRAGILIDADES NOS SISTEMAS DE VIGILÂNCIA SANITÁRIA
items.summary: This integrative literature review examined the reemergence of previously controlled diseases and its relationship with weaknesses in health surveillance systems, considering epidemiological, social, and structural factors. The authors searched multiple databases using standardized descriptors related to emerging and reemerging infectious diseases, epidemiological surveillance, and public health, ultimately selecting a final sample of studies published between 2016 and 2026. The review found that disease reemergence is associated with low vaccination coverage, underreporting, antimicrobial resistance, climate change, population displacement, and structural deficiencies such as inadequate technological infrastructure and poor integration between information systems. Conversely, emerging strategies including digital surveillance, genomic monitoring, and wastewater analysis showed promise for improving early outbreak detection and epidemiological risk anticipation. The authors concluded that continuous strengthening of health surveillance, combined with integration of digital technologies, environmental monitoring, and intersectoral public policies, is essential for the prevention and control of reemerging diseases.
items.venue: Veredas do Direito Direito Ambiental e Desenvolvimento Sustentável
items.citation: Ana Beatriz da Silva Conceição, Caio Augusto Dias Carneiro, Leonardo Pinho Do Amaral et al.. REEMERGÊNCIA DE DOENÇAS PREVIAMENTE CONTROLADAS: FRAGILIDADES NOS SISTEMAS DE VIGILÂNCIA SANITÁRIA. Veredas do Direito Direito Ambiental e Desenvolvimento Sustentável. 2026

items.title: PCR-Based Molecular Diagnostics for Strengthening Environmental Pathogen Surveillance and Public Health Preparedness Across United States Communities
items.summary: This review examines the role of PCR-based molecular diagnostic technologies in strengthening environmental pathogen surveillance and public health preparedness across the United States. The authors address limitations of conventional culture-based methods, such as slow turnaround times and reduced sensitivity for fastidious organisms, and assess how various PCR approaches enable rapid detection of bacterial, viral, fungal, and protozoan pathogens from complex environmental matrices including wastewater, water, air, and soil. The review covers advances across multiple PCR modalities, including quantitative, digital, and multiplex formats, as well as point-of-need platforms, with attention to assay design, quality assurance, sample processing, and computational data interpretation. The authors also evaluate the demonstrated utility of wastewater-based epidemiology for early outbreak detection and antimicrobial resistance monitoring within national surveillance frameworks. The review concludes by discussing implementation challenges and the potential for integrating artificial intelligence with molecular diagnostics to further improve outbreak preparedness and public health resilience.
items.venue: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews
items.citation: Iyanuoluwa Oluwafemi. PCR-Based Molecular Diagnostics for Strengthening Environmental Pathogen Surveillance and Public Health Preparedness Across United States Communities. International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews. 2026

items.title: Resistance indicators in sewage microbiota mirror clinical antibiotic use with temporal lag linked to host
items.summary: This study investigated whether wastewater-based surveillance could serve as a reliable epidemiological tool for monitoring antibiotic resistance in the community, and how microbial ecological processes within sewer systems complicate the interpretation of antibiotic resistance gene signals. The researchers conducted intensive, twice-weekly sampling of a conventional wastewater treatment plant over one year, applying deep metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatics analysis alongside a multi-year dataset of community outpatient antibiotic prescription rates. They found that the relationship between sewage antibiotic resistance genes and clinical antibiotic use depended critically on the bacterial host carrying the resistance genes: genes associated with Enterobacteriaceae correlated directly and contemporaneously with antibiotic usage, while genes associated with Pseudomonadaceae showed a lagged correlation of one to three months. This temporal lag in the Pseudomonadaceae signal is interpreted as reflecting the environmental persistence and ecological dynamics of sewage-associated microbiota rather than direct human fecal input. The study concludes that accounting for the bacterial host identity and environmental stability of resistance genes is essential for extracting meaningful public health signals from wastewater surveillance of antibiotic resistance.
items.citation: Connor Brown, MA. Rumi, Lauren F. McDaniel et al.. Resistance indicators in sewage microbiota mirror clinical antibiotic use with temporal lag linked to host. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive sequence analysis reveals the vast β-lactam resistome
items.summary: This paper investigated the global distribution of β-lactamase antibiotic resistance genes across diverse microbial taxa and environmental ecosystems, addressing limitations in scalability and taxonomic resolution that have hampered previous studies. The researchers performed comprehensive sequence analysis of publicly available genomic and metagenomic data, identifying a vast number of β-lactamases spanning all five enzyme classes and mapping their occurrence across bacterial phyla and habitat types. β-lactamases were found to be remarkably prevalent in environmental microbes, approaching the abundance of a core housekeeping gene across many ecosystems, with particularly strong enrichment in wastewater and plant-associated samples. The pronounced abundance in plant environments suggests these settings as a long-standing arena for the evolutionary arms race between β-lactam-producing and resistant organisms over millions of years. The study also traces the origins of clinically relevant β-lactamases primarily to Gamma-Proteobacteria and reveals that the environmental reservoirs of these resistance genes extend well beyond wastewater into plant, terrestrial, and aquatic habitats.
items.citation: Sevan Gholipour, John Z. Chen, Dong‐Kyu Lee et al.. Comprehensive sequence analysis reveals the vast β-lactam resistome. Microbiome. 2026

items.title: Aircraft and Airport Wastewater Surveillance for Public Health Preparedness Demands an Integrated and Sustainable Approach.
items.summary: This review paper examined the use of wastewater surveillance conducted on aircraft and at airports as a public health tool for detecting and monitoring infectious pathogens among traveling populations. The authors synthesized existing evidence through a structured narrative review, drawing primarily on experience gained during the COVID-19 pandemic to assess how this approach functions and what factors shape its reliability. They found that while detection of pathogens such as SARS-CoV-2 RNA in aircraft lavatory and airport terminal wastewater can provide timely aggregate signals about pathogen circulation, the interpretation of such signals is complicated by numerous variables including pathogen shedding dynamics, flight duration, sampling matrix, and assay sensitivity. The review highlights that wastewater signals are population-level indicators and cannot be used for individual diagnosis, evidence of transmission, or attribution to specific flights or countries of origin. The authors conclude that aviation wastewater surveillance functions best as an early-warning and situational-awareness tool, but its full value depends on rigorous methodology, pathogen-specific validation, and integration with clinical and genomic surveillance systems.
items.citation: Vaidya SR, Pandey PG, Giri S et al.. Aircraft and Airport Wastewater Surveillance for Public Health Preparedness Demands an Integrated and Sustainable Approach.. Viruses. 2026

items.title: From Sewers to Surveillance: Monitoring Salmonella Through Wastewater.
items.summary: Wastewater surveillance is a population-level monitoring strategy that can detect pathogens among individuals who never seek clinical care, thereby complementing traditional disease reporting systems. This study developed and validated a methodological pipeline for detecting Salmonella in wastewater, involving sample concentration through polyethylene glycol precipitation, magnetic bead-based nucleic acid extraction, and quantitative PCR. The approach was deployed across a statewide surveillance network, where it revealed seasonal transmission patterns and provided approximately one week of advance warning ahead of clinical case reports. Importantly, the system identified outbreak activity that passive clinical surveillance had missed entirely. While limitations such as low pathogen concentrations in samples and insufficient resolution at the serovar level remain, the authors conclude that integrating wastewater surveillance with conventional public health infrastructure offers meaningful potential for early outbreak detection and a deeper understanding of Salmonella transmission dynamics.
items.citation: Kuhn KG, Shelton K, Rimal B et al.. From Sewers to Surveillance: Monitoring Salmonella Through Wastewater.. Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.). 2027

items.title: Multi-virus Wastewater Surveillance in Heterogeneous Urban-Sewage Systems: Comparative Insights From Sewage Treatment Plants and Open Drains.
items.summary: This study examined how different types of urban wastewater infrastructure affect the detection and interpretation of pathogen signals in wastewater-based epidemiology, focusing on Mumbai's fragmented sewer network. Researchers collected wastewater samples during two monitoring periods from both centralized sewage treatment plants and decentralized open drains, analyzing them for SARS-CoV-2, influenza viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus using RT-qPCR. Centralized treatment plants showed higher and more consistent viral detection rates, reflecting signal integration across larger populations, while open drains displayed greater temporal variability consistent with more localized, short-term transmission dynamics. SARS-CoV-2 was reliably detected across both infrastructure types, whereas influenza detection was more sporadic and variable, suggesting seasonal patterns, and co-detection of influenza A and B subtypes was observed. The authors conclude that wastewater signal profiles reflect both pathogen-specific characteristics and the structural configuration of the sampling network, and advocate for integrated surveillance frameworks combining centralized and decentralized nodes alongside clinical validation to strengthen epidemiological interpretation.
items.citation: Shaikh A, Nikam S, Mistry N. Multi-virus Wastewater Surveillance in Heterogeneous Urban-Sewage Systems: Comparative Insights From Sewage Treatment Plants and Open Drains.. Food and environmental virology. 2026

items.title: A Rapid Decision Framework for Wastewater and Environmental Surveillance (WES) during Rapidly Emerging and Evolving Outbreak Settings
items.citation: Ahmed W, Medlicott K, Nolan M. A Rapid Decision Framework for Wastewater and Environmental Surveillance (WES) during Rapidly Emerging and Evolving Outbreak Settings. ACS ES&T water. 2026

items.title: Wastewater pathogen composition in Atlanta, GA prior to and during the 2026 FIFA World Cup
items.summary: This study examined whether the 2026 FIFA World Cup influenced the detection of infectious pathogens in wastewater in Atlanta, Georgia, one of the host cities. Researchers collected wastewater samples from three water reclamation facilities over several months spanning periods before, during, and after the tournament, testing them with multiplexed PCR panels targeting a broad range of respiratory and gastrointestinal pathogens. The primary analysis found no statistically significant differences in pathogen detection between the pre-tournament and tournament periods. A sensitivity analysis that included the post-tournament period identified a significant increase in SARS-CoV-2 detection, but this increase aligned with broader regional and national trends rather than being attributable to the event itself. The study demonstrates the feasibility of using qualitative, multiplexed PCR-based wastewater surveillance as a complementary tool for monitoring infectious disease during large mass gathering events, while acknowledging limitations including wide confidence intervals and limited post-event sampling.
items.citation: Raymo N, Kraft CS, Gulick D et al.. Wastewater pathogen composition in Atlanta, GA prior to and during the 2026 FIFA World Cup. 2026

items.title: Machine learning-enabled wastewater-based surveillance for emerging pathogen detection and monitoring: current applications, challenges, and future prospects.
items.summary: This review examined how machine learning is being applied to wastewater-based surveillance to detect and monitor emerging pathogens at the community level. The authors conducted a narrative review of published literature, classifying studies by analytical approach across four tiers ranging from classical statistical models to deep learning and hybrid mechanistic methods, and evaluated evidence across five analytical tasks including forecasting, anomaly detection, and data harmonization. The reviewed work was heavily dominated by studies focused on SARS-CoV-2, with early-warning evidence most strongly supported by classical statistical approaches rather than more complex machine learning methods, and performance across studies was highly context-dependent. Key barriers identified include sampling variability, laboratory inconsistencies, population-dependent biases, and the high-dimensional complexity of wastewater signals, all of which limit generalizability and validation. The authors call for standardized collaborative frameworks, multimodal data integration, mechanistic modeling with explicit uncertainty quantification, and attention to governance and public acceptability to advance the field beyond its current predominantly retrospective and pathogen-specific scope.
items.citation: Song A, Jia P, Luo J et al.. Machine learning-enabled wastewater-based surveillance for emerging pathogen detection and monitoring: current applications, challenges, and future prospects.. Emerging microbes & infections. 2026

items.title: Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of accurately estimating the transmission dynamics of co-circulating SARS-CoV-2 variants. The authors extended existing epidemiological methods for inferring effective reproduction numbers from case count data to jointly incorporate genetic sequencing data, enabling simultaneous estimation of variant-specific effective reproduction numbers and variant frequencies. This joint modeling framework also allows structured relationships between reproduction numbers to be inferred across time series, including fixed variant-specific growth advantages that remain consistent across locations. Applying the method to data from United States states spanning early 2021 through early 2022, they estimated variant-specific effective reproduction numbers for multiple variants of concern and interest and identified consistent growth advantages for particular variants across different geographic locations. The study demonstrates that combining case and sequencing data provides richer epidemiological insights into variant dynamics than sequence frequency data alone.
items.citation: Marlin D Figgins, Trevor Bedford. Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data. eLife. 2026

items.title: Developing an AI-Powered Occupational Health Surveillance System for Real-Time Detection and Management of Workplace Health Hazards
items.summary: This paper addresses the limitations of traditional occupational health surveillance systems, which suffer from delayed hazard detection and poor adaptability to dynamic workplace conditions. The authors propose an artificial intelligence-powered surveillance framework that integrates wearable devices and Internet of Things sensors to continuously collect data on both environmental conditions and individual employee health metrics. Machine learning algorithms and predictive analytics are applied to these data streams to identify patterns, detect anomalies, and anticipate risks before they escalate into critical incidents. The system also includes a dashboard for visualizing findings, generating automated compliance documentation, and delivering actionable safety recommendations to both managers and workers. The authors conclude that this scalable framework can be adapted across industries and has broad potential to reduce workplace injuries, support regulatory compliance, and improve overall employee well-being.
items.venue: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
items.citation: Cynthia Obianuju Ozobu. Developing an AI-Powered Occupational Health Surveillance System for Real-Time Detection and Management of Workplace Health Hazards. WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY. 2026

items.title: SciCheck: A Framework for Verifying the Integrity of Deep Learning Training
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of verifying the integrity of deep learning training within scientific workflows, where stochastic processes prevent simple recomputation checks. The authors developed SciCheck, a framework combining a provenance ledger with two verification layers: a statistical judge that compares per-step gradient statistics between a submitted run and a verifier's reference run, and a spot-check that re-executes randomly sampled training segments whose checkpoints are committed incrementally. The system was evaluated against attacks including gradient sign flipping, label poisoning, and fully fabricated runs across three neural network architectures, achieving high integrity detection while keeping false rejection of honest runs very low. The study characterizes the theoretical detection guarantees of each layer, showing that statistical methods alone suffice for strong gradient manipulations but fail against fabricated runs that replay genuine statistics, while the spot-check provides probabilistic soundness guarantees that scale predictably with the number of sampled segments. Overall, SciCheck achieves strong verification performance at a computational cost of roughly one to two times a single retraining, with efficient checkpoint storage through per-epoch commitments.
items.citation: Alexander Nguyen, Dylan Gresham, Gaby G. Dagher et al.. SciCheck: A Framework for Verifying the Integrity of Deep Learning Training. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Locating Contact on Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots From Tendon Measurements Alone via Constrained Moving Horizon Estimation
items.summary: This paper investigates the problem of detecting and localizing contact along tendon-driven continuum robots using only tendon tension measurements, without additional dedicated contact sensors. The authors first establish that this is a fundamental structural limitation: the mapping from contact forces to tendon measurements has a non-trivial null space, making free contact localization impossible without additional constraints. They show that when the obstacle geometry is known, incorporating non-penetration and complementarity conditions renders the contact force locally identifiable and the system locally exponentially strongly detectable. To exploit this, they develop a constrained moving horizon estimator formulated as a quadratic program that encodes these geometric conditions and runs in real time. In benchmark simulations of a robot pressing and sliding along a wall, the proposed estimator substantially outperformed a tuned extended Kalman filter in both contact location and force estimation accuracy, and remained robust to obstacle position errors, unmodeled friction, and randomized model mismatch across repeated trials, while offering no advantage over the Kalman filter in the absence of contact—confirming that the gains stem specifically from the contact constraints.
items.citation: Haitham El-Hussieny. Locating Contact on Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots From Tendon Measurements Alone via Constrained Moving Horizon Estimation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Health-System-Wide Mapping of Demographic Information in Routine Clinical Histopathology
items.summary: This paper investigated how much demographic information — specifically sex, age group, and self-reported race — is encoded within routine clinical histopathology slides across a broad range of organs and disease states. The researchers analyzed a very large collection of hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images drawn from hundreds of thousands of patients spanning twenty-five organs, applying pathology foundation-model representations and multiple-instance learning to systematically detect demographic signals. They found that demographic attributes were broadly recoverable across organ-demographic combinations, with performance varying by demographic category and organ, and that these signals persisted even after diagnosis-based grouping and class balancing, suggesting the associations are not simply artifacts of disease composition. Literature-guided analysis was used to generate candidate histomorphological and contextual explanations for these demographic signals. The authors conclude that this systematic mapping informs understanding of the sources of demographic-associated information in histopathology, with implications for shortcut learning risks and the development of more interpretable computational pathology models.
items.citation: Shengjia Chen, Ruchika Verma, Kevin Clare et al.. Health-System-Wide Mapping of Demographic Information in Routine Clinical Histopathology. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Designing Effective Monitor-Based Interventions for Mitigating Reward Hacking During RL
items.summary: This paper investigates how to effectively use monitors to detect and penalize reward hacking during reinforcement learning training, where models learn unintended behaviors by exploiting flaws in the reward signal. The researchers created and open-sourced three realistic environments in which a language model exhibits reward hacking through test overwriting in coding tasks, sycophancy in medical chat, and hallucination in biography generation. Through systematic study of the coding environment, they found that models can learn to evade even highly accurate monitors by exploiting systemic weaknesses in detection probes and judge models, that monitors providing richer learning signals suppress reward hacking but are more vulnerable to evasion, and that including easier training problems reduces reward hacking. Building on these findings, they designed improved monitor-based interventions for the other two environments, in some cases reducing reward hacking rates back to pre-training levels. The work demonstrates that thoughtful monitor intervention design can meaningfully mitigate reward hacking and that lessons learned in one setting can transfer to new environments.
items.citation: Aria Wong, Joshua Engels, Neel Nanda. Designing Effective Monitor-Based Interventions for Mitigating Reward Hacking During RL. arXiv. 2026

items.title: When Instruction Files Go Stale: Documentation Debt and Hidden Cost in Coding Agents
items.summary: This paper investigates how stale instruction files in coding agent repositories — documents like AGENTS.md that guide LLM-based agents during every session — create hidden inefficiencies analogous to technical debt. The researchers studied three real-world cases of outdated instructions from active open-source repositories, each representing a different type of guidance, and had agents complete maintenance tasks under stale, corrected, and removed versions of those instructions. By analyzing hundreds of agent trajectories at the level of individual tool calls, they found that agents tend to follow stale guidance when it appears relevant, sometimes even when accurate information is available elsewhere in the repository. While agents generally recovered from immediate failures caused by stale instructions, none spontaneously repaired the underlying instruction file itself, and the stale test command measurably increased tool call overhead compared to corrected instructions. The study concludes that evaluating agents solely on task success obscures the costs imposed by documentation debt, and argues for assessment methods that examine agent behavior and efficiency beyond final outcomes.
items.citation: Tural Mehtiyev, Biruk Tadesse, Lawrence Arkoh et al.. When Instruction Files Go Stale: Documentation Debt and Hidden Cost in Coding Agents. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Are These Programmers Ripe Enough to Eat? Evaluating How LLMs Handle Lexical Knowledge Conflicts in Translation
items.summary: This paper investigated how large language models handle conflicts between their internally learned lexical knowledge and external lexical information supplied in prompts during translation tasks. The researchers constructed a controlled Mandarin-to-English translation task in which familiar source words were deliberately assigned novel meanings, both within and across semantic categories, allowing them to isolate the effect of this conflict from other confounds. They systematically varied word frequency, sentence context, and prompt framing across nine models to assess how much models relied on the prompt-supplied contextual knowledge versus their prior knowledge. Models showed greater reliance on the supplied meanings for lower-frequency words and when sentence context supported those meanings, yet most models continued to favor the supplied meanings even when explicitly instructed to ignore them, with larger models within the same family tending to rely more on the provided information. Follow-up experiments revealed that modal weakening reduced reliance on supplied meanings, while the effects of repetition and reasoning varied depending on prompt layout and model, collectively underscoring the need for better methods to detect and manage lexical conflicts in model-based translation.
items.citation: Dongxu Wu, Sara Court, Micha Elsner. Are These Programmers Ripe Enough to Eat? Evaluating How LLMs Handle Lexical Knowledge Conflicts in Translation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.
items.summary: The paper studied the detection of *Schistosoma mansoni* infections in its intermediate snail hosts, aiming to improve on conventional parasitological methods that have limited sensitivity. The researchers developed a novel loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay targeting the mitochondrial NADH dehydrogenase subunit 1 gene of *S. mansoni*, optimized for a simple one-hour reaction, and evaluated its performance against microscopy, conventional PCR, and real-time PCR using both laboratory-infected snails and field-collected samples from two African countries. The assay achieved complete specificity and high sensitivity in laboratory settings, outperforming microscopy and performing comparably to real-time PCR, while in field surveys it detected a higher proportion of positive snails than conventional PCR and identified infections entirely missed by parasitological techniques. The authors conclude that this LAMP assay is a sensitive, specific, and field-applicable diagnostic tool suitable for routine surveillance and early warning of shifts in schistosomiasis transmission.
items.citation: Li HM, Qin ZQ, Lv S et al.. Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.. Tropical medicine and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: Point of Care Testing and Recombinase Polymerase Amplification.
items.citation: Weidmann M, El Wahed AA. Point of Care Testing and Recombinase Polymerase Amplification.. Journal of clinical laboratory analysis. 2026

items.title: CRISPR/Cas-Based Molecular Diagnostics for Intestinal Parasites: From Proof-of-Concept to Point-of-Care Testing.
items.summary: This review examined the application of CRISPR/Cas-based molecular diagnostic systems for detecting intestinal and foodborne parasitic infections, with a focus on pathogens including *Giardia duodenalis*, *Cryptosporidium parvum*, and several trematode species. The authors surveyed published assays that predominantly use Cas12a coupled with isothermal amplification methods, enabling rapid detection with fluorescence or lateral-flow readouts as an alternative to conventional microscopy and PCR-based approaches. The reviewed assays demonstrated high analytical sensitivity and specificity, with performance generally comparable to established molecular methods and characteristics suited to decentralized or point-of-care testing. However, the authors identified persistent limitations including dependence on nucleic acid extraction, small clinical validation cohorts, absence of standardized protocols, and false-negative results at low parasite burdens. They conclude that while CRISPR/Cas diagnostics are a promising next-generation platform for intestinal parasite detection, large-scale clinical validation and workflow optimization remain necessary before routine implementation in clinical or field settings.
items.citation: Alsaady IM. CRISPR/Cas-Based Molecular Diagnostics for Intestinal Parasites: From Proof-of-Concept to Point-of-Care Testing.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Smartphone-integrated RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a detection system with microneedle sampling for early point-of-care diagnosis of potato late blight
items.citation: Jinbiao Zhao, Hanbo Xu, Shifang Fei et al.. Smartphone-integrated RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a detection system with microneedle sampling for early point-of-care diagnosis of potato late blight. Biosensors and Bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness
items.summary: This review paper examines hantaviruses as emerging rodent-borne pathogens responsible for hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, synthesizing current knowledge across virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnostics, and public health preparedness. The authors identify environmental change, climate variability, urbanization, and land-use transformation as key drivers shaping rodent reservoir dynamics and increasing the risk of spillover to humans. Particular attention is given to surveillance and diagnostic gaps in tropical and Caribbean regions where hantavirus circulation is likely underrecognized. The review also discusses advances in molecular diagnostics, genomic surveillance, vaccine development, monoclonal antibody therapies, and climate-based early warning systems as tools to address these challenges. The authors argue that integrated One Health surveillance combining human, animal, and environmental monitoring, alongside strengthened laboratory capacity and regional collaboration, is essential for reducing the global burden of hantavirus disease and improving preparedness for future zoonotic threats.
items.citation: Maria E. Ramos‐Niño, Nicolette Chiem, Prakash V. A. K. Ramdass. Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Viral metagenomics of synanthropic urban bats: A surveillance strategy for uncovering potentially zoonotic viruses
items.summary: This study investigated the viral diversity harbored by urban bats in Brazil, using the country's existing rabies passive surveillance infrastructure as a foundation for broader pathogen detection. Researchers applied a selection algorithm to identify representative specimens from thousands of collected bats, then performed nanopore metagenomic sequencing on paired lung and intestinal tissue samples. The approach revealed a substantial diversity of viruses spanning multiple families of public health concern, including coronaviruses, arenaviruses, and paramyxoviruses, and critically identified a previously unknown filovirus in bats from the Americas. These results demonstrate that repurposing existing animal surveillance systems for metagenomic analysis can efficiently uncover undetected viral threats. The framework was further validated by multisectoral One Health experts as a scalable and cost-effective model suitable for national expansion and applicable to low- and middle-income countries.
items.citation: Juliana Amorim Conselheiro, Filipe Romero Rebello Moreira, Gisely Toledo Barone et al.. Viral metagenomics of synanthropic urban bats: A surveillance strategy for uncovering potentially zoonotic viruses. One Health. 2026

items.title: A Framework for Linking Pre- and Post-Common Envelope Binary Properties with Star Clusters: The First Demonstration with a Massive White Dwarf+M Dwarf Binary in Alessi 12
items.summary: This paper develops a framework for reconstructing the evolutionary histories of post-common envelope binary systems by exploiting membership in star clusters, where the cluster age provides an independent constraint on the white dwarf progenitor mass and rules out a merger origin for the white dwarf. The authors demonstrate this approach using a newly characterized white dwarf plus M-dwarf binary in the open cluster Alessi 12, carefully measuring the companion spectral type, the white dwarf mass, and confirming the orbital period through radial velocity monitoring. Combining the white dwarf mass, cooling age, and cluster age with stellar evolution models, they infer a massive progenitor star that entered a common envelope phase on the asymptotic giant branch. Common envelope evolution models in which convection sets the efficiency parameter reproduce the observed orbital separation under exactly two scenarios, corresponding to either a mid-asymptotic giant branch interaction with high efficiency or a late-asymptotic giant branch interaction with very low efficiency. The framework is broadly applicable to other post-common envelope binaries in clusters, offering empirical constraints on common envelope physics that cannot be obtained from field binaries alone.
items.citation: S. Grondin, M. R. Drout, Jason Nordhaus et al.. A Framework for Linking Pre- and Post-Common Envelope Binary Properties with Star Clusters: The First Demonstration with a Massive White Dwarf+M Dwarf Binary in Alessi 12. arXiv (Cornell University). 2026

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Foodborne Pathogen Detection from Sensing to Food Safety Systems: A Systematic Review
items.summary: This systematic review examined the application of artificial intelligence and machine learning to the detection of foodborne pathogens across a range of sensing technologies and food supply chain contexts. Following established guidelines, the authors searched major databases over more than a decade of literature, selecting studies that explicitly detected a pathogen using a described algorithm and reported quantitative validation metrics, ultimately synthesising a substantial corpus of research. They found that AI-assisted microscopy, spectroscopy, and biosensor platforms can achieve very high accuracy under controlled or internal validation conditions, with convolutional neural networks performing particularly well for bacterial identification and resistant strain detection. However, a critical finding was that model performance degrades substantially when evaluated on independent external datasets, exposing concerns about generalisation that are compounded by data heterogeneity, matrix interference, and inconsistent validation protocols. The authors conclude that AI serves best as a decision-support complement to existing food safety controls rather than a replacement, and that reliable translation into routine practice will require rigorous external validation, standardised benchmarks, and harmonised regulatory frameworks.
items.citation: Maria Schirone, Giovanni D’Ambrosio, Antonello Paparella. Artificial Intelligence in Foodborne Pathogen Detection from Sensing to Food Safety Systems: A Systematic Review. Foods. 2026

items.title: Bundibugyo Virus Disease: Diagnostics and Medical Countermeasures for a Neglected Ebolavirus
items.citation: Katharina Kopp. Bundibugyo Virus Disease: Diagnostics and Medical Countermeasures for a Neglected Ebolavirus. Viruses. 2026

items.title: Seeing What Matters: Benchmarking Task-Conditioned Actionable Spatial Belief for Manipulation
items.summary: This paper addresses a gap in how robotic spatial reasoning is evaluated, arguing that existing benchmarks assess general scene description rather than the task-specific visual evidence a robot actually needs to execute a manipulation command. The authors introduce a benchmark called Seeing What Matters, which pairs candidate camera views with manipulation commands across three simulated tabletop domains, measuring whether a view-selection policy acquires the observations necessary to make a command executable rather than simply characterizing the scene. The benchmark encompasses hundreds of frozen evaluation cases and expands to over a hundred thousand evaluation episodes under two protocols: closed-loop actionability and functional out-of-distribution generalization. A reference pipeline that maintains a spatial-functional belief state and ranks views by missing evidence achieves near-perfect success under both protocols, while ablating its functional or command-binding components collapses performance to near zero, and seven tested vision-language models reach only a fraction of that performance. The findings suggest that spatial belief for manipulation must be evaluated by whether it captures command-relevant evidence, not by scene-level completeness.
items.citation: Yina Jian, Mingkun Xu. Seeing What Matters: Benchmarking Task-Conditioned Actionable Spatial Belief for Manipulation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Time-gated optical-parametric-amplification and field-resolved detection of mid-infrared free-induction decay signals
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental challenge in infrared spectroscopy: the difficulty of resolving weak or broad vibrational modes that decay rapidly, limiting spectral resolution and dynamic range. The researchers developed a technique that uses synchronized time-gated optical parametric amplification of mid-infrared free-induction decay signals, implemented with a specific laser system and nonlinear crystal, to amplify molecular infrared signals while suppressing background noise. The approach achieved a substantial increase in electric field strength of the molecular signal, yielding dramatic improvements in dynamic range and signal-to-noise ratio compared to conventional detection. Using isopropyl alcohol as a test case, the method was shown to significantly extend the observable window of vibrational modes, enabling reconstruction of high-fidelity molecular fingerprints that reveal complex vibrational relaxation pathways and subtle structural dynamics previously buried in noise. The authors conclude that this technique opens a pathway toward new high-sensitivity and time-resolved studies of complex chemical structures.
items.citation: Sergio Revuelta, Gerard Faustino, Ka Fai Mak et al.. Time-gated optical-parametric-amplification and field-resolved detection of mid-infrared free-induction decay signals. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Scalable Unitary State-Encoding for Generic Large Data
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of efficiently encoding classical data into quantum states, which is a major obstacle for many quantum computing applications that would otherwise outperform classical methods. The authors introduce two complementary deterministic algorithms for simplifying fully controlled multiplexer circuits into one- and two-qubit gates: one that maps the elimination of redundant gate controls to a Boolean logic minimization problem, and another that uses a single ancilla qubit to decompose multi-controlled rotation gates via the Walsh-Hadamard spectrum of gate angles. These approaches support encoding of arbitrary complex data or queryable functions using tensor networks, enabling encoding beyond the limits of classical memory, without requiring amplitude amplification or mid-circuit measurements. Benchmarking across a broad range of function classes shows that hybridizing the two methods yields orders-of-magnitude reductions in circuit depth at equivalent fidelity compared to the default state-preparation method in the Qiskit package, with tunable trade-offs between depth and fidelity. Demonstration on real quantum hardware with square lattice connectivity confirmed excellent encoding fidelity even with minimal noise mitigation, suggesting the methods can enable practical quantum applications on current near-term devices that would otherwise be overwhelmed by noise before useful computation begins.
items.citation: Vittorio Pagni, Peter K. Schuhmacher, Michael Felderer et al.. Scalable Unitary State-Encoding for Generic Large Data. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Continuous wavelet-based feature extraction for laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy classification of human plasma samples
items.summary: This study investigated whether continuous wavelet transform-based feature extraction from laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy spectra could distinguish human plasma samples from individuals who tested positive or negative for SARS-CoV-2. Dried plasma droplets were analyzed using a nanosecond laser system, with multiple single-shot measurements averaged per specimen after outlier removal, and the extracted spectral peaks were fed into a support vector machine classifier. The wavelet-based pipeline identified emission lines associated with calcium, potassium, and nitrogen as discriminative features between the two groups. The leave-one-out cross-validation results indicated high accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, though the authors caution these estimates are provisional and require reconciliation at the specimen level. Independent validation and further assessment of variability arising from specimens, substrates, and acquisition conditions are noted as necessary steps before any diagnostic relevance can be established.
items.citation: Md Mahmudur Rahman, Atqiya Munawara Mahi, Nazim Ahmed Belabbaci et al.. Continuous wavelet-based feature extraction for laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy classification of human plasma samples. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Probing injection locking of an integrated nanolaser pair through RF beating
items.summary: This paper investigated optical injection locking of two photonic-crystal nanolasers integrated on a silicon waveguide and coupled to a shared master laser. Because fabrication-induced disorder caused the two nanolasers to emit at slightly different wavelengths, their individual locking ranges could be distinguished and mapped as a function of master laser detuning and power. The researchers identified a region where both nanolasers lock simultaneously to the master, and probed this collective state by modulating each nanolaser at a distinct radio frequency. A beat note at the difference frequency emerged exclusively within the overlap locking region, serving as a clear radio-frequency signature of simultaneous injection locking. The work establishes RF beating as a practical diagnostic tool for characterizing common-master injection locking in integrated nanolaser systems.
items.citation: Jan-Niklas Topf, Roberto Gajardo, Guillaume Huyet et al.. Probing injection locking of an integrated nanolaser pair through RF beating. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Local Correlations Determine the Dephasing Threshold of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ Topology
items.summary: This paper investigates how dephasing noise affects the topological properties of the Kane-Mele topological insulator, a canonical example of a system with a symmetry-protected topological invariant. The authors construct an auxiliary single-particle correlation Hamiltonian that reproduces the same single-particle correlations as the full dephased system and use the gap closing of this object to identify the phase boundary between topological and trivial phases, connecting it to the purity gap. By directly computing the topological invariant and examining two-terminal transport through the correlation Hamiltonian, they demonstrate quantized conductance in the topologically nontrivial regime, while carefully noting this does not imply physical conductance under dephasing. The key finding is that local correlations are sufficient to predict the survival of band topology, yielding a tractable local criterion for determining when single-particle topological structure persists under a given noise channel.
items.citation: Rishith Reddy, Ashutosh Dubey, Partha Sarathi et al.. Local Correlations Determine the Dephasing Threshold of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ Topology. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Molecular point-of-care: technological evolution, clinical applications, and future perspectives
items.citation: Zhang D, Cui X, Zhang R et al.. Molecular point-of-care: technological evolution, clinical applications, and future perspectives. Frontiers in bioengineering and biotechnology. 2026

items.title: From sepsis biomarker discovery to regulated in vitro diagnostics: evidence, certification status and implementation gaps
items.citation: Plata-Menchaca E, Hernández-Jiménez E. From sepsis biomarker discovery to regulated in vitro diagnostics: evidence, certification status and implementation gaps. Frontiers in medical technology. 2026

items.title: Circulating calprotectin and S100A8/A9-related biomarkers for diagnosis and prognostic stratification in adult acute infection and sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined whether circulating calprotectin and related S100A8/A9 biomarkers can reliably diagnose acute infection and sepsis or stratify prognosis in adult patients. The researchers searched multiple biomedical databases and trial registries, pooling diagnostic and prognostic accuracy data from over twenty independent cohorts using random-effects models alongside rigorous bias and evidence-certainty assessments. They found that these biomarkers demonstrated only moderate discriminative ability across diagnostic and prognostic outcomes, with pooled areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve in the low-to-mid range for both sepsis identification and mortality prediction. Threshold-based analyses revealed inconsistent sensitivity and specificity profiles depending on the clinical context, and paired comparisons with other biomarkers did not establish clear superiority for calprotectin. The authors conclude that while these markers may serve an adjunctive role in characterizing host immune response, the overall evidence certainty is very low and does not support their use as stand-alone diagnostic tools, universal decision thresholds, or replacements for established biomarkers and clinical evaluation.
items.venue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
items.citation: Liao YS, Deng YP, Song JL et al.. Circulating calprotectin and S100A8/A9-related biomarkers for diagnosis and prognostic stratification in adult acute infection and sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology. 2026

items.title: Procalcitonin-Guided Antimicrobial Therapy: Current Evidence for Clinical Decision-Making and Practical Limitations
items.citation: Alshammari S, Alrawaili B, Alshammari R et al.. Procalcitonin-Guided Antimicrobial Therapy: Current Evidence for Clinical Decision-Making and Practical Limitations. Cureus. 2026

items.title: Mechanism-informed diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy: a systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review investigated the diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy, a serious form of acute brain dysfunction occurring in sepsis patients. The researchers conducted a comprehensive search of multiple databases and applied Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis to compare and rank biomarkers spanning an immune activation–blood-brain barrier–glial–neuronal injury axis, using an advantage index derived from posterior distributions to establish comparative rankings. Blood-brain barrier and glial markers such as GFAP and S100β demonstrated more balanced diagnostic discrimination than classic neuronal injury markers, while upstream immune and alarmin candidates ranked highly in Bayesian comparisons, though many top-ranked biomarkers were supported by only single studies. The analysis revealed that diagnostic performance was substantially influenced by how sepsis-associated encephalopathy was defined and by the timing of biomarker sampling relative to anchor events, and few studies assessed whether biomarkers provided incremental value beyond established clinical predictors such as illness severity scores. The authors conclude that findings are hypothesis-generating rather than practice-changing, and call for prospective head-to-head validation using standardized phenotyping and anchor-based sampling protocols to determine whether mechanism-staged biomarker panels offer genuine incremental diagnostic utility.
items.citation: Zhang Q, Zhu R, Li Y et al.. Mechanism-informed diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy: a systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis.. Frontiers in molecular neuroscience. 2026

items.title: Dynamic Changes of Neutrophil Nuclear Membrane CD63 as a Potential Biomarker for Early Adjunctive Diagnosis and Prognostic Evaluation of Sepsis in Critically Ill Patients: A Prospective Cohort Study.
items.summary: This prospective cohort study investigated whether neutrophil nuclear membrane CD63 (nmCD63), a marker reflecting the early pathological process of targeted nuclear degranulation during neutrophil extracellular trap formation, could serve as a biomarker for sepsis diagnosis and prognosis in critically ill patients. The researchers developed a flow cytometry assay to quantify nmCD63 and validated it across two centers using a derivation cohort and an independent external validation cohort, applying established cutoffs and models without recalibration. nmCD63 levels rose progressively with disease severity and outperformed conventional inflammatory markers such as C-reactive protein and procalcitonin in distinguishing non-infectious systemic inflammation from infection. When combined with the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score, nmCD63 achieved strong discriminative performance for identifying sepsis in patients with confirmed infection. Dynamic changes in nmCD63 preceded shifts in all conventional biomarkers, and seven-day trajectories provided reliable prognostic stratification, suggesting nmCD63 has dual diagnostic and prognostic utility in sepsis management.
items.citation: Gao X, Zhang M, Li L et al.. Dynamic Changes of Neutrophil Nuclear Membrane CD63 as a Potential Biomarker for Early Adjunctive Diagnosis and Prognostic Evaluation of Sepsis in Critically Ill Patients: A Prospective Cohort Study.. MedComm. 2026

items.title: Procalcitonin and Presepsin in Gram-Negative Sepsis: Diagnostic, Prognostic, and Antimicrobial Stewardship Perspectives.
items.summary: This review examined the clinical utility of two biomarkers, procalcitonin and presepsin, in the context of Gram-negative sepsis, which poses particular challenges in intensive care settings due to multidrug-resistant pathogens and delays in pathogen identification. The authors assessed evidence regarding how these biomarkers can support early diagnosis, predict disease severity, monitor treatment response, and guide antimicrobial stewardship decisions. They found that procalcitonin is especially useful for distinguishing Gram-negative infections from Gram-positive or fungal causes, while presepsin offers rapid early identification and strong prognostic value even in culture-negative cases. Serial monitoring of both biomarkers together may help detect treatment failure and flag potential multidrug-resistant infections before conventional culture results are available, though confounding conditions such as renal failure, trauma, and sterile inflammation must be considered in interpretation. The review concludes that integrating these biomarkers with rapid molecular diagnostics could improve early treatment decisions, reduce unnecessary antibiotic use, and advance precision care for critically ill septic patients.
items.citation: Yadav BC, Patil HV, Patil SR. Procalcitonin and Presepsin in Gram-Negative Sepsis: Diagnostic, Prognostic, and Antimicrobial Stewardship Perspectives.. Cureus. 2026

items.title: Detection of Chagas disease from the ECG: the George B. Moody PhysioNet Challenge 2025
items.summary: The paper describes a machine learning competition aimed at detecting Chagas disease, a parasitic infection causing cardiomyopathy, using electrocardiogram data rather than serological testing. The George B. Moody PhysioNet Challenge 2025 tasked participating teams with developing algorithms to identify the patients most likely to have Chagas disease, framed as a triage problem reflecting real-world testing capacity constraints in Brazil. The challenge used a large collection of Brazilian ECG databases combining weakly labelled patient-report data with smaller strongly labelled serologically confirmed datasets, and evaluated performance using a metric capturing the true positive rate among the top five percent of patients ranked by algorithmic suspicion. An ensemble model combining the best individual submissions was also developed and demonstrated consistent performance across multiple held-out datasets. The challenge attracted substantial global participation and demonstrated that ECG-based screening can achieve clinically meaningful sensitivity for prioritising patients for Chagas disease testing and treatment.
items.citation: Matthew A. Reyna, Soheil Saghafi, Zuzana Koscova et al.. Detection of Chagas disease from the ECG: the George B. Moody PhysioNet Challenge 2025. Physiological Measurement. 2026

items.title: Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction (2026)
items.summary: This document presents the Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction, a consensus document developed jointly by major international cardiology and heart health organizations to update the clinical and pathophysiological framework for diagnosing and classifying myocardial infarction. The updated definition restructures the classification of myocardial infarction into three principal categories — primary myocardial infarction due to acute coronary pathology, secondary myocardial infarction arising from myocardial supply-demand imbalance, and procedure-related myocardial infarction as a complication of cardiac intervention or surgery — replacing the previous numerical type-based classification system to better reflect underlying pathophysiology and guide clinical evaluation. The document refines criteria for distinguishing acute from chronic myocardial injury based on the rise and fall pattern of cardiac troponin relative to the ninety-ninth percentile upper reference limit, and updates accelerated diagnostic pathways incorporating high-sensitivity troponin testing. Additional updates address diagnosis following sudden death, silent or unrecognized myocardial infarction, myocardial injury with non-obstructive coronary arteries, and special clinical situations including heart failure, chronic kidney disease, and cardio-oncology. The classification is also aligned with International Classification of Diseases coding and includes adapted diagnostic criteria for low-resource settings where biomarker testing and cardiac imaging may not be available.
authors: ESC/ACC/AHA/WHF Universal Definition Document Advisory Group
items.venue: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
items.citation: Nicholas L. Mills, Laura Kristin Newby, Sarah J. Zaman et al.. Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction (2026). Journal of the American College of Cardiology. 2026

items.title: Objective Bayes Factor Based Model Selection for Zero-Inflated Microbiome Count Data Under Jeffreys Prior
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of selecting appropriate statistical models for microbiome count data, which are characterized by excess zeros and overdispersion arising from the complex relationships between microbial communities and disease states, diet, genetics, and environmental factors. The authors developed a Bayes factor approach for model selection among four count data models — negative binomial, Poisson, zero-inflated negative binomial, and zero-inflated Poisson — using non-informative Jeffreys prior to maintain objectivity. Through both simulation studies and real data analysis, the proposed method was evaluated against traditional model selection criteria, specifically the Akaike information criterion and Vuong's test. The Bayes factor approach was found to outperform these traditional methods in both settings. The authors also released a dedicated R package to facilitate implementation of the proposed Bayesian model selection framework.
items.citation: Paramahansa Pramanik, Arnab K. Maity. Objective Bayes Factor Based Model Selection for Zero-Inflated Microbiome Count Data Under Jeffreys Prior. Statistics in Biopharmaceutical Research. 2026

items.title: Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis
items.summary: This review examines the relationship between gut microbial-derived metabolites and kidney disease, focusing on how disruptions in the gut microbiome contribute to renal injury and fibrosis. The authors synthesize current evidence showing that kidney injury creates a feedback loop involving intestinal barrier dysfunction, microbial dysbiosis, and altered metabolite production, characterized by reductions in beneficial short-chain fatty acids and excessive accumulation of uremic toxins. These metabolic shifts influence kidney pathology through multiple signaling pathways, with tryptophan metabolites identified as particularly central mediators of gut-kidney communication. The review covers the role of these metabolites across several conditions including acute kidney injury, chronic kidney disease, diabetic kidney disease, and immune-mediated nephropathies, elucidating the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms. The authors also survey therapeutic strategies targeting gut dysbiosis, including natural products, prebiotics, probiotics, and renal replacement therapy, with the aim of informing more precise treatment approaches for kidney disease.
items.citation: Wan-Ying Zhang, Yu-Lu Zhang, Qing-Qing Yu et al.. Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis. International Journal of Biological Sciences. 2026

items.title: Benchmarking AI Agents for Addressing Scientific Challenges Across Scales
items.summary: This paper addresses the gap between the growing use of AI agents in scientific contexts and the lack of rigorous, realistic benchmarks for evaluating their capabilities. The authors developed SciAgentArena, a benchmark comprising approximately two hundred tasks drawn from real-world scientific research scenarios spanning multiple domains, featuring stepwise verification and an interactive environment compatible with diverse AI agents. Evaluating current agents on this benchmark revealed that they perform reasonably well on structured data-analysis workflows with clear task definitions and evaluation criteria, but struggle considerably with open-ended research questions, generating novel insights, and sustaining self-directed exploration. The study also characterizes recurring failure modes and identifies specific areas where agent reliability, autonomy, and scientific reasoning need improvement. Overall, SciAgentArena is proposed as a practical framework for tracking progress in AI agents designed for science and for informing the development of more capable future systems.
items.citation: Tianyu Liu, A F Wang, Antonia Panescu et al.. Benchmarking AI Agents for Addressing Scientific Challenges Across Scales. arXiv (Cornell University). 2026

items.title: Stimuli-responsive nanocarriers for precision targeted and controlled antimicrobial drug delivery in drug-resistant infections
items.summary: This review examines stimuli-responsive nanocarriers as a strategy to overcome the limitations of conventional antibiotics, particularly their non-specific distribution and their role in accelerating antimicrobial resistance. The authors systematically analyze how nanocarriers engineered to respond to infection-specific microenvironmental cues — including acidic pH, elevated reactive oxygen species, pathogen-associated enzymatic activity, and hypoxia — enable spatiotemporally controlled drug release at infection sites while minimizing systemic exposure. The review details the mechanistic principles underlying pH-, enzyme-, redox-, and multi-stimuli-responsive systems, focusing on how trigger-induced physicochemical changes govern drug retention, activation, and penetration within drug-resistant infection niches. The authors further assess how these platforms address key resistance mechanisms such as biofilm tolerance, intracellular pathogen persistence, efflux pumps, and enzymatic antibiotic degradation, and critically compare their performance against passive nanocarriers and free antibiotics. The review concludes by identifying translational challenges — including microenvironmental heterogeneity, trigger variability, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory complexity — while arguing that stimuli-responsive nanocarriers represent a paradigm shift toward context-aware antimicrobial intervention capable of addressing drug-resistant infections beyond the pace of conventional antibiotic discovery.
items.citation: Li Dai, Xiaoyan Sun. Stimuli-responsive nanocarriers for precision targeted and controlled antimicrobial drug delivery in drug-resistant infections. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: SciCheck: A Framework for Verifying the Integrity of Deep Learning Training
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of verifying the integrity of deep learning training within scientific workflows, where non-determinism and flexible configurations make traditional recomputation-based checks infeasible. The authors developed SciCheck, a framework in which scientists commit training blueprints to a provenance ledger and verification proceeds through two complementary layers: a statistical judge that compares gradient statistics between a submitted run and an independent reference run, and a spot-check mechanism that re-executes randomly sampled training segments whose checkpoints are committed epoch by epoch. The framework was evaluated against attacks including gradient sign flipping, label poisoning, and fully fabricated runs across multiple neural network architectures spanning a range of parameter counts. SciCheck achieved high detection performance across all tested attack types while maintaining low false rejection rates for honest runs, with the spot-check layer contributing most of the detection accuracy and the statistical layer specifically catching sufficiently severe gradient manipulations. The authors also provide theoretical characterizations of each layer's detection guarantees and demonstrate that the approach is computationally practical, with verification costs roughly equivalent to one additional training run and efficient checkpoint storage requirements.
items.citation: Alexander Nguyen, Dylan Gresham, Gaby G. Dagher et al.. SciCheck: A Framework for Verifying the Integrity of Deep Learning Training. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Scenario Orchestration for Closed-loop Policy Evaluation of Autonomous Driving
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental challenge in autonomous driving evaluation: when a scripted test scenario encounters an ego vehicle whose behavior was not anticipated during scripting, the intended interaction may never actually occur, making the test uninformative. The authors propose a scenario orchestrator that continuously monitors the full traffic state during simulation and dynamically adapts non-ego actors through re-timing, re-routing, and role reassignment to reliably produce a desired interaction pattern. At each timestep, the system solves a constrained optimization problem that balances fidelity to the intended scenario against traffic feasibility and minimizing unnecessary interventions. A key conceptual contribution is separating whether a scenario was successfully realized from whether the ego policy succeeded or failed within that scenario, enabling cleaner attribution of test outcomes. Experiments in the CARLA simulator demonstrate that the orchestration approach produces the intended interactions more reliably than both scripted and learned actor baselines, particularly when initial conditions or ego behavior vary, supporting its use for controlled and reproducible policy evaluation.
items.citation: Frieda Rong, Zhaoyue Wang, Veer Kapadia et al.. Scenario Orchestration for Closed-loop Policy Evaluation of Autonomous Driving. arXiv. 2026

items.title: PhotoFinish: Portable Timerless Probing of Microarchitectural Latencies
items.summary: This paper investigates timerless methods for measuring microarchitectural latencies, motivated by the need to perform side-channel attacks even in environments where high-resolution timers are restricted. The researchers developed PhotoFinish, a portable primitive that races an operation under test against a reference operation in two parallel threads writing unique values to a shared memory location, converting latency differences directly into an observable architectural value without requiring any clock. PhotoFinish was evaluated across a broad range of processors spanning multiple instruction set architectures, demonstrating reliable cache state classification on widely varied microarchitectures. The technique was also shown to work when compiled to WebAssembly and run inside a browser, and was successfully applied to attacks including AES T-table and Evict+Reload, as well as to measuring TLB and execution-engine latencies and identifying last-level cache slice membership. The findings argue that restricting timers alone is insufficient as a defense, since shared-memory races provide a generic and precise means of observing fine-grained microarchitectural latency differences.
items.citation: Tristan Hornetz, Eduard Ebert, Lorenz Hetterich et al.. PhotoFinish: Portable Timerless Probing of Microarchitectural Latencies. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper investigates the reliability of majority-vote pseudo-labels used in test-time reinforcement learning, where pretrained language models are adapted to unlabeled target-domain data using self-generated supervision signals. The authors decompose the error of majority-vote supervision into two components: a population-majority bias that cannot be corrected without external labels, and a prompt-dependent finite-rollout variation that can be mitigated. To address the latter, they propose Prompt-Conditional Distributionally Robust DPO, a method that makes learning updates more conservative for prompts where sampled votes are unreliable, combined with a cache-based mechanism to reduce forgetting during online adaptation. Evaluated across a range of mathematical and knowledge-intensive reasoning benchmarks with multiple model backbones, their approach matches or outperforms the strongest existing test-time reinforcement learning baseline in the large majority of experimental settings.
items.citation: Haoyu Wang, Ru Wang, Yuanyuan Wang et al.. On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: An Empirical Study on Clustering-based Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm for Regression Test Case Selection
items.summary: The paper investigates quantum computing approaches to regression test case selection, a software engineering problem concerned with choosing which tests to re-run after code modifications without executing the full test suite. The authors extended and thoroughly evaluated their previously proposed clustering-based Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm approach, called QAOA-TCS, comparing it against both classical methods and other quantum approaches across single-objective and multi-objective problem formulations. The evaluation also assessed robustness to quantum noise, an important consideration given the limitations of current quantum hardware. Results indicate that QAOA-TCS outperforms state-of-the-art multi-objective approaches in most cases and maintains stable performance under high noise conditions, while quantum annealing-based selection proves most efficient for large multi-objective problems. The study concludes that QAOA-TCS offers the best trade-off between effectiveness and efficiency in single-objective settings when executed on realistic noisy simulators, though comparisons are complicated by differing computational environments across methods.
items.citation: Antonio Trovato, Martin Beseda, Dario Di Nucci. An Empirical Study on Clustering-based Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm for Regression Test Case Selection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Geometric Pairwise Classification of Affine Constraints over Ellipsoidal Regions
items.summary: This paper develops a deterministic geometric method for classifying affine (linear) constraints with respect to fixed ellipsoidal feasible regions, a problem motivated by chance-constrained optimization. The approach analytically categorizes each individual inequality as always violated, never violated, or cutting through the ellipsoid, and then extends to pairwise tests that determine whether two constraints can be simultaneously and strictly violated at a common point, producing a compatibility matrix. The underlying analysis relies on quadratic optimization and Karush–Kuhn–Tucker optimality conditions, with careful handling of edge cases such as tangencies, parallel constraint normals, and degenerate inequalities. The procedure is formulated for arbitrary finite-dimensional spaces and yields geometric information intended to support subsequent bounds on the probability of simultaneous constraint violations and the approximation of safe feasible regions.
items.citation: Igor M. L. Pataro, Martina Mammarella, Fabrizio Dabbene et al.. Geometric Pairwise Classification of Affine Constraints over Ellipsoidal Regions. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Off-panel resistance determinants in a high-resistance setting: comparative evaluation of syndromic multiplex PCR, metagenomic sequencing, and phenotypic AST in bloodstream infections.
items.summary: This study examined whether metagenomic next-generation sequencing could address the diagnostic gaps left by fixed-target syndromic multiplex PCR panels in bloodstream infections at a high antimicrobial resistance setting. Using a retrospective comparative design, the researchers evaluated direct-from-positive-blood-culture metagenomic sequencing alongside a commercial syndromic panel and routine microbiological methods across a substantial series of positive blood culture episodes. Metagenomic sequencing recovered a greater proportion of organisms identified by routine culture than the syndromic panel, and in cases where the panel failed to identify all organisms, metagenomic sequencing frequently restored complete coverage. For carbapenem resistance in particular, the syndromic panel produced false-susceptible results for certain non-fermenting gram-negative organisms, most notably *Acinetobacter baumannii*, where metagenomic sequencing detected off-panel resistance genes such as *bla*OXA-23 responsible for these errors. The authors conclude that targeted syndromic testing and metagenomic sequencing have complementary strengths, with metagenomic sequencing extending coverage of organisms and resistance mechanisms beyond predefined panel targets, though phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing remained necessary for definitive susceptibility determination because broader genomic detection did not reliably predict phenotypic resistance across all antimicrobial classes.
items.citation: Nitayanon P, Phoonthong S, Peizner MT et al.. Off-panel resistance determinants in a high-resistance setting: comparative evaluation of syndromic multiplex PCR, metagenomic sequencing, and phenotypic AST in bloodstream infections.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Rapid Diagnostics for Antimicrobial Resistance: From Bench to Bedside
items.citation: Mugisha N, Fawaz L, Noureddine R et al.. Artificial Intelligence in Rapid Diagnostics for Antimicrobial Resistance: From Bench to Bedside. Health science reports. 2026

items.title: Integrated evaluation of rapid diagnostic testing, genotypic-phenotypic resistance profiling, and AI-Assisted prediction models for antimicrobial stewardship and clinical outcomes in a resource-limited setting.
items.summary: This prospective observational study examined whether combining rapid diagnostic testing, molecular resistance gene profiling, and an artificial intelligence prediction model could improve antibiotic prescribing and patient outcomes compared to conventional susceptibility testing alone. The study enrolled adult patients with suspected bacterial infections at a hospital in Pakistan, measuring outcomes including time to effective therapy, antibiotic appropriateness, length of hospital stay, and mortality. Rapid diagnostics dramatically shortened the time to pathogen identification and to initiation of effective therapy compared with conventional testing, while appropriate antibiotic use increased substantially and broad-spectrum antibiotic use declined. The integrated approach was also associated with shorter hospital stays and lower mortality, and the AI model showed strong discriminatory performance for predicting antimicrobial resistance. The authors conclude that this combined diagnostic and predictive strategy represents a promising, scalable approach to combating antimicrobial resistance, particularly in resource-limited healthcare settings.
items.citation: Hammad M, Arif R, Fardoos S et al.. Integrated evaluation of rapid diagnostic testing, genotypic-phenotypic resistance profiling, and AI-Assisted prediction models for antimicrobial stewardship and clinical outcomes in a resource-limited setting.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Syndromic Testing in Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases: An Updated Review of Diagnostic Performance, Clinical and Healthcare Impact, and Emerging Developments.
items.summary: This review examines syndromic testing, an approach that uses nucleic acid amplification to simultaneously detect multiple pathogens and antimicrobial resistance determinants directly from clinical specimens, and how it has reshaped laboratory-based infectious disease diagnosis. The authors surveyed the current landscape of regulatory-cleared multiplex panels across seven major clinical syndromes, including respiratory, bloodstream, gastrointestinal, and central nervous system infections, among others, comparing their diagnostic performance and clinical applications against traditional culture-based workflows. Evidence reviewed indicates that syndromic panels reduce time to pathogen identification from days to hours, facilitating earlier targeted antimicrobial therapy, reduced unnecessary antimicrobial use, and, in certain populations such as those with bloodstream infections, potential mortality benefit. However, the review also highlights that rapid results do not automatically translate into improved clinical action or patient outcomes, underscoring the essential role of integrated diagnostic and antimicrobial stewardship programs. Ongoing challenges including evolving resistance epidemiology, geographically variable pathogen distributions, and questions around appropriate panel utilization are identified as key areas requiring continued attention.
items.citation: Wang G, Chen F. Syndromic Testing in Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases: An Updated Review of Diagnostic Performance, Clinical and Healthcare Impact, and Emerging Developments.. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances and Future Perspectives in the Detection of Carbapenem-Resistant <i>Acinetobacter Baumannii</i>.
items.summary: This review examines the detection landscape for carbapenem-resistant *Acinetobacter baumannii*, a pathogen classified by the World Health Organization as a critical priority due to its multidrug resistance, nosocomial transmissibility, and scarce treatment options. The authors surveyed a broad range of detection technologies, spanning conventional phenotypic and antimicrobial susceptibility testing, nucleic acid amplification methods, mass spectrometry, whole-genome and metagenomic sequencing, artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics, and biosensor or CRISPR-integrated platforms. They found that while culture-based susceptibility testing remains the reference standard, its lengthy turnaround limits early clinical decision-making, whereas molecular methods such as PCR, isothermal amplification, and advanced biosensor formats progressively reduce detection times and support point-of-care applications. Emerging genomic approaches enable comprehensive resistance profiling and outbreak surveillance, and AI tools show promise for resistance prediction, though challenges around multiplexing, standardization, cost, and clinical validation persist across newer platforms. The review concludes that the field is transitioning toward integrated, automated, and clinically adaptable diagnostic systems, requiring careful balance between analytical performance, speed, cost, and point-of-care suitability.
items.citation: Ye Q, Liu Y, Zhang K et al.. Recent Advances and Future Perspectives in the Detection of Carbapenem-Resistant <i>Acinetobacter Baumannii</i>.. Infection and drug resistance. 2026

items.title: AI-enhanced biosensing for antimicrobial resistance: translating rapid diagnostics to global surveillance.
items.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence can be integrated with biosensor technologies to improve the speed and accuracy of antimicrobial resistance detection and surveillance. The authors critically assess a range of platforms, including microfluidic and lab-on-chip devices, electrochemical and optical biosensors, and CRISPR-based systems, evaluating how AI contributes to signal processing, pattern recognition, and predictive interpretation of complex outputs.
