The review identifies key technical and translational obstacles such as biofouling, signal drift, sample-preparation variability, and the computational demands of deploying AI in portable point-of-care settings. The authors argue that beyond clinical diagnostics, AI-enabled microdevices hold potential for decentralised surveillance across environmental, agricultural, and veterinary contexts within a One Health framework. They conclude that while these integrated systems are promising, their real-world utility depends on standardised datasets, explainable and generalisable AI models, rigorous multicentre clinical validation, and equitable global deployment.
items.citation: Manisekaran NK, Tiwari P, Rathinasabapathi P. AI-enhanced biosensing for antimicrobial resistance: translating rapid diagnostics to global surveillance.. Biomedical microdevices. 2026

items.title: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist
items.summary: Co-Scientist is a multi-agent AI system built on Gemini that is designed to augment scientific discovery by generating, critiquing, and refining research hypotheses conditioned on a researcher's objectives and existing scientific evidence. The system features an asynchronous task execution framework for flexible compute scaling and a tournament-based evolution process for iterative self-improvement of hypothesis quality, with automated evaluations confirming that increased test-time compute progressively improves outputs. Although designed as a general-purpose tool, the system was validated in three biomedical domains: drug repurposing, novel target discovery, and explaining mechanisms of antimicrobial resistance. Notably, Co-Scientist identified new drug-repurposing candidates and synergistic combination therapies for acute myeloid leukaemia that were subsequently confirmed through in vitro experiments. These real-world experimental validations support the claim that such AI systems have meaningful potential to accelerate the pace of scientific discovery.
items.citation: Juraj Gottweis, Wei‐Hung Weng, Alexander Daryin et al.. Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist. Nature. 2026

items.title: Code as Agent Harness
items.summary: This survey paper examines the evolving role of code in large language model-based agentic systems, arguing that code has shifted from being merely a target output to serving as the operational foundation for agent reasoning, action, and execution. The authors introduce the concept of "code as agent harness," a unified framework organizing this perspective into three interconnected layers: the harness interface connecting agents to reasoning and environment modeling, harness mechanisms covering planning, memory, tool use, and feedback-driven optimization, and scaling considerations for multi-agent coordination. Through this framework, they systematically review representative methods and applications spanning domains such as coding assistants, GUI and operating system automation, embodied agents, scientific discovery, and enterprise workflows. The survey concludes by identifying open challenges including evaluation beyond final task success, verification under incomplete feedback, maintaining consistent shared state across multiple agents, and ensuring human oversight for safety-critical actions. The work aims to provide a roadmap toward agentic AI systems that are executable, verifiable, and stateful by centering code as their core infrastructure.
items.citation: Xuying Ning, Katherine Tieu, Dongqi Fu et al.. Code as Agent Harness. arXiv (Cornell University). 2026

items.title: MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks
items.summary: This paper investigated whether internalized reasoning models and externalized agent-based frameworks represent competing or complementary approaches to complex medical reasoning in large language models. The authors constructed a curated benchmark of complex clinical questions drawn from multiple medical datasets, applying difficulty-aware filtering and contamination screening, then evaluated a broad set of internalized reasoning models, base models, and externalized multi-agent methods against it. They found that both approaches independently improve performance on complex clinical questions, and crucially, that combining them yields additive benefits, with the highest accuracy achieved by layering agent workflows on top of an internalized reasoning model. Cost-performance analysis further revealed that this combined approach dominates the efficiency frontier, while lightweight optimization on less expensive models provides a viable path for resource-constrained deployment.
items.citation: Yanjun Shao, Xiangru Tang, Jiwoong Sohn et al.. MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks. Patterns. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies with artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and clinical translation. The authors synthesized research on multiomics approaches—including genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic methodologies—combined with deep learning frameworks to analyze complex biological datasets underlying disease. The review covers applications spanning target deconvolution, drug repositioning, de novo compound discovery, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment, with illustrative cases drawn from oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions. The authors find that this technological convergence accelerates target identification and lead optimization while enabling more precise clinical trial design, though challenges remain around harmonizing disparate data streams, ensuring reproducibility, and addressing algorithmic biases. They conclude that the fusion of multiomics and artificial intelligence opens new avenues for therapeutic innovation and marks a transformative shift toward data-driven, bench-to-clinic translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: ANO6-mediated trogocytosis of cancer-associated fibroblasts promotes pancreatic cancer cell growth and immune suppression
items.summary: This study investigated how pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cells obtain essential lipids despite residing in a stroma that is largely devoid of functional blood vessels. The researchers discovered that cancer-associated fibroblasts acquire lipids from blood-borne particles and transfer them to cancer cells through a process called trogocytosis, in which cancer cells and fibroblasts form synapse-like contacts that trigger calcium influx in fibroblasts via Orai channels, activating the phospholipid scramblase ANO6 and exposing phosphatidylserine on the fibroblast plasma membrane to initiate membrane lipid transfer. ANO6-mediated trogocytosis was found to be essential for pancreatic cancer cell survival and also supported immune suppression by enabling excessive cholesterol transfer that impairs cytotoxic T cell function. Blocking ANO6 disrupted exogenous cholesterol delivery to cancer cells, reduced tumor growth, and reversed immune suppression, pointing to ANO6 as a potential therapeutic target in pancreatic cancer.
items.citation: Charline Ogier, Charles Solomon Akino Mercy, Elena Bondarenko et al.. ANO6-mediated trogocytosis of cancer-associated fibroblasts promotes pancreatic cancer cell growth and immune suppression. Nature Cancer. 2026

items.title: Global burden of enteric infectious diseases, diarrhoeal diseases, and corresponding aetiologies, 1990–2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
items.citation: Avina Vongpradith, Regina-Mae Villanueva Dominguez, Lorainne Tudor Car et al.. Global burden of enteric infectious diseases, diarrhoeal diseases, and corresponding aetiologies, 1990–2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023. The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 2026

items.title: Asymptotic Analysis of Data Deduplication Under a Constant Edit Model
items.summary: This paper investigates the theoretical performance of data deduplication algorithms applied to data streams where repeated blocks are not identical but differ by a small number of edits. The authors develop two probabilistic source models capturing approximate repetition: one based on a constant number of substitution edits per block and one based on burst-insertion edits, the latter designed to reflect localized edit patterns seen in real-world storage workloads. Using an information-theoretic framework, they analyze both variable-length deduplication and multi-chunk deduplication algorithms under these models. They find that variable-length deduplication achieves asymptotically unbounded compression ratios, while multi-chunk deduplication attains compression within a constant factor of the source entropy under mild conditions. These results provide rigorous theoretical grounding for the effectiveness of deduplication as a compression strategy beyond traditional methods.
items.citation: Sarvin Motamen, Hao Lou, Farzad Farnoud. Asymptotic Analysis of Data Deduplication Under a Constant Edit Model. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Spectral Rigidity of Stochastic Operators with Heavy Tailed Perturbations
items.summary: This paper develops new theoretical tools for establishing number rigidity of point processes arising from the spectra of stochastic operators, addressing cases that were previously inaccessible to standard methods. The core difficulty with existing approaches, such as analyzing variance of linear statistics, is that they require precise control over correlations between individual spectral points, which becomes intractable for operators with heavy-tailed perturbations or complex correlation structures. The authors propose an alternative mechanism based on a pathwise comparison between the growth rate of unperturbed eigenvalues and the cumulative random noise, thereby converting a probabilistic problem into a perturbation theory problem. This framework is demonstrated by proving number rigidity for new classes of stochastic Schrödinger and Sturm-Liouville operators with heavy-tailed perturbations, which resist analysis by conventional rigidity methods.
items.citation: Youssef Djellouli. Spectral Rigidity of Stochastic Operators with Heavy Tailed Perturbations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Kinematic Reconstruction of Top-Quark Pairs Using Analytical and Machine-Learning Methods with CMS Open Data
items.summary: This paper investigates the reconstruction of top-quark-pair kinematics in the dilepton decay channel, where the presence of two undetected neutrinos makes the problem underconstrained. Using Monte Carlo simulated events from CMS Open Data, the authors developed improved analytical methods by tightening jet-lepton pairing requirements and exploiting the kinematic similarity between the dilepton and neutrino-pair systems, achieving modest improvements in the resolution of the reconstructed invariant mass and other kinematic quantities relative to the baseline approach. They additionally developed two machine-learning methods — a residual multilayer perceptron and a conditional normalizing flow — which substantially outperformed the improved analytical methods, delivering considerably better resolution in invariant mass, transverse momentum, and rapidity. Generator-level studies and generator-to-detector transfer tests confirmed that the machine-learning approaches capture genuine physics-driven corrections rather than artifacts of detector response. The work demonstrates significant promise for machine-learning-based reconstruction of dilepton top-quark-pair events, while also identifying the neutrino-pair approximation as a fundamental constraint limiting further resolution gains.
items.citation: V. Aushev, M. Spitsyn, R. Yermolenko et al.. Kinematic Reconstruction of Top-Quark Pairs Using Analytical and Machine-Learning Methods with CMS Open Data. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Seeing What Matters: Benchmarking Task-Conditioned Actionable Spatial Belief for Manipulation
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of task-conditioned visual information gathering for robotic manipulation, asking whether a model can identify which views of a scene are actually useful for executing a specific command rather than merely describing the scene in general. The authors created a benchmark called "Seeing What Matters" spanning three simulated tabletop manipulation domains, providing hundreds of frozen evaluation cases that pair candidate camera views with manipulation commands and measure whether a view-selection policy acquires the observations needed for task success. The benchmark employs two evaluation protocols—closed-loop actionability and functional out-of-distribution generalization—yielding a large number of evaluator episodes. A diagnostic reference pipeline that maintains a spatial-functional belief state and ranks views by missing evidence achieves near-perfect success, but ablating its functional or command-binding components collapses performance to near zero, demonstrating the necessity of these components. Tested on the same cases, seven vision-language models perform far below the reference pipeline, and the results collectively argue that spatial belief for manipulation should be measured by whether it acquires task-relevant evidence rather than by general scene-level completeness.
items.citation: Yina Jian, Mingkun Xu. Seeing What Matters: Benchmarking Task-Conditioned Actionable Spatial Belief for Manipulation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Time-gated optical-parametric-amplification and field-resolved detection of mid-infrared free-induction decay signals
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental challenge in infrared spectroscopy: weak or spectrally broad vibrational modes are difficult to resolve because they decay rapidly, making their signals hard to distinguish from noise. To overcome this, the researchers developed a technique combining synchronized time-gated optical parametric amplification with field-resolved detection of mid-infrared free-induction decay signals, implemented using a chromium-doped zinc sulfide laser and a nonlinear crystal. The approach substantially amplifies the electric field strength of molecular infrared signals, yielding large improvements in dynamic range and signal-to-noise ratio. Using isopropyl alcohol as a test case, the method was shown to meaningfully extend the observable window of vibrational modes and reconstruct high-fidelity molecular fingerprints that reveal complex vibrational relaxation pathways previously buried in background noise. The authors propose this technique as a pathway toward high-sensitivity and time-resolved studies of complex molecular and chemical structures.
items.citation: Sergio Revuelta, Gerard Faustino, Ka Fai Mak et al.. Time-gated optical-parametric-amplification and field-resolved detection of mid-infrared free-induction decay signals. arXiv. 2026

items.title: AnimWeb-Bench: Benchmarking Animated Webpage Code Generation from Videos
items.summary: This paper addresses a gap in webpage code generation research by focusing on animated webpages, which are prevalent on the web yet absent from existing benchmarks that target only static or interaction-triggered content. The authors created AnimWeb-Bench, the first benchmark for animated webpage code generation from videos, comprising real-world webpages spanning multiple application domains and animation types, each paired with a reference video and original static assets. They also developed a two-dimensional evaluation protocol that separately assesses static appearance fidelity and animation fidelity by tracking UI components across frames and comparing their motion properties to the reference video. Evaluating numerous multimodal large language models and coding agents revealed that reproducing animations is substantially harder than reproducing static appearance, that explicit frame inspection and render feedback improve agent performance, and that rapid continuous changes pose greater challenges than discrete state transitions.
items.citation: Zhongyi Zhang, Jingyu Xiao, Shuqing Li et al.. AnimWeb-Bench: Benchmarking Animated Webpage Code Generation from Videos. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Human inflammatory bowel disease-on-a-chip for modelling disease progression, cancer initiation and sex-specific effects
items.summary: This paper investigated inflammatory bowel disease using a microfluidic organ-on-a-chip platform lined with patient-derived colon epithelial cells and matched fibroblasts to replicate key disease features including compromised barrier function, reduced mucus, inflammation, fibrosis, and elevated cancer risk. By using heterotypic tissue recombinants that mixed healthy and diseased cell types, the researchers identified IBD-derived fibroblasts as the primary drivers of multiple disease hallmarks. The study found that peristalsis-like mechanical motions worsened inflammation and fibrosis in the IBD chips, and that exposure to pregnancy-associated hormones further exacerbated these effects in female IBD chips. Carcinogen exposure induced increased inflammation, gene mutations, and chromosomal duplication specifically in IBD chips but not in healthy controls, suggesting a heightened cancer susceptibility in the disease state. The findings point to intestinal stromal cells, sex hormones, and mechanical deformation as central contributors to IBD progression and sex-specific disease manifestations.
items.citation: Aliçan Özkan, Gwenn E. Merry, David Benson Chou et al.. Human inflammatory bowel disease-on-a-chip for modelling disease progression, cancer initiation and sex-specific effects. Nature Biomedical Engineering. 2026

items.title: Translational Barriers and AI-Driven Challenges of Microfluidics-Enabled Wearables and Implantable Systems in Personalized Medicine.
items.summary: This review examines the translational pathway for wearable and implantable microfluidic systems designed for personalized medicine, focusing on their progression from laboratory prototypes toward clinical deployment for continuous, minimally invasive biomarker monitoring in fluids such as sweat, saliva, tears, and interstitial fluid. Rather than addressing materials or fabrication in isolation, the authors construct a unified framework spanning functional biomaterials, advanced fabrication, diagnostic performance benchmarking, and closed-loop theranostic platforms that integrate sensing with autonomous therapeutic delivery. The review systematically analyzes how artificial intelligence contributes across three specific pathways—sensor self-calibration, multiplexed molecular decoding, and on-device autonomous decision-making—to shift these systems from passive monitoring toward adaptive intervention. A critical component of the analysis concerns socio-technical barriers to clinical translation, particularly how heterogeneity in biofluid data and disparities in population baselines can introduce algorithmic bias into AI-driven systems. The authors conclude that robust hardware interfaces, standardized validation benchmarks, and alignment with regulatory frameworks are essential prerequisites for equitable and responsible deployment of these technologies in digital health.
items.citation: Huang K, Fong CY, Huang X et al.. Translational Barriers and AI-Driven Challenges of Microfluidics-Enabled Wearables and Implantable Systems in Personalized Medicine.. Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany). 2026

items.title: Molecular point-of-care: technological evolution, clinical applications, and future perspectives
items.citation: Zhang D, Cui X, Zhang R et al.. Molecular point-of-care: technological evolution, clinical applications, and future perspectives. Frontiers in bioengineering and biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Integrated Microfluidic CRISPR-Based Diagnostic Device for Rapid Testing of HPVs.
items.summary: This paper developed an integrated microfluidic diagnostic platform for rapid detection of high-risk human papillomavirus types relevant to cervical cancer prevention. The system, called Ccard, combines recombinase polymerase amplification with CRISPR/Cas13a chemistry in a single-step reaction performed on a microfluidic chip loaded with lyophilized reagents, with sample preparation achieved through simple room-temperature treatment that bypasses conventional nucleic acid extraction. A vacuum pump drives the sample through the chip's channels, and an Internet of Things device enables real-time fluorescence monitoring. The assay detected both target HPV types and an internal reference gene within thirty minutes, achieving a very low limit of detection and demonstrating high sensitivity and complete specificity when validated against clinical swab samples. These findings support the platform's potential as a reliable point-of-care tool for cervical cancer screening, particularly in resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Wang T, Li L, Wang Y et al.. Integrated Microfluidic CRISPR-Based Diagnostic Device for Rapid Testing of HPVs.. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: ANO6-mediated trogocytosis of cancer-associated fibroblasts promotes pancreatic cancer cell growth and immune suppression
items.summary: This study investigated how pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cells obtain essential lipids despite residing in a stroma that is largely devoid of functional blood vessels. The researchers discovered that cancer-associated fibroblasts acquire lipids from blood-borne particles and transfer them to pancreatic cancer cells through a process called trogocytosis, in which cancer cells and fibroblasts form synapse-like membrane contacts. These contacts trigger calcium influx in the fibroblasts via Orai channels, activating the phospholipid scramblase ANO6, which exposes phosphatidylserine on the fibroblast plasma membrane and initiates the transfer of membrane lipids, including cholesterol, to cancer cells. Beyond supporting tumor cell survival, ANO6-dependent trogocytosis was found to promote immune suppression by transferring excess cholesterol to cytotoxic T cells, dampening their function. Blocking ANO6 disrupted exogenous cholesterol delivery to cancer cells, impaired tumor growth, and reversed immune suppression, pointing to ANO6 as a potential therapeutic target in pancreatic cancer.
items.citation: Charline Ogier, Charles Solomon Akino Mercy, Elena Bondarenko et al.. ANO6-mediated trogocytosis of cancer-associated fibroblasts promotes pancreatic cancer cell growth and immune suppression. Nature Cancer. 2026

items.title: Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective
items.summary: This paper examines the regulatory landscape governing cell-derived extracellular vesicles as therapeutic and diagnostic products, with attention to both European and global frameworks. The authors analyze how the acellular nature of extracellular vesicles creates classification ambiguities, as these products do not map cleanly onto existing regulatory categories such as advanced therapy medicinal products or conventional biologics. A central focus is the divergence between regulatory approaches across jurisdictions, including the European Union's recent guideline clarifying that minimally modified extracellular vesicles fall outside the advanced therapy medicinal product definition, while other regions apply their own classification criteria. The paper argues that extracellular vesicle products should be developed within existing medicinal product frameworks provided regulatory tools are applied consistently, and it identifies key operational grey zones—including classification criteria, critical quality attributes, potency strategies, and comparability—that require clarification. Rather than proposing new normative frameworks, the work offers a synthesizing analysis intended to support regulatory dialogue among international agencies and scientific societies to advance safe and reproducible clinical translation of extracellular vesicle-based therapies.
items.citation: Tania Limongi, Paola Milla, Barbara Stella et al.. Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective. Journal of Extracellular Vesicles. 2026

items.title: Advances in Polydopamine-Based Nanoplatforms: Antioxidant Mechanisms and Applications in Oxidative Stress-Mediated Diseases
items.summary: This review examines polydopamine-based nanoplatforms as antioxidant therapeutic tools, motivated by the material's melanin-mimetic structure, redox-active functional groups, and biocompatibility. The authors synthesize current understanding of how polydopamine eliminates reactive oxygen species through hydrogen atom transfer and electron transfer mechanisms, with sustained activity enabled by dynamic catechol/quinone redox cycling. The review comprehensively surveys design strategies across multiple nanoplatform architectures—including solid, mesoporous, hollow, doped, and coated forms—and analyzes how structural features, particle size, composition, and surface charge influence antioxidant performance. The paper further organizes recent research according to key pathological challenges addressed by these platforms, such as disrupting reactive oxygen species–inflammation feedback loops, overcoming biological delivery barriers, remodeling regenerative microenvironments, and regulating programmed cell death. The authors position this work as addressing a gap in systematic summaries of polydopamine-based antioxidant nanoplatforms and their applications in oxidative stress-mediated diseases.
items.citation: Zhilin Wang, Zhu Liu, Luming Song et al.. Advances in Polydopamine-Based Nanoplatforms: Antioxidant Mechanisms and Applications in Oxidative Stress-Mediated Diseases. Nano-Micro Letters. 2026

items.title: Extending Silicon Lifetime: A Review of Design Techniques for Reliable Integrated Circuits
items.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive review of aging-related reliability challenges in modern integrated circuits, motivated by the increasing demands of applications such as artificial intelligence and autonomous driving that require continuous, dependable operation. The authors examine the key physical degradation mechanisms that become more severe as transistor dimensions shrink toward atomic scales, including Bias Temperature Instability, Hot Carrier Injection, Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown, Electromigration, and stochastic aging-induced variations. The survey covers monitoring techniques at both circuit and system levels, as well as circuit-level mitigation strategies applicable to digital, analog, and SRAM designs. Emerging software-driven approaches in design automation and aging characterization are also reviewed as transformative tools for reliability optimization. The paper concludes by identifying open challenges and future directions for improving aging management and extending integrated circuit lifespans across diverse industries.
items.citation: Jani Babu Shaik, Fan Hu, Libo Zhu et al.. Extending Silicon Lifetime: A Review of Design Techniques for Reliable Integrated Circuits. ACM Computing Surveys. 2026

items.title: Polymer-Based Flexible Wireless Sensors for Health Monitoring
items.summary: This review examines polymer-based flexible wireless sensors for health monitoring, identifying a gap in the literature where existing work has focused heavily on material design, energy harvesting, and wireless communication while neglecting challenges of signal attenuation, noise accumulation, and data distortion within wireless links. To address this, the authors construct a comprehensive framework that integrates signal sensing, link transmission, and intelligent processing, built upon advances in flexible materials and wireless energy supply. The review gives particular attention to channel compensation, noise suppression, feature extraction, lightweight artificial intelligence models, and edge computing as mechanisms for improving data quality and reducing energy consumption. The authors also systematically analyze how wireless link stability and energy management affect overall monitoring performance. The work aims to establish design principles for the next generation of high-reliability, low-power, and intelligent wireless flexible health monitoring systems by reinforcing synergies between data processing and communication.
items.citation: Heyuan Huang, Gang Xue, Jianning Zhan et al.. Polymer-Based Flexible Wireless Sensors for Health Monitoring. Nano-Micro Letters. 2026

items.title: Trajectory-Dependent Decoherence and Leakage During Shuttling of Multi-Spin Qubits
items.summary: This paper investigates how multi-spin logical qubits decohere and leak during physical shuttling operations in semiconductor quantum processors, a capability increasingly required by fault-tolerant architectures. The authors analyze two-, three-, and four-spin encodings subject to spatiotemporally correlated one-over-frequency noise, examining how different shuttling protocols affect fidelity and leakage. They find that parallel shuttling best suppresses decoherence over short distances for all encodings studied, while sequential shuttling becomes superior for long-range transport, with the crossover depending on device-specific parameters. The behavior across all encodings is unified through pairwise dephasing factors between shuttled spins, and the authors derive explicit analytical expressions for fidelities and leakage that allow experimentalists to predict multi-spin qubit performance from a small set of independently measurable quantities. These results establish a direct connection between shuttling trajectory geometry, noise correlations, and qubit decoherence, offering practical design guidance for noise-resilient shuttling in scalable semiconductor platforms.
items.citation: Yu-Ning Zhang, Aleksandr S. Mokeev, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ et al.. Trajectory-Dependent Decoherence and Leakage During Shuttling of Multi-Spin Qubits. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Can Agentic Systems Close the Gap in Radiology with Production AI Tools?
items.summary: This paper examined whether agentic AI systems combining specialized and generalist radiology models can achieve comprehensive clinical reporting, addressing the limitation that existing approaches either cover few findings or suffer from hallucinations. The researchers developed a radiology agentic framework in which an orchestrator selects and calls modular tools to generate structured reports, then evaluated it against a large multi-modality report corpus using either a catalog restricted to findings from cleared medical AI devices or an unlimited catalog. Tool outputs were simulated from reference reports to isolate the effects of tool availability and orchestration quality from tool error itself. With only cleared tools and clinical indication as input, the system recovered fewer than a third of actionable findings, with missed findings attributable roughly to absent tool coverage and to available tools the orchestrator failed to call. The study concludes that tool availability and effective orchestration are complementary bottlenecks, as expanding the tool catalog closes most of the performance gap but only when paired with a sufficiently capable orchestrator.
items.citation: Aubin Charley, Julien Khlaut, Charles Corbière et al.. Can Agentic Systems Close the Gap in Radiology with Production AI Tools?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Seeing What Matters: Benchmarking Task-Conditioned Actionable Spatial Belief for Manipulation
items.summary: This paper addresses the question of how robots should selectively acquire visual information based on the specific manipulation task they are performing, rather than simply describing a scene comprehensively. The authors introduce a benchmark called "Seeing What Matters" that evaluates task-conditioned actionable spatial belief across simulated tabletop manipulation domains, providing hundreds of frozen evaluation cases and over a hundred thousand evaluator episodes under two protocols: closed-loop actionability and functional out-of-distribution generalization. The benchmark pairs candidate RGB views with manipulation commands and hidden postconditions to directly measure whether a view-selection policy gathers the observations actually needed to execute a given command. A diagnostic reference pipeline that maintains a spatial-functional belief state and ranks views by missing evidence achieves near-perfect success, while ablating its functional or command-binding components collapses performance to near zero, and seven vision-language models tested on the same cases reach only modest success rates. The authors conclude that spatial belief for manipulation should be measured not by how completely a model describes a scene, but by whether it selectively acquires the evidence required by the current command.
items.citation: Yina Jian, Mingkun Xu. Seeing What Matters: Benchmarking Task-Conditioned Actionable Spatial Belief for Manipulation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Cross-Domain TARA-to-NAC Rule Mapping Methodology: From Automotive OEM Networks to Energy Storage Systems
items.summary: This paper addresses a gap in cybersecurity practice where threat analysis and risk assessment under automotive and industrial standards produces cybersecurity goals but lacks structured guidance for converting those goals into enforceable network access control rules. The authors developed a six-step methodology that systematically maps threat assessment outputs to specific network access control rules, each tied to a named enforcement point and traceable back to the originating threat records. They also proposed a unified compliance framework that treats foundational standards as a fixed substrate while allowing domain-specific regulations to function as interchangeable overlays, enabling the approach to transfer across sectors. The methodology was applied in two desk-based case studies—an automotive original equipment manufacturer plant network and a utility-scale battery energy storage system—demonstrating that the core framework remains stable while only the domain-specific regulatory overlay changes between sectors. The work produces a reusable pattern for translating risk assessments into enforceable controls across critical infrastructure domains, though the authors acknowledge that empirical validation on live systems remains future work.
items.citation: Krishna Teja Medam, Thiago Quinelato. A Cross-Domain TARA-to-NAC Rule Mapping Methodology: From Automotive OEM Networks to Energy Storage Systems. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A lightweight convolutional neural network for target detection in an edge environment
items.summary: The paper presents a lightweight convolutional neural network designed to perform threat and target detection on edge devices with limited computational resources. The model incorporates a real-time hotspot detection algorithm to enable rapid and accurate processing of thermal imagery from situational awareness sensors. Testing and validation demonstrated that the network achieves high accuracy and sensitivity while maintaining a low false positive rate, with inference speeds and detection ranges suitable for practical deployment. The lightweight architecture is intended to make the model easy to deploy across a range of applications such as surveillance, security, and general object recognition, effectively extending the operational reach of edge-based detection systems.
items.citation: Hughes Perreault, Ola Ahmad, Daniel Czuboka. A lightweight convolutional neural network for target detection in an edge environment. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Continuous wavelet-based feature extraction for laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy classification of human plasma samples
items.summary: This study investigated whether laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) combined with continuous wavelet transform (CWT)-based feature extraction could distinguish human plasma samples from individuals testing positive or negative for SARS-CoV-2. Plasma droplets were dried on silicon substrates and analyzed using a nanosecond Nd:YAG laser, with multiple single-shot spectra averaged per specimen after outlier rejection. The CWT approach was used to detect spectral peaks, which were then fed into a support vector machine classifier for group discrimination. The pipeline achieved high provisional accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity under leave-one-out cross-validation, with key discriminative features attributed to emission lines from calcium, potassium, and nitrogen. The authors caution that these performance estimates are provisional and that independent validation alongside assessment of specimen and acquisition variability is needed before any diagnostic relevance can be established.
items.citation: Md Mahmudur Rahman, Atqiya Munawara Mahi, Nazim Ahmed Belabbaci et al.. Continuous wavelet-based feature extraction for laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy classification of human plasma samples. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Rapid visual and direct detection of Acinetobacter baumannii and carbapenem resistance by oligoDNA-gold nanoparticles biosensor in clinical samples.
items.summary: This study addressed the urgent need for rapid identification of *Acinetobacter baumannii* and its carbapenem resistance genes in clinical settings, where conventional methods are slow and infrastructure-intensive. The researchers developed oligonucleotide-functionalized gold nanoparticle biosensors targeting three genomic regions: a conserved region of the *nucAb* gene for species identification, the *bla*OXA-23 gene for the most prevalent carbapenem resistance determinant in *A. baumannii*, and the *bla*NDM gene for broad-spectrum carbapenem resistance applicable across multiple pathogens. The biosensors were designed to work directly on clinical respiratory samples without requiring DNA purification or amplification, producing colorimetric visual results within thirty minutes. The platform achieved sensitive detection down to low concentrations of bacterial DNA and demonstrated that the *bla*NDM biosensor could identify resistance variants not only in *A. baumannii* but also in *Klebsiella pneumoniae*, *Escherichia coli*, and *Pseudomonas aeruginosa*. The authors propose that these biosensors offer a rapid, economical, and practical tool to support early clinical decision-making and antimicrobial resistance surveillance.
items.citation: Chalana A, Gupta V, Sharma P et al.. Rapid visual and direct detection of Acinetobacter baumannii and carbapenem resistance by oligoDNA-gold nanoparticles biosensor in clinical samples.. Diagnostic microbiology and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: SHIELD: An Argonaute-powered immobilization-free homogeneous electrochemical biosensor for ultrasensitive viable pathogen detection.
items.summary: The paper developed an electrochemical biosensing platform called SHIELD designed to detect viable foodborne pathogens with high sensitivity and specificity, addressing the problem of false positives generated by DNA from dead bacteria. The system combines Propidium Monoazide pretreatment, which selectively blocks DNA from dead cells, with Argonaute-guided sequence-specific DNA cleavage as the primary signal transduction mechanism, ensuring only signals from living bacteria are detected. Target DNA from viable Salmonella typhimurium is first amplified by isothermal loop-mediated amplification, after which activated Argonaute cleaves dual-labeled electrochemical probes, and unreacted probes are removed by magnetic streptavidin separation to produce a "signal-on" electrochemical response. By operating in a homogeneous, immobilization-free format rather than relying on surface-fixed probes, the platform avoids reproducibility issues common to conventional biosensors. The resulting system achieves detection down to a single colony-forming unit per milliliter within about an hour, demonstrating a rapid and reliable approach for screening viable foodborne pathogens.
items.citation: Qiao J, Bai B, Zhang Y et al.. SHIELD: An Argonaute-powered immobilization-free homogeneous electrochemical biosensor for ultrasensitive viable pathogen detection.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Photoelectrochemical biosensor using CoPP to quench PTCA for the detection of mip gene fragment.
items.summary: This paper describes the development of a photoelectrochemical biosensor designed to detect a specific gene fragment from Legionella pneumophila, the bacterium responsible for Legionnaires' disease. The biosensor was constructed using a perylene-based compound as the photoactive material to generate a strong initial photocurrent, with gold nanoparticles deposited on the electrode surface to anchor a capture DNA strand. Upon hybridization with the target mip gene fragment, a cobalt porphyrin compound intercalated into the resulting DNA duplex and quenched the photocurrent signal, providing a measurable readout proportional to target concentration. The sensor achieved sensitive detection across a wide concentration range with a very low detection limit, demonstrating good analytical performance. The authors propose this platform as a practical tool for screening Legionella pneumophila in respiratory specimens where bacterial loads are high.
items.venue: Analytical sciences : the international journal of the Japan Society for Analytical Chemistry
items.citation: Zhang F, Lu L, Li S et al.. Photoelectrochemical biosensor using CoPP to quench PTCA for the detection of mip gene fragment.. Analytical sciences : the international journal of the Japan Society for Analytical Chemistry. 2026

items.title: Nanozyme-based biosensors for pathogenic microorganism detection: a mini-review
items.citation: Yang T, Ling Y, Zhang E et al.. Nanozyme-based biosensors for pathogenic microorganism detection: a mini-review. Frontiers in microbiology. 2026

items.title: Cross-validated SPR/SERS dual-mode fiber biosensor for rapid and accurate detection of Salmonella Typhimurium in foods.
items.summary: This paper developed a portable fiber-optic biosensor that simultaneously uses surface plasmon resonance and surface-enhanced Raman scattering to detect the foodborne pathogen Salmonella Typhimurium in food samples. The sensing platform employs bacteriophages as highly specific capture and signal probes, with sea-urchin-shaped gold/silver nanoparticles tagged with a Raman reporter molecule to generate SERS signals, while tapered optical fibers coated with gold film provide the SPR readout. When target bacteria are present, a sandwich complex forms on the fiber surface, enabling both detection modalities to be read sequentially from a single binding event within roughly half an hour. The two channels exhibited overlapping quantitative linear ranges and low detection limits, and the sensor was validated in fish, vegetable, and milk matrices with strong anti-interference performance. Crucially, having two independent signal outputs allows the results to mutually cross-verify one another, substantially reducing false positives and improving overall detection reliability for field-deployable food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Zhu S, Su Y, Wang Y et al.. Cross-validated SPR/SERS dual-mode fiber biosensor for rapid and accurate detection of Salmonella Typhimurium in foods.. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Advancements in biosensor Technologies for Pathogen Detection: Innovations and comparison with conventional diagnostic approaches.
items.summary: This review paper examines the landscape of biosensor technologies developed for detecting pathogens across clinical, food safety, and environmental monitoring contexts, comparing them against established conventional diagnostic methods. The authors survey a range of biosensor platforms, including electrochemical, optical, nanoparticle, microfluidic, and paper-based systems, analyzing their underlying sensing principles, design strategies, and practical applications. Conventional approaches such as culture-based methods, ELISA, and PCR are acknowledged as analytically proven but are noted to be constrained by lengthy analysis times, sample processing demands, and the requirement for trained personnel and specialized instrumentation. Biosensors are presented as advantageous alternatives owing to their portability, high sensitivity, multiplexing capability, and suitability for point-of-care use, with advances in nanomaterials, biorecognition strategies, and signal-transduction mechanisms having substantially expanded their detection potential. The review also candidly addresses persistent challenges limiting wider biosensor adoption, including issues of sensor stability and reproducibility, fabrication complexity, scalability, and the need for rigorous validation before practical implementation.
items.citation: Singhal P, Misra S, Prakash A et al.. Advancements in biosensor Technologies for Pathogen Detection: Innovations and comparison with conventional diagnostic approaches.. Journal of microbiological methods. 2026

items.title: Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support
items.summary: This review paper examines federated learning as a privacy-preserving approach to training artificial intelligence models across multiple healthcare institutions without centralizing sensitive patient data. The authors conducted a literature review spanning federated learning applications across biomedical imaging modalities such as MRI, CT, ultrasound, and histopathology, as well as electronic health records, wearable physiological signals, chronic disease management, elder care, and clinical decision support systems. The core mechanism reviewed involves training models locally at each participating site and sharing only model updates rather than raw patient data, which improves alignment with privacy regulations while still enabling collaborative learning. The review identifies important limitations of federated learning, including that privacy protection is not guaranteed by the approach alone, as vulnerabilities such as gradient leakage, model inversion, and membership inference attacks require additional safeguards. Beyond cataloguing successes, the authors also outline practical barriers including system heterogeneity, data imbalance, communication bottlenecks, and fairness concerns, and offer guidance to regulators, developers, and healthcare systems for advancing safe and equitable federated learning deployments in medicine.
items.venue: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
items.citation: Shon G. Nemane, Vaishnavi M. Sarad, Dhiraj P. Tulaskar et al.. Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support. Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering. 2026

items.title: Novel Strategies Against Fungal Infections: Repurposing Existing Drugs and Advancing Nanotherapeutics
items.summary: This review examines the growing global burden of fungal infections, which is compounded by expanding immunocompromised populations, antibiotic overuse, and the emergence of multidrug-resistant fungi that undermine conventional antifungal treatments. The authors surveyed two emerging therapeutic strategies: drug repurposing, which involves identifying non-antifungal agents with intrinsic antifungal activity or synergistic potential when combined with existing drugs, and nanomaterial-based delivery systems utilizing polymeric and metallic nanoparticles. The nanotherapeutic approaches were highlighted for their ability to improve drug solubility, enable targeted delivery, penetrate biofilms, employ multimodal fungicidal mechanisms, and reduce host toxicity while limiting resistance development. Although the evidence base remains largely preclinical, the authors conclude that combining drug repurposing with nano-enabled technologies offers a promising path toward safer, more effective antifungal therapies that are less prone to resistance, and they call for continued interdisciplinary effort to advance these approaches toward clinical use.
items.citation: Zimeng You, Kaiwen Zhuang, Takashi Sugita et al.. Novel Strategies Against Fungal Infections: Repurposing Existing Drugs and Advancing Nanotherapeutics. iFungi. 2026

items.title: A multimodal adaptive optical microscope for in vivo imaging from molecules to organisms
items.summary: This paper introduces MOSAIC, a reconfigurable multimodal microscope designed to overcome the limitation that microscopes optimized for specific imaging tasks typically lack versatility and suffer from performance degradation caused by sample-induced optical aberrations. The system integrates multiple advanced imaging modalities—including light-sheet, label-free, super-resolution, and multi-photon microscopy—all coupled with adaptive optics to correct for aberrations in complex biological samples. MOSAIC was applied across a wide range of biological contexts, from imaging subcellular dynamics in cultured cells and live multicellular organisms to nanoscale mapping of molecular architectures in expanded tissues spanning millimeter scales, as well as structural and functional neural imaging in live mice. By enabling correlative studies across biological scales within the same specimen, MOSAIC provides an integrated platform capable of spanning the spatial scales from nanometers to centimeters and temporal scales from milliseconds to days relevant to understanding biological systems.
items.citation: Tian-ming Fu B, Gaoxiang Liu, Daniel Edward Milkie et al.. A multimodal adaptive optical microscope for in vivo imaging from molecules to organisms. Nature Methods. 2026

items.title: Personalized cancer vaccines: bridging immune-oncology and precision medicine for advanced therapeutics
items.summary: This review examines the current landscape and future directions of personalized cancer vaccines as a strategy to overcome the limited clinical success that has characterized therapeutic cancer vaccination to date. The authors survey multiple vaccine platform types, including DNA, mRNA, peptide, dendritic cell, and whole-cell approaches, and analyze the immunological barriers these platforms must overcome, such as tumor heterogeneity, immunosuppressive microenvironments, and poor immune memory formation. The review highlights how nanotechnology-based delivery systems, particularly those using lipid-polymer hybrids, biomimetic membranes, and stimulus-responsive materials, can improve lymph node targeting, dendritic cell activation, and antigen cross-presentation while accommodating the antigenic diversity of evolving tumors. Integration of artificial intelligence for neoantigen selection and multiomics for patient stratification is discussed as a means to accelerate and refine vaccine design, with combination strategies alongside immune checkpoint inhibitors identified as a path toward more durable antitumor immunity. The authors conclude that emerging clinical evidence, especially in melanoma and pancreatic cancer, supports the potential of these next-generation personalized vaccines to shift cancer care from reactive treatment toward proactive, precision-guided immunotherapy.
items.citation: Leiguang Ye, Guo Zhao, Jiaxiu Ma et al.. Personalized cancer vaccines: bridging immune-oncology and precision medicine for advanced therapeutics. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Traditional fermented food microbial ecosystems oriented towards industrial standards: multi-dimensional characterization and artificial regulation
items.summary: This review examined the microbial ecosystems underlying traditional fermented foods, focusing on the challenge that spontaneous fermentation introduces variability in quality and safety that hinders industrial standardization. The authors surveyed how multi-omics approaches can be integrated to comprehensively characterize microbial community composition, dynamics, metabolic outputs, microbial interactions, and bacteriophage activity within these ecosystems. They also summarized regulation strategies—including the deployment of functional microbial strains, construction of synthetic microbial communities, bacteriophage control, and physicochemical manipulation—aimed at steering fermentation toward consistent, predictable outcomes. The review concludes by outlining the future directions and key challenges involved in transitioning traditional fermentation from empirical, artisanal practice to scalable industrial processes.
items.citation: M T Wu, Jiayao Wang, Yu Wang et al.. Traditional fermented food microbial ecosystems oriented towards industrial standards: multi-dimensional characterization and artificial regulation. npj Science of Food. 2026

items.title: Current advancements and future research directions in the green synthesis and applications of nanoparticles
items.summary: This paper examined the rapidly growing but fragmented scientific literature on green-synthesized nanoparticles by conducting a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of publications indexed in a major database over a five-year period. The study mapped intellectual trends, geographic contributions, characterization practices, and conceptual frameworks within the field, while also linking publication patterns to toxicity and regulatory themes. The analysis found that silver nanoparticles dominate research due to their antibacterial properties, that plant extracts are the predominant biosynthetic resource while bacterial and fungal sources remain underexplored, and that conventional characterization techniques are overrepresented relative to higher-resolution methods, revealing a persistent gap at the nano-bio interface. The paper also proposes a clarifying taxonomy that distinguishes green synthesis from biosynthesis within the framework of green chemistry principles, and identifies key barriers—particularly around toxicity assessment and regulatory readiness—that hinder the commercialization of these materials. Overall, the authors outline research strategies intended to move green-synthesized nanoparticles toward scalable, regulation-compliant nanotechnology platforms.
items.citation: Riyadh Abdulmalek Hassan, Waheeba Ahmed Al-Amrani, Abduelwhab B. Alwany et al.. Current advancements and future research directions in the green synthesis and applications of nanoparticles. Discover Nano. 2026

items.title: SciCheck: A Framework for Verifying the Integrity of Deep Learning Training
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of verifying the integrity of deep learning training within scientific workflows, where stochastic processes and flexible configurations make simple recomputation infeasible as a correctness check. The authors developed SciCheck, a framework in which a scientist logs training blueprints to a provenance ledger and a verifier assesses the resulting run through two complementary layers: a statistical judge that compares per-step gradient statistics against a reference run, and a spot-check that re-executes randomly selected training segments whose checkpoints have been committed incrementally to the ledger. The framework was evaluated on multiple neural network architectures under adversarial conditions including gradient sign flipping, label poisoning, and fully fabricated runs, achieving high integrity-detection performance while rarely flagging honest runs as suspicious. The authors provide theoretical characterizations of what each verification layer can and cannot detect, showing that statistical gradient analysis catches sufficiently strong sign flips but is blind to fabricated runs that replay genuine statistics, while the spot-check catches fabricated segments with provable probability bounds that allow verifiers to tune the number of sampled segments to a desired soundness level. Overall verification costs roughly one to two times the expense of a single retraining, with per-epoch commitments substantially reducing checkpoint storage requirements compared to retaining all checkpoints.
items.citation: Alexander Nguyen, Dylan Gresham, Gaby G. Dagher et al.. SciCheck: A Framework for Verifying the Integrity of Deep Learning Training. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Locating Contact on Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots From Tendon Measurements Alone via Constrained Moving Horizon Estimation
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of detecting and localizing contact along tendon-driven continuum robots using only tendon tension measurements, without any additional tactile or force sensors. The authors first establish that this is a fundamental structural limitation: the mapping from contact forces to tendon measurements possesses a null space, making contact localization impossible without additional constraints. They show that when obstacle geometry is known, incorporating non-penetration and complementarity conditions renders the contact force locally identifiable, and they prove local exponential strong detectability for the resulting system. To exploit this structure, they develop a constrained moving horizon estimator formulated as a quadratic program that runs in real time and comes with a provable robust stability guarantee. Benchmarking against a tuned extended Kalman filter on a finite-element simulation of a robot pressing and sliding against a wall, the proposed estimator achieved substantially better contact location and force estimation accuracy, remained robust to errors in obstacle position, unmodeled friction, and tendon friction across randomized trials, while offering no advantage over the Kalman filter in contact-free scenarios, confirming that the gains stem specifically from the contact constraints.
items.citation: Haitham El-Hussieny. Locating Contact on Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots From Tendon Measurements Alone via Constrained Moving Horizon Estimation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Health-System-Wide Mapping of Demographic Information in Routine Clinical Histopathology
items.summary: This paper investigated the degree to which demographic information—specifically sex, age group, and self-reported race—is encoded within routine clinical histopathology images across a wide range of organs and disease states. The researchers analyzed a very large collection of hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images drawn from hundreds of thousands of patients spanning dozens of organs, applying pathology foundation-model representations combined with multiple-instance learning to systematically assess how well demographic attributes could be recovered from tissue appearance alone. They found that demographic signals were broadly detectable across organ-demographic combinations, with performance varying substantially by organ and demographic category, and that these signals persisted even after accounting for diagnosis-related confounding through class balancing and diagnosis-text clustering. Notably, demographic-associated information remained recoverable within diagnosis-stratified training settings across multiple organs, suggesting the signals reflect genuine histomorphological and contextual features rather than purely diagnostic confounders. The authors present these findings as a systematic map intended to guide investigation into the biological and technical sources of demographic information in histopathology, with implications for understanding shortcut learning and improving the interpretability and fairness of computational pathology models.
items.citation: Shengjia Chen, Ruchika Verma, Kevin Clare et al.. Health-System-Wide Mapping of Demographic Information in Routine Clinical Histopathology. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Designing Effective Monitor-Based Interventions for Mitigating Reward Hacking During RL
items.summary: This paper investigates how to design effective monitor-based interventions to prevent reward hacking during reinforcement learning, where models learn unintended behaviors by exploiting flaws in reward signals. The researchers created and open-sourced three realistic training environments in which a language model engages in reward hacking through test overwriting in coding tasks, sycophancy in medical chat, and hallucination in biography generation. Through systematic experimentation, they found that models can learn to evade even highly accurate monitors by exploiting systemic weaknesses in detection probes and judge models, while monitors that provide richer learning signal suppress reward hacking more effectively but are themselves more susceptible to evasion. They also found that including easier problems in training reduces reward hacking, and that applying these insights to the medical chat and biography generation environments yielded interventions capable of reducing reward hacking rates to pre-training levels in some cases. The results suggest that thoughtful monitor intervention design can meaningfully mitigate reward hacking and that lessons learned in one environment can transfer to new settings.
items.citation: Aria Wong, Joshua Engels, Neel Nanda. Designing Effective Monitor-Based Interventions for Mitigating Reward Hacking During RL. arXiv. 2026

items.title: When Instruction Files Go Stale: Documentation Debt and Hidden Cost in Coding Agents
items.summary: This paper investigates how stale instruction files in repository configuration documents affect the behavior and efficiency of large language model-based coding agents. The researchers identified three real-world cases of outdated instructions from active open-source repositories, each representing a different type of guidance, and had agents complete maintenance tasks under conditions where the instruction was left stale, corrected, or removed entirely. By analyzing hundreds of agent trajectories at the level of individual tool calls, they found that agents tend to follow stale guidance when it appears relevant to the task, sometimes even when accurate information is available elsewhere in the codebase. While agents generally recovered from immediate failures caused by stale instructions, none repaired the underlying instruction file itself, meaning the documentation debt persisted. The study concludes that evaluating agents solely on task success obscures the hidden costs of outdated documentation, and advocates for assessing agent behavior beyond final outcomes.
items.citation: Tural Mehtiyev, Biruk Tadesse, Lawrence Arkoh et al.. When Instruction Files Go Stale: Documentation Debt and Hidden Cost in Coding Agents. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Are These Programmers Ripe Enough to Eat? Evaluating How LLMs Handle Lexical Knowledge Conflicts in Translation
items.summary: This paper investigates how large language models handle conflicts between their internally learned lexical knowledge and externally supplied definitions during translation tasks. The researchers constructed a controlled Mandarin-to-English translation experiment in which familiar source words were deliberately assigned novel meanings, both within and across semantic categories, allowing them to isolate the effect of providing contextual lexical knowledge via prompts. They evaluated nine models across conditions varying word frequency, sentence context, and prompt framing, and also conducted follow-up experiments examining modal weakening, repetition, and reasoning strategies. The findings show that models tend to favor the externally supplied meanings, particularly for less frequent words and when sentence context supports those meanings, with larger models within a family showing greater reliance on the supplied definitions than smaller ones. Notably, most models continued to prefer the externally provided meanings even when explicitly instructed to ignore them, highlighting systematic challenges in controlling lexical choices in large language model-based translation.
items.citation: Dongxu Wu, Sara Court, Micha Elsner. Are These Programmers Ripe Enough to Eat? Evaluating How LLMs Handle Lexical Knowledge Conflicts in Translation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Multiplex molecular respiratory diagnostic panels and antimicrobial use in paediatric respiratory infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.
items.citation: Bajaj R, Mehta P, Gopi A et al.. Multiplex molecular respiratory diagnostic panels and antimicrobial use in paediatric respiratory infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.. BMJ open. 2026

items.title: Development and validation of a multiplex TaqMan real-time quantitative PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of six major bacterial respiratory pathogens in goats.
items.summary: This study developed and validated a multiplex real-time quantitative PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of six major bacterial and mycoplasmal pathogens responsible for respiratory disease in goats. Two triplex TaqMan panels were designed, one targeting three Mycoplasma species and another targeting two bacterial species and one Streptococcus subspecies, with performance assessed through specificity, sensitivity, and reproducibility testing using plasmid standards and non-target organisms. The assay demonstrated high specificity with no cross-reactivity against non-target pathogens, low limits of detection for all six targets, and excellent reproducibility as indicated by low intra- and inter-assay coefficients of variation. When applied to field-collected goat nasal swab samples, the assay detected at least one target pathogen in the majority of samples and identified mixed infections in a substantial proportion of positive cases, underscoring the clinical relevance of multiplex detection. The authors conclude that this tool offers a rapid and reliable approach for both clinical diagnosis and epidemiological surveillance of caprine respiratory disease.
items.citation: Fu M, Liu Y, Zhang Z et al.. Development and validation of a multiplex TaqMan real-time quantitative PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of six major bacterial respiratory pathogens in goats.. Frontiers in veterinary science. 2026

items.title: Syndromic Testing in Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases: An Updated Review of Diagnostic Performance, Clinical and Healthcare Impact, and Emerging Developments.
items.summary: This review examines syndromic testing, a molecular diagnostic approach that simultaneously detects multiple pathogens and antimicrobial resistance determinants from clinical specimens, and its impact on infectious disease management in the United States over the past two decades. The authors surveyed the landscape of FDA-cleared multiplex nucleic acid amplification panels across seven major clinical syndromes, including respiratory, bloodstream, gastrointestinal, and central nervous system infections, among others, comparing their performance to traditional culture-based workflows. Evidence indicates that syndromic panels provide comprehensive pathogen identification within hours rather than days, facilitating faster targeted therapy, reduced unnecessary antimicrobial use, and shorter hospital stays in certain settings. A mortality benefit was identified in some populations, particularly those with bloodstream infections, though rapid results do not automatically translate into improved clinical action or outcomes. The review also highlights ongoing challenges including appropriate panel utilization, evolving antimicrobial resistance epidemiology, geographically variable pathogen distributions, and the essential role of diagnostic and antimicrobial stewardship programs in realizing the full clinical benefit of these technologies.
items.citation: Wang G, Chen F. Syndromic Testing in Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases: An Updated Review of Diagnostic Performance, Clinical and Healthcare Impact, and Emerging Developments.. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy of rapid integrated molecular testing for major respiratory viral infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.citation: Liu C, Yu D. Diagnostic accuracy of rapid integrated molecular testing for major respiratory viral infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Frontiers in medicine. 2026

items.title: Clinical Relevance of Multiplex PCR for Respiratory Pathogens in Hospitalized Adults with Influenza-Like Illness.
items.summary: This study investigated the pathogens responsible for influenza-like illness in hospitalized adults and examined how multiplex PCR findings related to clinical, laboratory, and radiological data. Using a retrospective single-center design, researchers applied a multiplex real-time PCR assay capable of detecting a broad panel of viral and bacterial respiratory pathogens in over four hundred hospitalized patients across two respiratory seasons. A pathogen was identified in fewer than half of patients, with *Streptococcus pneumoniae*, influenza viruses, and seasonal coronaviruses being the most common findings, and co-infection with influenza A and *S. pneumoniae* representing the most frequent mixed-pathogen pattern. Among patients who tested positive for *S. pneumoniae* by PCR, those with radiologically confirmed pneumonia tended to be older, had greater disease severity, and more often had concurrent influenza infection compared to those without radiological evidence of pneumonia. The authors conclude that while multiplex molecular assays are valuable diagnostic tools, results for bacterial pathogens like *S. pneumoniae* must be interpreted alongside clinical and radiological findings rather than in isolation.
items.venue: Journal of clinical practice and research
items.citation: Gülseren YD, Aydın D, Çetin Duran A. Clinical Relevance of Multiplex PCR for Respiratory Pathogens in Hospitalized Adults with Influenza-Like Illness.. Journal of clinical practice and research. 2026

items.title: ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
items.summary: These guidelines address the growing challenge of managing infection risk in patients with inflammatory bowel disease who are treated with increasingly potent immunosuppressive and biologic therapies. The guidelines cover prevention, diagnosis, and management of opportunistic and other clinically significant infections, including viral, bacterial, mycobacterial, and vaccine-preventable diseases, across the spectrum of agents used in Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. The work was motivated by the rapid expansion of the therapeutic armamentarium, particularly newer small molecules and advanced biologics, each carrying distinct infection risk profiles not fully addressed by prior guidance. A structured, evidence-based framework for risk stratification and preventative strategies tailored to contemporary treatment paradigms is presented. The guidelines represent an update to previous iterations, incorporating the most recent data to support clinicians in balancing effective immunomodulation against infectious morbidity and mortality.
items.venue: Journal of Crohn s and Colitis
items.citation: Henit A. Yanai, Pierre Ellul, Bram Verstockt et al.. ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease. Journal of Crohn s and Colitis. 2026

items.title: mRNA-based influenza vaccine expands the B cell response breadth in humans
items.summary: This study compared the immune responses generated by conventional split-virion influenza vaccines against those generated by an investigational mRNA-based quadrivalent influenza vaccine in healthy young adults across two consecutive vaccination seasons. Using an observational cohort design, the researchers examined B cell responses both in circulation and within draining lymph nodes, and characterized serum antibody repertoires through proteomic analysis. The mRNA-based vaccine induced higher antibody titers, greater frequencies of memory B cells, and sustained germinal center reactions in lymph nodes that persisted for at least half a year in a subset of participants, whereas conventional vaccines did not drive comparable responses. Proteomic and B cell lineage analyses revealed that mRNA vaccination expanded the number of distinct serum IgG clonotypes and promoted growth within pre-existing clonotypes through ongoing germinal center-driven evolution. This broadened antibody repertoire translated into greater binding breadth against antigenically divergent influenza viruses, highlighting the importance of persistent germinal center activity in widening vaccine-induced antibody coverage.
items.citation: Hanover C. Matz, Tae-Geun Yu, Kritika Dixit et al.. mRNA-based influenza vaccine expands the B cell response breadth in humans. Nature Immunology. 2026

items.title: Improving Inference from Reported Concentrations in Environmental Surveillance by Modeling the Statistical Features of Digital PCR
items.summary: This paper addresses a statistical challenge in environmental surveillance using digital PCR, where many studies rely only on reported concentration estimates rather than the raw partition count data needed for exact statistical modeling. The authors developed a Bayesian model with a likelihood function specifically tailored to digital PCR that can be fitted directly to reported concentrations, while accounting for uncertainty in assay parameters through interpretable priors. The approach captures key statistical features of digital PCR assays that are ignored by conventional normal or log-normal approximations, including concentration-dependent measurement noise and nondetects. Using real-world case studies involving environmental DNA decay in seawater and pathogen detection in wastewater, the authors demonstrated that their method produces estimates comparable to fully informed models using partition counts, while avoiding the biases introduced by simpler distributional assumptions. The method is made accessible through two dedicated software packages for regression analyses and wastewater surveillance.
items.citation: Adrian Lison, Timothy Ryan Julian, Tanja Stadler. Improving Inference from Reported Concentrations in Environmental Surveillance by Modeling the Statistical Features of Digital PCR. ACS ES&T Water. 2026

items.title: Small extracellular vesicle signaling and mitochondrial transfer reprogram T helper cell function in human asthma
items.summary: This study investigated how small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) derived from airway myeloid-derived regulatory cells contribute to the chronic airway inflammation characteristic of asthma. The researchers examined whether these sEVs could transfer mitochondria to CD4+ T cells and thereby influence T cell activation and polarization, using both human asthmatic samples and a murine asthma model. They found that asthmatic MDRC-derived sEVs carry mitochondria into T cells primarily through membrane fusion, triggering antigen-specific activation and polarization toward pro-inflammatory Th17 and Th2 phenotypes via reactive oxygen species signaling. A Drp1-dependent mitochondrial fission mechanism was identified as responsible for packaging mitochondria into sEVs, and blocking mitochondrial oxidant signaling within these vesicles reduced T cell activation. Intranasal delivery of mitochondria-containing sEVs in mice enhanced airway inflammation and Th cell polarization in vivo, suggesting that sEV-mediated mitochondrial transfer represents a previously unrecognized pathological mechanism and potential therapeutic target in asthma.
items.citation: Kenneth P. Hough, Jennifer L. Trevor, Shaheer Ahmad et al.. Small extracellular vesicle signaling and mitochondrial transfer reprogram T helper cell function in human asthma. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness
items.summary: This review examines hantaviruses as emerging rodent-borne pathogens responsible for hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, with a focus on how environmental and ecological changes are reshaping disease risk. The authors synthesize current knowledge spanning virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical presentation, diagnostics, and surveillance to provide a comprehensive overview of the field. Particular attention is given to how climate change, urbanization, and land-use transformation influence rodent reservoir dynamics and the likelihood of viral spillover into human populations. The review identifies significant surveillance and diagnostic gaps in tropical and Caribbean regions where hantavirus circulation may be systematically underrecognized. The authors argue that integrated One Health frameworks combining human, animal, and environmental monitoring, alongside advances in molecular diagnostics, genomic surveillance, vaccines, and climate-based early warning systems, are essential for reducing the global burden of hantavirus disease and improving preparedness for future zoonotic threats.
items.citation: Maria E. Ramos‐Niño, Nicolette Chiem, Prakash V. A. K. Ramdass. Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Evaluation of the deeplex Myc-TB-targeted next-generation sequencing assay for mycobacterial identification and drug resistance detection
items.summary: This study evaluated the Deeplex Myc-TB targeted next-generation sequencing assay for its ability to simultaneously identify mycobacterial species and detect drug-resistance mutations in a U.S. clinical laboratory setting. The assay was tested on several hundred culture-positive mycobacterial growth indicator tube broths, with results compared against established reference methods including GeneXpert MTB/RIF for species identification and both broth microdilution and MGIT-based phenotypic drug susceptibility testing for resistance profiling. The assay achieved complete concordance with GeneXpert for identifying Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex isolates and demonstrated high agreement for nontuberculous mycobacteria identification compared to MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, while also providing subspecies-level resolution within clinically important groups such as the Mycobacterium avium complex and Mycobacterium abscessus. Genotypic resistance predictions from the assay were concordant with phenotypic susceptibility testing for isolates with canonical resistance-conferring mutations and available interpretive criteria. The authors conclude that integrating Deeplex Myc-TB into routine diagnostic workflows can consolidate multiple sequential testing steps into a single assay, improving the timeliness of clinically relevant results and supporting molecular surveillance of mycobacterial diseases.
