items.citation: Kin Israel Notarte, Kristine Allen, Derek T. Armstrong et al.. Evaluation of the deeplex Myc-TB-targeted next-generation sequencing assay for mycobacterial identification and drug resistance detection. Journal of Clinical Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Scalable Unitary State-Encoding for Generic Large Data
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently encoding classical data into quantum states, which represents a major practical bottleneck for quantum computing applications. The authors introduce deterministic, scalable amplitude-encoding algorithms that use tensor networks to handle data beyond classical memory limits, requiring no amplitude amplification or mid-circuit measurements. Their two complementary approaches simplify fully controlled multiplexer circuits into one- and two-qubit gates: one maps redundant gate control elimination to a Boolean logic minimization problem, while the other uses a single ancilla qubit and the Walsh-Hadamard spectrum to decompose multi-controlled rotation gates. Benchmarking across diverse function classes shows that hybridizing these methods yields orders-of-magnitude reductions in circuit depth at equivalent state fidelity compared to the default state-preparation method in Qiskit. Experimental validation on quantum hardware with square lattice connectivity confirmed high encoding fidelity even with minimal noise mitigation, extending the practical reach of near-term quantum devices to applications that would otherwise be overwhelmed by noise before useful computation begins.
items.citation: Vittorio Pagni, Peter K. Schuhmacher, Michael Felderer et al.. Scalable Unitary State-Encoding for Generic Large Data. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Universal photonic synthetic temporal-mode converter for heterogeneous quantum interconnects
items.summary: This paper proposes a synthetic temporal-mode converter designed to interface heterogeneous quantum systems that emit single photons with incompatible temporal waveforms. The device uses programmable couplers and optical delays to coherently mix time bins across multiple stages, concentrating photon amplitudes spread across many time bins into a single output bin. Simulations demonstrate mode overlaps exceeding a threshold of near-perfect indistinguishability for both exponential and Gaussian input waveforms. Compared to conventional temporal gating, the approach achieves dramatically higher photon-pair coincidence rates, with gains of tens-of-fold depending on the number of time bins and the degree to which time-multiplexing capacity is exploited. The authors argue that this architecture offers a practical route to universal temporal-mode conversion in quantum networks connecting disparate quantum hardware.
items.citation: Joohyung Song, James I. Kwon, Edo Waks et al.. Universal photonic synthetic temporal-mode converter for heterogeneous quantum interconnects. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Payload-Blind Bistatic Delay-Doppler Sensing with Phase-Injected Chirps in CE-OFDM
items.summary: This paper addresses bistatic radar sensing using Constant-Envelope OFDM (CE-OFDM) signals, which pose a challenge because their Hermitian-symmetric structure makes conventional sensing pilot approaches either costly or disruptive to the constant-envelope property. The authors propose injecting a known chirp sequence, specifically a Zadoff-Chu sequence, into the CE-OFDM phase domain, which causes the ensemble mean of the transmitted signal to act as an implicit superimposed pilot that a receive-only node can exploit for delay-Doppler sensing without requiring dedicated sensing frames or a pilot power split. A Doppler-aligned receiver coherently integrates this implicit reference across frames while payload-induced interference averages down, and closed-form expressions are derived to characterize the payload-induced noise floor, detection probability, and tolerance to direct-path interference. The proposed approach is shown to substantially outperform phase-domain injected training frame averaging, which suffers a large detection loss in the simulated target scenario, and the method achieves performance close to a payload-aware matched filter with only a small detection gap. Crucially, it matches the detection performance of a dedicated-pilot benchmark at equivalent reference energy while eliminating the substantial frame overhead that benchmark requires.
items.citation: Gustavo P. Gonçalves, Henrique L. Senger, Bruno S. Chang et al.. Payload-Blind Bistatic Delay-Doppler Sensing with Phase-Injected Chirps in CE-OFDM. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Multi-Mode Pinching-Antenna-Based OFDM Systems: A Robust Design Perspective
items.summary: This paper proposes a robust transmission framework for a multi-mode pinching-antenna system combined with orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing, addressing the practical challenges of imperfect channel state information and antenna positioning errors simultaneously. The authors first develop a physical model grounded in coupled-mode equations that captures frequency-dependent guided-mode propagation and coupling between guided modes and pinching antennas across the OFDM band. Using this model, they formulate a worst-case sum-rate maximization problem that jointly optimizes the baseband beamformer and pinching-antenna positions subject to quality-of-service and power constraints, then solve the resulting non-convex problem through an alternating optimization algorithm combining trust-region subproblems, scenario construction, weighted minimum mean-square error updates, and successive convex approximation. The proposed approach efficiently exploits Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions for both subproblems. Numerical results demonstrate that the robust design consistently outperforms non-robust and conventional robust benchmarks in worst-case sum rate and quality-of-service satisfaction, and more reliably meets user requirements than methods that account for only one type of error.
items.citation: Hao Liang, Xidong Mu, Mingzhe Chen et al.. Multi-Mode Pinching-Antenna-Based OFDM Systems: A Robust Design Perspective. arXiv. 2026

items.title: COMBIO: Automated Discovery of a Compact Composite Biomarker from Routine Laboratory Panels
items.summary: COMBIO is an automated pipeline designed to distill complex machine-learning models trained on routine laboratory data into simple, interpretable closed-form biomarkers. The system constructs composite biomarkers as products of laboratory measurements raised to small integer powers, using Shapley additive explanation values to identify candidate measurements and guide the sign of each exponent, followed by exhaustive search to select the best formula. The pipeline was evaluated across six clinical prediction tasks spanning population health surveys, liver disease classification, and intensive care outcomes including in-hospital mortality and sepsis identification, with external validation performed for the hospital-based tasks. COMBIO's predictive performance closely matched that of logistic regression using the same candidate laboratory measurements, differing by no more than a small margin in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve across all test sets. The authors emphasize that the multiplicative representation offers compactness and interpretability rather than improved accuracy, and that local validation and recalibration are necessary before any clinical deployment.
items.citation: Tomer D. Meirman, Lior S. Rokach, Bracha Shapira et al.. COMBIO: Automated Discovery of a Compact Composite Biomarker from Routine Laboratory Panels. arXiv. 2026

items.title: AlienBench: A Benchmark of Structural Novelty in Language Model Outputs
items.summary: This paper investigates whether large language models can produce structurally novel creative outputs, specifically by adapting the structured imagination task from cognitive psychology, in which participants invent creatures from another planet and their departures from Earth-typical biological features serve as a measure of creativity. The researchers created AlienBench, a benchmark in which language models generate alien creature descriptions under multiple prompt conditions, and a panel of automated judges extracts and scores ten biological features per description based on how much each departs from familiar Earth-animal defaults. Ten language models ranging from frontier proprietary systems to open-weight models were evaluated, each producing a large set of descriptions across varied prompt framings and environmental contexts. The results show notable variation in structural novelty across models, with open-weight models outscoring proprietary models on average, and all models surpassing a human comparison group in departing from Earth defaults on every biological feature examined. The work highlights that current proprietary models are not necessarily the most creative by this structural measure, and provides a reproducible, reference-grounded framework for evaluating novelty in language model outputs.
items.citation: Jonas Oppenlaender, Johanna M. Silvennoinen. AlienBench: A Benchmark of Structural Novelty in Language Model Outputs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Two Pentaplex Real-Time Fluorescent PCR Assays for Simultaneous Detection of Ten Ovine Respiratory and Reproductive Pathogens.
items.summary: Two pentaplex real-time fluorescent PCR assay panels were developed to simultaneously detect ten major pathogens responsible for respiratory and reproductive disease in sheep. The first panel targets five respiratory pathogens, including Bluetongue virus, Foot-and-mouth disease virus, and Peste des petits ruminants virus, while the second targets five reproductive pathogens, including *Brucella* spp., *Toxoplasma gondii*, and *Chlamydia abortus*, with each panel utilizing six fluorescent channels for multiplexed detection. Validation against reference materials demonstrated very low limits of detection, excellent linearity, and minimal variation within and between assays, alongside high specificity with no cross-reactivity among the ten targets. Testing against a large collection of clinical samples from multiple regions confirmed strong agreement with established reference methods. The authors conclude that these assays provide a rapid, sensitive, and reliable platform for the differential diagnosis and epidemiological surveillance of major ovine pathogens.
items.citation: Wang S, Bai Z, Wan B et al.. Two Pentaplex Real-Time Fluorescent PCR Assays for Simultaneous Detection of Ten Ovine Respiratory and Reproductive Pathogens.. Viruses. 2026

items.title: Nanobodies: A Promising Toolkit for Diagnostic Applications
items.summary: This paper reviews the structural and functional properties of nanobodies — single-domain antigen-binding fragments derived from camelid heavy-chain-only antibodies — and examines their growing utility in diagnostic applications. The authors survey how characteristics such as small molecular weight, high solubility, and favorable stability enable nanobodies to access epitopes and penetrate tissues in ways that conventional antibodies may not. The review covers their integration into a broad range of detection platforms, including immunoassays, biosensors, and in vivo imaging modalities such as positron emission tomography and single-photon emission computed tomography. Advances including multivalent designs, site-specific conjugation strategies, and improved expression systems are discussed as factors that have enhanced diagnostic performance. The paper also highlights ongoing clinical trials and emerging strategies for developing scalable, sensitive nanobody-based diagnostic platforms.
items.citation: Wei Wu, Abid Ali, Li Sun et al.. Nanobodies: A Promising Toolkit for Diagnostic Applications. SmartMat. 2026

items.title: Machine-learning-integrated NLRC3 and cardiac troponin T dual-analyte lateral-flow biosensor for point-of-care acute coronary syndrome screening and acute myocardial infarction-unstable angina discrimination.
items.summary: This paper developed a point-of-care lateral-flow biosensor designed to simultaneously detect two biomarkers—NLRC3, an inflammatory mediator, and cardiac troponin T, a myocardial injury marker—for screening acute coronary syndrome and distinguishing acute myocardial infarction from unstable angina. The biosensor uses europium nanoparticle time-resolved fluorescence in a dual-channel configuration, completing quantitative measurement of both analytes from serum within twenty minutes. A Naïve Bayes machine-learning classifier was integrated to combine the two biomarker readouts, improving diagnostic discrimination beyond what either marker achieved alone. Clinical evaluation showed that while NLRC3 alone provided moderate accuracy for acute coronary syndrome identification, the dual-analyte machine-learning approach substantially improved sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy for differentiating acute myocardial infarction from unstable angina. The authors propose this platform as a practical decentralized triage tool that bridges inflammatory-risk and myocardial-injury detection within a single lateral-flow format.
items.citation: Gu X, Teng P, Li X et al.. Machine-learning-integrated NLRC3 and cardiac troponin T dual-analyte lateral-flow biosensor for point-of-care acute coronary syndrome screening and acute myocardial infarction-unstable angina discrimination.. Mikrochimica acta. 2026

items.title: Smartphone AI-Enabled Lateral Flow Immunoassay Platform Using Advanced Quantum Dots for Intelligent Quantitative Diagnostics.
items.citation: Atta S, Thorsen TL, Vasse T et al.. Smartphone AI-Enabled Lateral Flow Immunoassay Platform Using Advanced Quantum Dots for Intelligent Quantitative Diagnostics.. ACS applied materials & interfaces. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future potential of lateral flow immunoassay technology for detecting viral pathogens in the context of infectious disease surveillance. The authors reframe the technology not merely as a point-of-care testing tool but as a point-of-need self-testing platform capable of supporting large-scale epidemic screening and pandemic preparedness. The review systematically covers advances in signal generation using diverse nanomaterials spanning colorimetric, fluorescent, magnetic, surface-enhanced Raman scattering, and photothermal approaches, alongside multimodal and multiplex detection strategies and the integration of machine learning for signal interpretation. Applications across viral antigen, antibody, and nucleic acid detection are comprehensively surveyed, and persistent limitations including sensitivity, target specificity, cost, usability, and stability are critically assessed. The authors conclude that continued development in nanomaterials, intelligent data processing, and multi-target detection will be essential to realizing the transformative potential of this platform in both emergency pandemic response and routine decentralized diagnostics.
items.citation: Li L, Liu F, He X et al.. Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Ligand-directed Janus self-assembly with dual-aggregation enabling magneto-optical switching for enhanced lateral flow immunoassay.
items.citation: Liu T, Sun J, Huang J et al.. Ligand-directed Janus self-assembly with dual-aggregation enabling magneto-optical switching for enhanced lateral flow immunoassay.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: SARS-CoV-2 Point-of-Care Testing Modalities: Integrating Molecular, Immunological, Biosensor, and AI Approaches.
items.summary: This review examined the landscape of point-of-care testing technologies developed for COVID-19 diagnosis, motivated by the pandemic's demonstration that rapid, decentralized diagnostics are essential for clinical decision-making and public health response. The authors conducted a structured literature search across major databases to evaluate molecular assays, antigen and antibody tests, biosensor platforms, and artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostic approaches. Molecular methods such as rapid RT-PCR, LAMP, and CRISPR-based technologies were found to offer high sensitivity and specificity suited to decentralized use, while antigen tests provide rapid and affordable screening with performance that varies by viral load and circulating variant. Antibody-based testing proved most useful for seroprevalence and immune monitoring rather than acute infection detection, and emerging biosensor and AI systems showed analytical promise but largely remain at prototype or early-validation stages requiring further clinical study. The review concludes that no single testing modality is universally optimal, and that complementary use of multiple approaches, alongside advances in multiplexing, digital connectivity, and variant-resilient detection, will strengthen both COVID-19 management and future infectious disease preparedness.
items.citation: Hetta HF, Ahmed R, Haseeb A et al.. SARS-CoV-2 Point-of-Care Testing Modalities: Integrating Molecular, Immunological, Biosensor, and AI Approaches.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Identification of candidate markers for the isolation of neuron-specific extracellular vesicles
items.summary: This paper addressed the challenge of isolating brain cell type-specific extracellular vesicles from biofluids for non-invasive monitoring of neurological conditions. The researchers combined gene expression data, proteomics of extracellular vesicles from cerebrospinal fluid and plasma, and computational analysis to identify candidate surface protein markers capable of distinguishing vesicles derived from neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and microglia. They developed a high-purity extracellular vesicle isolation method and used ultrasensitive immunoassays to validate candidate neuron-specific markers, confirming that NRXN3 is present on extracellular vesicles in both cerebrospinal fluid and plasma. Building on this, they demonstrated efficient immunoisolation of NRXN3-positive extracellular vesicles, establishing a generalizable workflow for capturing cell type-specific vesicles. The work advances the broader goal of leveraging extracellular vesicles as accessible biomarkers for studying brain diseases.
items.citation: Dmitry Ter‐Ovanesyan, Sara T. Whiteman, Tal Gilboa et al.. Identification of candidate markers for the isolation of neuron-specific extracellular vesicles. Nature Neuroscience. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in Alzheimer’s disease: From molecular mechanisms to therapeutic strategies
items.summary: This review examines the current state of Alzheimer's disease research, encompassing both the molecular mechanisms underlying the disease and the therapeutic strategies being developed to address it. The authors synthesize recent advances across several domains, including the pathological roles of amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles, apolipoprotein E biology, neuroimmunology, and biomarker discovery. New disease-modifying therapies capable of slowing cognitive decline by clearing amyloid plaques from the brain are highlighted as a meaningful clinical advance, though treatments that can halt or prevent cognitive impairment altogether remain unavailable. The review argues that these collective discoveries are transforming how Alzheimer's disease is diagnosed and treated, raising the prospect that the condition could eventually become both treatable and preventable.
items.citation: Michelle Diane Rudman, Jason D. Ulrich, David M. Holtzman. Recent advances in Alzheimer’s disease: From molecular mechanisms to therapeutic strategies. Cell. 2026

items.title: Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness
items.summary: This review examines hantaviruses as emerging rodent-borne pathogens responsible for hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, synthesizing current knowledge across virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical presentation, and public health response. The paper addresses how environmental drivers such as climate change, urbanization, and land-use transformation are reshaping rodent reservoir dynamics and increasing the risk of viral spillover to humans. Particular attention is paid to surveillance and diagnostic shortfalls in tropical and Caribbean regions where hantavirus circulation is likely underappreciated. The review highlights recent advances including molecular diagnostics, genomic surveillance tools, vaccine candidates, monoclonal antibody therapies, and climate-informed early warning systems. The authors argue that integrated One Health frameworks combining human, animal, and environmental monitoring, alongside strengthened laboratory capacity and regional collaboration, are essential for improving outbreak detection and reducing the global burden of hantavirus disease.
items.citation: Maria E. Ramos‐Niño, Nicolette Chiem, Prakash V. A. K. Ramdass. Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Quantum dot biosensors for highly sensitive and multiplex detection in biomedical diagnostics
items.summary: This review examines quantum dot-based biosensors as platforms for biomedical diagnostics, focusing on how their unique optical properties address the limitations of conventional immunoassays such as low sensitivity, photobleaching, and poor tissue penetration. The authors survey recent advances across fluorescent, photoelectrochemical, and electrochemiluminescent biosensor formats, explaining how quantum dot surface chemistry can be engineered with antibodies, aptamers, peptides, or nucleic acids to enable selective and multiplexed detection of pathogens, cancer biomarkers, and metabolites. Near-infrared-emitting quantum dots are highlighted for their ability to reduce tissue autofluorescence and improve imaging depth for real-time in vivo molecular tracking. The review also addresses persistent challenges including toxicity and biocompatibility, discussing mitigation strategies such as surface passivation, cadmium-free compositions, and biocompatible coatings. Distinctively, the authors offer an integrated mechanistic framework that links surface engineering choices to sensing performance and clinical translational relevance, aiming to guide next-generation diagnostic development.
items.citation: Soumendu Patra, Harshita Shand. Quantum dot biosensors for highly sensitive and multiplex detection in biomedical diagnostics. Discover Sensors. 2026

items.title: Plant-Derived Compounds as Antibiotic Adjuvants Against Drug-Resistant ESKAPE Pathogens: Mechanisms of Action, Synergistic Strategies, and Translational Challenges
items.summary: This review examined plant-derived compounds as potential adjuvants for restoring antibiotic effectiveness against drug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens, a group of bacteria responsible for a major share of difficult-to-treat clinical infections. The authors systematically analyzed published studies focusing on the mechanisms by which phytochemicals enhance antibiotic activity, their synergistic interactions with conventional drugs, structure-activity relationships, and translational evidence from animal models. They found that numerous plant-derived compounds can potentiate antibiotics through several resistance-modulating mechanisms, including efflux pump inhibition, biofilm disruption, membrane permeabilization, and quorum sensing interference, with specific examples such as quercetin restoring ciprofloxacin susceptibility in Staphylococcus aureus and ajoene sensitizing Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms to tobramycin. Despite these promising in vitro findings, the review identifies substantial barriers to clinical translation, including poor bioavailability, inconsistent standardization, and limited pharmacokinetic data. The authors conclude that while phytochemical adjuvants represent a compelling strategy against multidrug-resistant pathogens, progress toward therapeutic use requires more rigorous translational research and standardized experimental methodologies.
items.citation: Stefano Ruga, Elisa Matarese, Fabio Castagna et al.. Plant-Derived Compounds as Antibiotic Adjuvants Against Drug-Resistant ESKAPE Pathogens: Mechanisms of Action, Synergistic Strategies, and Translational Challenges. Antibiotics. 2026

items.title: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of generating videos with precise spatial structure, coherent motion dynamics, and controllable scene composition—limitations that persist despite recent advances in video generation quality. The authors introduce Video-Coder, a code-driven agent trained to autonomously write and execute code that constructs dynamic three-dimensional scenes, which then serve as structural and motion guides for downstream video generation models. To enable this approach, they developed a dedicated data pipeline with curated datasets, a unified interactive environment for agent training and inference, and a training procedure combining supervised fine-tuning with agentic reinforcement learning using dual rewards based on code execution and video quality. A key design choice is an annealing strategy that progressively shifts the model's reliance from execution-based rewards toward video-based rewards during training. The resulting system achieves substantial improvements on established benchmarks for physical plausibility and video quality compared to a strong baseline generator.
items.citation: Chaoyang Wang, Sicheng Gao, Junan Hu et al.. Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Unconditional Uniqueness of KdV and mKdV Green Solutions at Low Regularity
items.summary: This paper studies uniqueness of solutions to two classical nonlinear dispersive equations—the Korteweg–de Vries equation and the real defocusing modified Korteweg–de Vries equation—at the lowest known regularities for which well-posedness has been established. The authors work within the framework of Green solutions, a solution concept defined through the diagonal Green functions of the Lax operators associated with these equations via inverse scattering, which provides an intrinsically well-defined notion of evolution at low regularity. A central technical achievement is the derivation of automatic local smoothing directly from the Green identities, yielding improved integrability of solutions and their nonlinear expressions in spacetime uniformly over spatial translates. Using these estimates, the authors establish unconditional uniqueness within the class of Green solutions, meaning uniqueness holds without imposing any auxiliary integrability conditions beyond the natural solution space. As a consequence, every Green solution in these regularity classes is identified with the unique continuous extension of the smooth Schwartz-class flow.
items.citation: Zhimeng Ouyang. Unconditional Uniqueness of KdV and mKdV Green Solutions at Low Regularity. arXiv. 2026

items.title: FlowMoP: Stochastic Multi-Person Motion Prediction
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of predicting future 3D motions for multiple people simultaneously, treating it as an inherently stochastic rather than deterministic task. The authors developed a conditional flow matching framework that jointly generates diverse plausible future motions for multiple agents, using a B-spline reparameterization to enforce temporal smoothness and reduce the generative state space, alongside a dual-stream transformer that incorporates observed motions of nearby agents to enable interaction-aware predictions. The approach models both global trajectories and body pose, producing a full predictive distribution rather than a single fixed output per agent. Evaluated on established benchmarks, the method outperforms deterministic baselines across multiple error metrics despite generating a distribution of predictions, and also establishes the first motion prediction baseline on a large-scale professional soccer dataset. Results on the soccer dataset further demonstrate that social conditioning meaningfully shapes predictive uncertainty, concentrating it along directions constrained by inter-agent interactions.
items.citation: Aadya Agrawal, Ho Kei Cheng, Alexander Schwing. FlowMoP: Stochastic Multi-Person Motion Prediction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Multi-phase Carbon Structure and Dynamics in NGC 6334: Insights from CO, [C I], and [C II]
items.summary: This study presents high-resolution observations of multiple carbon-tracing emission lines toward the central region of the massive star-forming complex NGC 6334, combining morphological, kinematic, and line ratio analyses to characterize carbon across its ionized, atomic, and molecular phases. The researchers mapped emission from ionized carbon, neutral atomic carbon, and both common and rare isotopologue forms of carbon monoxide, then applied techniques including K-means clustering of line ratios against dust continuum emission to identify spatial and chemical structure. They find that ionized carbon emission is the most spatially extended and dynamically complex tracer, permeating the region and arising from photodissociation regions near ionized hydrogen bubbles as well as more diffuse warm gas associated with cloud formation or dispersal, while molecular carbon tracers are compact and quiescent. Neutral atomic carbon occupies an intermediate spatial regime and appears to trace gas dynamics linked to colliding flows or cloud-cloud collisions, with its broader extent relative to the rare isotopologue suggesting it probes transitional layers connecting dense molecular gas to diffuse envelopes. The combined evidence portrays NGC 6334 as a clumpy, feedback-dominated photodissociation region ridge in which UV photons penetrate deeply into the dense gas through a porous structure, with multiple carbon phases coexisting and dynamical processing evident through distinct velocity components.
items.citation: S. Neupane, F. Wyrowski, N. Schneider et al.. Multi-phase Carbon Structure and Dynamics in NGC 6334: Insights from CO, [C I], and [C II]. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Flow-Guided Target-Space Alignment via Path Consistency
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of multimodal alignment where a source modality must be mapped into a fixed target space that is used directly for downstream analysis, requiring both preservation of global target distribution structure and accurate instance-level paired correspondence. The authors identify limitations in existing approaches, noting that contrastive, distribution-matching, and pointwise regression objectives each capture only part of this dual requirement. They propose FlowAlign, a method that repurposes conditional flow matching as a training-time alignment signal, using the learned flow field to guide source representations toward the fixed target space in a way that respects both paired correspondences and the geometric structure of the target distribution. Theoretical analysis is provided showing how the method controls endpoint accuracy and captures local target-space geometry to improve paired correspondence. Experiments across synthetic data, paired single-cell multiome benchmarks, and image-text alignment demonstrate that FlowAlign achieves improved instance-level correspondence while maintaining compatibility with target-space structure.
items.citation: Ruizhi Yuan, Zeqiu Yu, Wei Gao et al.. Flow-Guided Target-Space Alignment via Path Consistency. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Quantifying the importance of equation of state and transport property compatibility in supercritical fluids
items.summary: This paper investigated the accuracy of thermodynamic and transport property calculations in high-fidelity simulations of supercritical fluids, with a focus on supercritical carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and methane. The study identified and quantified two distinct sources of error that arise when generalized equations of state and generalized transport property correlations are used instead of species-specific ones: errors in density as a function of temperature and pressure, and the propagation of those density errors into viscosity and thermal conductivity calculations, since transport correlations are expressed as functions of temperature and density rather than temperature and pressure directly. A systematic procedure was developed to disentangle these two error contributions and assess their relative magnitudes across thermodynamic state space. Both sources of error were found to be largest near the critical temperature, and their combined magnitude was judged sufficient to compromise both the numerical stability and physical accuracy of supercritical flow simulations. The work underscores the importance of ensuring compatibility between the equation of state and transport property correlations used in such simulations.
items.citation: Tyler Fara, Shashank Yellapantula, Bruce Perry et al.. Quantifying the importance of equation of state and transport property compatibility in supercritical fluids. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Beyond lateral flow: vertical flow immunoassays as thermodynamically assisted rapid diagnostics.
items.summary: This review examines vertical flow immunoassays (VFAs) as an alternative to the dominant lateral flow immunoassay format used in point-of-care diagnostics. The authors analyze how the single-pass capillary architecture of lateral flow devices imposes fundamental constraints on analyte capture kinetics, non-specific background, multiplexing capacity, and performance at high analyte concentrations, then describe how VFAs use a stacked-membrane design to overcome each of these limitations. Through decoupling convective delivery from immunoreaction kinetics, VFAs enable selective thermodynamic washing, two-dimensional multiplexing arrays, and elimination of the hook effect. Head-to-head comparisons with chemistry-matched lateral flow devices demonstrate large improvements in detection limits, and integration with surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy, electrochemical transduction, nanoparticle amplification, and deep-learning analysis extends sensitivity into the sub-picogram-per-milliliter range. The review surveys the physicochemical basis of these performance gains, maps applications across clinical, food safety, and environmental contexts, and critically examines the engineering and commercial barriers that have so far prevented VFAs from achieving widespread deployment despite their demonstrated sensitivity advantages.
items.citation: Nainar SNS, Chu YY, Lin HC et al.. Beyond lateral flow: vertical flow immunoassays as thermodynamically assisted rapid diagnostics.. Chemical communications (Cambridge, England). 2026

items.title: Validation and performance of a rapid HIV-1 viral load assay.
items.summary: The study evaluated whether a rapid quantitative nucleic acid test, the Xpert HIV-1 Viral Load XC assay, could serve as a primary diagnostic tool within HIV-1 testing workflows, potentially enabling both diagnosis and initial viral load measurement in a single clinical encounter. The assay was assessed for analytical performance including range, precision, and reproducibility, and was compared against standard-of-care methods and several other HIV assays using plasma samples from HIV-positive and HIV-negative individuals. The assay demonstrated strong quantitative linearity and full agreement with a reference quantitative assay on a panel of HIV-positive and HIV-negative samples, and its turnaround time was substantially faster than conventional batch testing. However, positive agreement with comparator assays was imperfect, with most discrepancies occurring in samples below the lower limit of quantification, and the assay produced a small proportion of invalid results. The findings suggest that while rapid molecular HIV diagnostics offer promise for point-of-care linkage to care, current limitations in sensitivity at low viral loads underscore the need for continued development of tools that are both highly sensitive and rapid.
items.citation: Uhteg K, Bayan MH, Boudreau A et al.. Validation and performance of a rapid HIV-1 viral load assay.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Patient perspectives on point-of-care HIV nucleic acid tests for viral load monitoring in Seattle, WA.
items.summary: This study investigated how people with HIV perceive and accept point-of-care nucleic acid testing for viral load monitoring as an alternative to standard laboratory-based testing, which can take days to return results. Participants enrolled in a clinical study received a semi-quantitative point-of-care test using fingerstick whole blood samples, then completed surveys and in-depth interviews about their experiences. Participants generally preferred the point-of-care approach over standard testing, particularly valuing the faster turnaround time and the convenience of receiving results during the clinic visit. Despite this overall acceptance, participants expressed a preference for an even shorter turnaround time and a lower limit of detection than the tested device currently offers. The findings suggest that point-of-care nucleic acid testing is acceptable to people with HIV and could be especially beneficial for those with inconsistent engagement in care, though improvements in speed and sensitivity would enhance its practical implementation.
items.citation: Niemann LA, Murphy M, Violette LR et al.. Patient perspectives on point-of-care HIV nucleic acid tests for viral load monitoring in Seattle, WA.. AIDS care. 2026

items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article examines the contested question of whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection. The paper presents opposing arguments on key issues, including whether high-performance athletes are genuinely more infection-prone than the general population, whether exercise independently alters immunity beyond confounding factors such as sleep disruption, psychological stress, travel, and nutritional deficits, and whether the biomarkers and study designs used in this field are adequate to draw firm conclusions. There is broad agreement that regular moderate-intensity exercise of limited duration benefits immune defense, particularly in older adults and those with chronic disease, while arduous exercise characteristic of elite athletes and military personnel has long been associated with elevated infection burden. However, the opposing groups contest whether exercise per se is causally responsible for increased infection risk, or whether this risk is instead driven by the many non-exercise stressors that accompany intense training and competition. The authors conclude that infection susceptibility is multifactorial and call for more rigorous empirical research to resolve whether exercise is an independent causative factor.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. PubMed. 2026

items.title: MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks
items.summary: This paper investigated whether internalized reasoning models and externalized agent-based frameworks represent competing or complementary approaches to complex medical reasoning in large language models. The researchers developed MedicalAgentsBench, a curated benchmark of challenging clinical questions drawn from multiple medical datasets using difficulty-aware selection and contamination screening, then systematically evaluated a broad range of internalized reasoning models, base models, and agent-based methods against it. They found that both approaches independently improve performance on complex clinical questions, and critically, that their benefits are additive rather than exclusive. The best performance was achieved by combining an internalized reasoning model with an agent workflow, while Pareto analysis confirmed this combination also dominates the cost-performance trade-off frontier. Additionally, the study identified that lightweight optimization of less expensive models provides a viable pathway for resource-constrained deployment.
items.citation: Yanjun Shao, Xiangru Tang, Jiwoong Sohn et al.. MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks. Patterns. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and clinical translation. The authors synthesize how genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic approaches collectively illuminate the molecular underpinnings of disease, while deep learning architectures decode these complex biological datasets to uncover hidden patterns. The combined framework is assessed for its capacity to accelerate target identification, lead optimization, drug repositioning, de novo compound discovery, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. Applications across oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions are examined to illustrate the translational potential of this convergence. The review also highlights persistent challenges, including harmonization of disparate data streams, reproducibility concerns, and the mitigation of algorithmic biases, while presenting a forward-looking vision for bench-to-clinic medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Trial design and end points in hepatocellular carcinoma: an EASL–AASLD–ILCA consensus statement
items.citation: Josep Maria Llovet, Ezequiel Mauro, Lorenza Rimassa et al.. Trial design and end points in hepatocellular carcinoma: an EASL–AASLD–ILCA consensus statement. Nature Reviews Clinical Oncology. 2026

items.title: APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update
items.summary: This paper presents updated clinical practice guidelines from the Asian Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver (APASL) for the management of chronic hepatitis B infection. The guidelines were developed by a Viral Elimination Taskforce composed of key opinion leaders from member countries and regions, taking into account shifting hepatitis B epidemiology, socioeconomic changes, and technological advancements. The document addresses the persistent and growing burden of chronic hepatitis B in the Asia Pacific region, which continues to cause significant morbidity and mortality through complications such as acute-on-chronic liver failure, end-stage liver cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma despite decades of progress in screening, vaccination, antiviral therapy, and surveillance. The guidelines provide recommendations across thirteen major areas encompassing screening, vaccination, treatment, and hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance, with the goal of offering practical and cost-effective guidance to healthcare professionals, policy-makers, and patients. The overarching aim is to advance efforts toward eliminating the disease burden attributable to chronic hepatitis B infection across the Asia Pacific region.
items.citation: Hong You, Rakhi Maiwall, Jing Chen et al.. APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update. Hepatology International. 2026

items.title: Time to HIV rebound after infusion of long-acting broadly neutralising antibodies 3BNC117-LS and 10-1074-LS and analytical treatment interruption (the RIO trial): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial
items.summary: This trial investigated whether long-acting, Fc-engineered broadly neutralising antibodies (LS-bNAbs) could maintain HIV viral suppression in people who interrupted antiretroviral therapy. In a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled design, participants who had been virally suppressed on antiretroviral therapy initiated during early-stage HIV received either two LS-bNAbs (3BNC117-LS and 10-1074-LS) or placebo before undergoing an analytical treatment interruption. By twenty weeks after treatment interruption, the LS-bNAb group was substantially less likely to experience viral rebound compared to the placebo group, with the antibody recipients showing a markedly delayed time to rebound. Notably, a subset of LS-bNAb recipients maintained ART-free viral control beyond ninety-six weeks even when modelled antibody concentrations had fallen below presumed therapeutic thresholds, suggesting that the antibodies may have induced durable immune mechanisms beyond their direct antiviral activity. The authors conclude that LS-bNAbs represent a meaningful step toward ART-free HIV remission and that these findings should inform future combination strategies aimed at sustaining post-treatment HIV control.
items.citation: Ming Jie Lee, Louise-Rae Cherrill, Panagiota Zacharopoulou et al.. Time to HIV rebound after infusion of long-acting broadly neutralising antibodies 3BNC117-LS and 10-1074-LS and analytical treatment interruption (the RIO trial): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial. The Lancet HIV. 2026

items.title: Raman anyon-Hubbard model in a 1D Bose lattice gas
items.summary: This paper investigates how one-dimensional anyons—quantum particles with fractional statistics interpolating between bosons and fermions—can be realized and studied in a cold-atom lattice setting. The authors show theoretically that loading a Raman-coupled Bose gas with imbalanced interactions into a one-dimensional optical lattice gives rise to what they call the Raman anyon-Hubbard model, in which bosons acquire density-dependent Peierls phases during tunneling, effectively behaving as anyons. This model generalizes the standard anyon-Hubbard model by featuring unbounded rather than periodic statistical interactions in a certain limit, connecting to the chiral BF field theory as its continuum description. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the system exhibits hallmark anyon signatures including a density-dependent asymmetry in the momentum distribution, interaction-induced asymmetric transport, and chiral bound states. The authors argue that these phenomena are experimentally accessible using Raman-coupled potassium atoms, making this proposal a viable platform for exploring many-body anyonic physics beyond the few-particle regime.
items.citation: Josep Cabedo, Claudio Iacovelli, Leticia Tarruell et al.. Raman anyon-Hubbard model in a 1D Bose lattice gas. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Classical control of quantum-state relaxation in confined molecular hydrogen
items.summary: This paper investigated how the surrounding environment controls quantum-state conversion between the ortho and para nuclear-spin isomers of molecular hydrogen, a process forbidden in isolated H₂ but enabled by intermolecular interactions. The researchers confined H₂ within crystalline CO₂ and N₂O host solids and used rotationally resolved infrared spectroscopy at low temperature to directly measure how nuclear-spin conversion rates depend on H₂ concentration. They found that increasing the amount of H₂ loaded into the crystal progressively suppresses nuclear-spin conversion, reaching nearly complete suppression at moderate loading levels. Molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations revealed two complementary mechanisms behind this effect: concentration-dependent changes in the thermally available phonon modes that mediate relaxation, and strain-induced clustering of H₂ molecules that removes them from the host crystal field responsible for enabling the spin conversion. Together, these findings establish a multiscale mechanism in which a classical, collective mechanical response of the host lattice governs the connectivity and dynamics of a microscopic quantum two-level system.
items.citation: Nathan McLane, Richard C. Remsing, Leah G. Dodson. Classical control of quantum-state relaxation in confined molecular hydrogen. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Fifty-Two Shades of Pig: What the UCR Archive Really Asks Classifiers to Do
items.summary: This paper examines the UCR Time Series Classification Archive, the dominant benchmark used to evaluate time series classification methods, questioning whether its datasets actually reflect the problems the field intends to solve. The authors conducted a provenance audit of the archive's datasets, tracing their origins and intended tasks. They found that multiple datasets have been repurposed from their original classification objectives, derive from artificial or toy experimental setups, or contain flawed train-test splits, using the pig airway pressure recordings as a prominent example where the original clinical task of detecting hemorrhage was replaced with individual pig identification. The authors also raise concerns about the prevalence of non-temporal ordered sequences such as spectra and shape outlines being treated as time series, and about potential distortions introduced by decomposing multivariate problems. These findings challenge the validity of using archive-wide performance scores as a meaningful measure of progress in time series classification and call for greater scrutiny in benchmark design and deployment-relevant evaluation.
items.citation: Omar Swelam, Jaris Küken, Shi Bin Hoo et al.. Fifty-Two Shades of Pig: What the UCR Archive Really Asks Classifiers to Do. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Logic of Factor Portfolios: Boolean Rules, Interactions, and Trading Costs
items.summary: This paper examines how investors construct portfolios by converting signals into holdings through decision rules, framing many common strategies as Boolean functions of threshold statements about signal ranks. The authors apply a Walsh decomposition to decompose any such rule's returns into exposures to individual signals and their interactions, and derive closed-form predictions for portfolio turnover based on the persistence of underlying statements and the order of interactions involved. Empirical tests in U.S. stocks spanning several decades confirm that predicted and realized persistence are nearly perfectly correlated and that predicted turnover closely matches realized turnover, while smooth rank-based implementations are shown to trade less than threshold-based ones for equivalent interaction exposures. A key finding is that trading costs scale with interaction order while return premia decline with order, so that the majority of single-signal portfolios cover their transaction costs but only a small fraction of higher-order interaction portfolios do. Nevertheless, interaction portfolios provide out-of-sample Sharpe ratio improvements over single-signal tangency portfolios and capture risk exposures that conventional factor sorts fail to span, as evidenced by rejection of a six-factor model.
items.citation: Ziyao Wang, Svetlozar T. Rachev, Frank J. Fabozzi. The Logic of Factor Portfolios: Boolean Rules, Interactions, and Trading Costs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Generalized H matrix stability for power systems
items.summary: This paper investigates the small-signal stability of power systems with arbitrary load configurations, focusing on locally constant power loads in lossless networks. The central analytical tool is a matrix H formed from partial derivatives of generator powers with respect to relative angles, whose properties are shown to determine the local stability of any equilibrium point: positive definiteness of H implies asymptotic stability, while a full-rank H that is not positive definite implies instability. The key contribution is extending this H matrix stability criterion to allow loads to be located anywhere within the transmission network, removing the previous restriction that loads must share buses with generators. Quantitative relationships between the eigenvalues of H and the system Jacobian matrix are also established, providing deeper insight into stability margins. Case studies on large networks demonstrate that the generalized criterion maintains accurate stability assessments where alternative approaches prove overly conservative, while achieving a substantial computational speedup relative to Jacobian-based methods.
items.citation: Elinor Ginzburg-Ganz, Yoash Levron, Juri Belikov et al.. Generalized H matrix stability for power systems. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Path-dependent triage: Early judgments lead conversational AI chatbots to miss mental-health emergencies
items.summary: This paper examined how AI chatbots handle mental health triage in multi-turn conversations, where clinically relevant information is disclosed gradually rather than all at once. The researchers evaluated thirteen frontier AI chatbots conducting ten-turn conversations with simulated users drawn from a large set of structured mental health case files spanning urgency levels from routine care to emergency. The chatbots failed to recognize a substantial proportion of mental health emergencies, and this failure rate was far higher than when all clinical details were presented in a single message, even though the decisive facts had typically been disclosed by the conversation's end. The core problem was identified as path dependence: early triage judgments anchored subsequent ones, so emergencies missed in early turns were rarely corrected as new evidence emerged, and chatbots also perseverated on narrow, stereotyped lines of questioning more than human clinicians did with the same transcripts. The authors argue that these failure modes are invisible to single-turn benchmarks, underscore the need for multi-turn evaluation frameworks, and point toward concrete mitigations for making conversational AI safer in consumer mental health contexts.
items.citation: Veith Weilnhammer, Raymond Dolan, Lennart Luettgau et al.. Path-dependent triage: Early judgments lead conversational AI chatbots to miss mental-health emergencies. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Evaluating long-term programmatic outcomes of patients with advanced HIV disease: Insights from 12 years of antiretroviral therapy scale-up in rural KwaZulu-Natal.
items.summary: This study examined long-term treatment outcomes among patients initiating antiretroviral therapy with advanced HIV disease in rural KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, over a twelve-year period spanning multiple policy eras. Using retrospective cohort data from public health facilities, the researchers analyzed retention in care and virological suppression among adults with low CD4 counts or advanced WHO disease staging, applying competing risk and Poisson regression models to identify factors associated with loss to follow-up and viral suppression. Retention in care remained high across follow-up periods, and among those with available viral load data, suppression exceeded eighty-three percent at all time points, with outcomes notably improving under the Universal Test and Treat era compared with earlier treatment periods. Men and individuals with the lowest CD4 counts faced higher risks of loss to follow-up, while women and those initiating treatment within one week of diagnosis were more likely to achieve virological suppression. The authors conclude that although retention and suppression rates are encouraging, viral load testing uptake remains suboptimal and a substantial gap persists in achieving undetectable viral loads, underscoring the need for the WHO advanced HIV disease care package and targeted male-focused interventions.
items.citation: Kitenge MK, Fatti G, Laxmeshwar C et al.. Evaluating long-term programmatic outcomes of patients with advanced HIV disease: Insights from 12 years of antiretroviral therapy scale-up in rural KwaZulu-Natal.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: An Evaluation of Perinatal Human Immunodeficiency Virus Transmissions in New York State, 2007-2020.
items.summary: This population-based retrospective cohort study examined predictors of perinatal HIV transmission and unsuppressed viral load near delivery among birthing parent-infant dyads in New York State over more than a decade. Using linked surveillance, laboratory, and medical record data, the researchers applied multivariable models to identify factors associated with both transmission and viral non-suppression. The overall rate of perinatal HIV transmission was very low, yet having an unsuppressed viral load at the test closest to delivery was the strongest predictor of transmission. Key predictors of viral non-suppression included not using antiretroviral therapy during pregnancy, documented illicit substance use during pregnancy, and later initiation of prenatal care. The findings highlight that while perinatal transmission has become rare, ensuring viral suppression through timely prenatal care and antiretroviral therapy use remains critical for eliminating the remaining cases.
items.citation: Swain CA, Wong C, Stolz A et al.. An Evaluation of Perinatal Human Immunodeficiency Virus Transmissions in New York State, 2007-2020.. O&G open. 2026

items.title: Testing for Recent HIV Infections: A Conceptual Review.
items.summary: This paper reviewed the science and application of HIV recency assays, which are laboratory-based or point-of-care tests designed to distinguish recent from long-standing HIV infections in order to estimate incidence from cross-sectional data. The authors conducted a narrative synthesis of foundational methods papers, validation studies, and global guidance documents to trace how these tools have developed and been deployed. The review identifies four generations of assay technology, progressing from early detuned enzyme immunoassays through avidity-based tests, rapid point-of-care platforms, and emerging genomic approaches, with performance characterized by two key metrics: mean duration of recent infection and false-recent rate. The authors found that assay performance is complicated by biological variability, HIV subtype differences, antiretroviral therapy exposure, and host factors, all of which can introduce misclassification. They conclude that while recency assays are valuable for surveillance, outbreak detection, and prevention program monitoring, their future utility depends on improved assay design, integration with genomic and programmatic data, real-time surveillance infrastructure, and sustained attention to ethical and community engagement considerations.
items.citation: Suligoi B, Galli C. Testing for Recent HIV Infections: A Conceptual Review.. Pathogens (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: A qualitative study exploring factors associated with the accuracy of recording malaria rapid diagnostic test results in two high-burden regions of Côte d'Ivoire.
items.summary: This study investigated why healthcare workers in two high-burden regions of Côte d'Ivoire sometimes fail to accurately record malaria rapid diagnostic test results, a practice that undermines disease surveillance. Using a qualitative approach embedded within a broader mixed-methods evaluation, researchers photographed RDTs performed by healthcare workers, had results independently verified by an external panel, and conducted semi-structured interviews with workers selected based on how well their recorded interpretations agreed with the independent readings. The key differentiator between high- and low-agreement groups was not procedural knowledge or resource access, but rather confidence in RDT results, particularly trust in negative results for symptomatic patients. Healthcare workers with low agreement more frequently feared missing true malaria cases and the consequences of withholding antimalarials, leading some to deliberately falsify registers by converting negative results to positive or omitting treatment documentation to avoid scrutiny. The authors conclude that interventions should focus on building clinical confidence in managing RDT-negative fevers through supportive supervision, expanding non-malarial diagnostic options, and redesigning documentation systems to allow transparent recording of non-adherence without creating incentives for misreporting.
items.citation: Kouakou OMA, Bédia-Tanoh VA, Arnzen A et al.. A qualitative study exploring factors associated with the accuracy of recording malaria rapid diagnostic test results in two high-burden regions of Côte d'Ivoire.. Malaria journal. 2026

items.title: Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a multi-antigen rapid diagnostic test (RDT) for malaria in a region of southern Ethiopia where both *Plasmodium falciparum* and *P. vivax* co-circulate, a setting complicated by low-density infections and pfhrp2/3 gene deletions that undermine conventional HRP2-based testing. A cross-sectional study enrolled febrile patients at health facilities during peak transmission season, comparing the new Bioline Malaria multi-Ag Pf/Pf/Pv RDT—which detects HRP2 alongside dual pLDH markers for both species—against expert microscopy and quantitative PCR as reference standards. The multi-antigen RDT showed high specificity and near-perfect agreement with expert microscopy, but its sensitivity declined notably when qPCR served as the reference, revealing a substantial proportion of submicroscopic infections that the RDT failed to detect. qPCR identified the highest overall malaria prevalence and uncovered more cases of each species as well as mixed infections than either RDT or microscopy. The authors conclude that while the multi-antigen RDT is clinically useful for routine diagnosis, more sensitive tools are needed for malaria surveillance and control in endemic settings where low-parasite-density infections are common.
items.citation: Bogale A, Mitiku A, Tefera S et al.. Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.. Scientific reports. 2026
