items.title: Evolving Machine Learning in Non-Stationary Environments: A Unified Survey of Drift, Forgetting, and Adaptation
items.summary: This survey examines the challenges facing machine learning models deployed in dynamic, non-stationary environments where data distributions change over time. The authors propose evolving machine learning as a unifying paradigm that integrates four interrelated challenges—data drift, concept drift, catastrophic forgetting, and skewed learning—into a single coherent framework. They systematically reviewed a large body of recent studies, categorizing approaches across supervised, unsupervised, and semi-supervised learning settings. Beyond taxonomy, the survey synthesizes structural interdependencies among these challenges and foregrounds the fundamental tension between stability and adaptability in continuously updating systems. The work also reviews evaluation protocols, benchmark datasets, and real-world applications, identifying methodological limitations and open research directions for building robust, scalable adaptive learning systems.
items.citation: Ignacio Cabrera Martin, Subhaditya Mukherjee, Almas Baimagambetov et al.. Evolving Machine Learning in Non-Stationary Environments: A Unified Survey of Drift, Forgetting, and Adaptation. Applied Artificial Intelligence. 2026

items.title: Global trends in the burden of malaria: mapping the prevalence, incidence and mortality of Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax in the era of climate change and emerging drug resistance
items.summary: This review examined the global burden of malaria caused by the two predominant parasite species, synthesizing current epidemiological evidence on prevalence, incidence, and mortality. The paper assessed how climate change, emerging drug resistance, and vector adaptation are influencing geographic distribution and transmission dynamics. The review found that despite prior advances in malaria control, progress has stalled and resurgence has occurred in certain regions, driven by these compounding threats. The authors highlight key challenges facing elimination efforts and outline future directions for addressing them.
items.citation: Ebrahim Abbasi. Global trends in the burden of malaria: mapping the prevalence, incidence and mortality of Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax in the era of climate change and emerging drug resistance. BMJ Global Health. 2026

items.title: Harness-Aware Self-Evolving: Co-Evolving Model Weights, Harness, and Task Solutions
items.summary: This paper investigates whether the scaffolding or "harness" surrounding a self-evolving AI system — typically held fixed while only task solutions are optimized — can itself be improved during the learning process. The authors introduce Harness-Aware Self-Evolving (HASE), an agentic reinforcement-learning framework that allows a single model to both generate task solutions and edit selected harness components within a multi-turn action space. The approach is evaluated across diverse tasks including text classification, alpha factor mining, and circle-packing algorithm discovery. HASE enables a small model to match or exceed the performance of much larger models that rely on separate, more powerful systems to propose harness configurations. The findings demonstrate that jointly optimizing both the harness and the solution through a single unified agentic process yields substantial performance improvements over conventional fixed-harness self-evolving approaches.
items.citation: Haochen Luo, Yi Huang, Sichun Luo et al.. Harness-Aware Self-Evolving: Co-Evolving Model Weights, Harness, and Task Solutions. arXiv (Cornell University). 2026

items.title: The spatial proteome of the Plasmodium falciparum schizont illuminates the composition and evolutionary trajectories of its organelles
items.summary: This paper investigated the subcellular organization of proteins in *Plasmodium falciparum*, the parasite responsible for the majority of malaria deaths, during its invasive erythrocytic stage. Using a high-resolution spatial proteomics technique called hyperLOPIT combined with supervised machine learning, the researchers mapped the subcellular locations of thousands of parasite proteins expressed in late schizont stages. The analysis resolved a large number of distinct cellular compartments, including sites within the infected host red blood cell, and assigned confident localizations to a substantial proportion of the proteome that previously lacked known cellular context. By integrating comparative genomics, the study also traced evolutionary patterns that shaped organelle composition across *Plasmodium* species and illuminated adaptive pressures relevant to disease management. The resulting resource substantially advances understanding of parasite cell biology and the distinctive compartments underlying erythrocyte invasion and remodeling.
items.citation: Scott A. Chisholm, Victor Flores, Alison Kemp et al.. The spatial proteome of the Plasmodium falciparum schizont illuminates the composition and evolutionary trajectories of its organelles. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: SciCheck: A Framework for Verifying the Integrity of Deep Learning Training
items.summary: SciCheck is a framework designed to address the challenge of verifying the integrity of deep learning training within scientific workflows, where stochastic processes prevent simple recomputation from serving as a validity check. The framework allows scientists to freely explore training configurations and then commit a blueprint to a provenance ledger, after which a verifying scientist evaluates the run using two complementary layers: a statistical judge that compares per-step gradient statistics against a reference run, and a spot-check that re-executes randomly selected training segments whose checkpoints have been committed to the ledger. The system was tested against attacks including gradient sign flipping, label poisoning, and fully fabricated runs across three model architectures, achieving high detection accuracy while rejecting very few honest runs. The authors formally characterize the detection capabilities of each layer, showing that gradient statistics alone can catch sufficiently strong sign flips while being blind to fabricated runs that replay genuine statistics, whereas the spot-check provides probabilistic guarantees against fabricated segments that scale with the number of sampled segments. Verification costs roughly one to two times the expense of a single retraining, and the per-epoch commitment scheme substantially reduces checkpoint storage compared to retaining every checkpoint.
items.citation: Alexander Nguyen, Dylan Gresham, Gaby G. Dagher et al.. SciCheck: A Framework for Verifying the Integrity of Deep Learning Training. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Scenario Orchestration for Closed-loop Policy Evaluation of Autonomous Driving
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental challenge in autonomous driving evaluation: when a scripted scenario with fixed actor routes and speeds is tested in closed loop, the ego vehicle's responses can invalidate the intended interaction, making evaluation unreliable. The authors propose a scenario orchestrator that continuously monitors the joint traffic state and dynamically adapts non-ego actors through re-timing, re-routing, and role reassignment to preserve a specific scenario intent throughout execution. At each timestep, the system solves a constrained optimization problem that balances maintaining the intended interaction against limiting interventions and preserving traffic feasibility. The approach also separates scenario realization from policy failure, enabling testers to first verify that the intended interaction actually occurred before judging how the ego policy responded to it. Experiments in the CARLA simulator demonstrate that orchestration more reliably produces targeted interactions compared to scripted and learned actor baselines, particularly when initial conditions or ego behavior vary, supporting its use as a tool for controlled and reproducible policy evaluation.
items.citation: Frieda Rong, Zhaoyue Wang, Veer Kapadia et al.. Scenario Orchestration for Closed-loop Policy Evaluation of Autonomous Driving. arXiv. 2026

items.title: PhotoFinish: Portable Timerless Probing of Microarchitectural Latencies
items.summary: This paper investigates whether microarchitectural timing attacks can be carried out without access to explicit high-resolution timers, which are a common defensive target in security-conscious environments like web browsers. The authors developed PhotoFinish, a portable timerless probing primitive that races an operation under test against a reference operation in two parallel threads writing distinct values to a shared memory location, converting latency differences directly into an architectural outcome rather than a timestamp. The technique requires only parallel execution and shared memory, making it broadly applicable across diverse hardware. Testing across dozens of CPUs spanning multiple instruction set architectures, as well as in WebAssembly running inside browsers, the primitive reliably classified cache states and was successfully applied to attacks including AES T-table leakage, Evict+Reload, TLB probing, and last-level cache slice identification. The work demonstrates that restricting timers is insufficient as a defense, since shared-memory races can serve as a precise and portable substitute for explicit timing measurements.
items.citation: Tristan Hornetz, Eduard Ebert, Lorenz Hetterich et al.. PhotoFinish: Portable Timerless Probing of Microarchitectural Latencies. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper investigates the reliability of majority-vote pseudo-labels used in test-time reinforcement learning, where pretrained language models are adapted to unlabeled target-domain data using self-generated supervision signals. The authors analyze the error structure of majority-vote supervision in the context of online Direct Preference Optimization, decomposing it into a population-majority bias component and a prompt-dependent finite-rollout variation component. Because population-majority bias cannot be corrected without external supervision, the authors focus on mitigating finite-rollout variation by proposing Prompt-Conditional Distributionally Robust DPO, which applies conservative updates to prompts where vote reliability is low. They additionally introduce a cache-based mechanism to reduce forgetting during online adaptation. Evaluated across a broad set of mathematical and knowledge-intensive reasoning benchmarks and multiple model backbones, the proposed method matches or outperforms the strongest baseline in the large majority of experimental settings.
items.citation: Haoyu Wang, Ru Wang, Yuanyuan Wang et al.. On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: An Empirical Study on Clustering-based Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm for Regression Test Case Selection
items.summary: The paper investigates the application of a quantum computing approach to the regression test case selection problem, where the goal is to identify an optimal subset of tests to run after software modifications without executing the entire test suite. The authors extended their previously proposed clustering-based Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm for test case selection, called QAOA-TCS, by conducting a thorough empirical evaluation against both classical methods and other quantum approaches. They assessed its performance across single-objective and multi-objective problem formulations and examined its robustness under varying levels of quantum noise using realistic noisy simulators. In multi-objective settings, QAOA-TCS outperformed state-of-the-art competing approaches in most cases and remained stable even at high noise levels, while in single-objective settings it performed comparably to other quantum methods. The analysis also revealed trade-offs in computational efficiency, with a prior quantum annealing method proving most efficient for large multi-objective problems, while QAOA-TCS offered the best effectiveness-efficiency balance in the single-objective case, though comparisons were complicated by differing computational environments across methods.
items.citation: Antonio Trovato, Martin Beseda, Dario Di Nucci. An Empirical Study on Clustering-based Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm for Regression Test Case Selection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Geometric Pairwise Classification of Affine Constraints over Ellipsoidal Regions
items.summary: The paper develops a deterministic geometric method for classifying affine constraints defined over fixed ellipsoidal regions, motivated by problems in chance-constrained optimization and set approximation. Individual inequalities are categorized as always violated, never violated, or cutting with respect to the ellipsoid, while pairwise tests determine whether two inequalities can be simultaneously and strictly violated at a common point, producing a compatibility matrix. These classifications are derived through quadratic optimization and Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions, with careful handling of special cases such as tangencies, parallel normals, and degenerate constraints. The framework is formulated for arbitrary finite dimensions and is intended to supply geometric information useful for bounding probabilities of simultaneous constraint violations and for approximating safe feasible regions.
items.citation: Igor M. L. Pataro, Martina Mammarella, Fabrizio Dabbene et al.. Geometric Pairwise Classification of Affine Constraints over Ellipsoidal Regions. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic performance and testing costs of pooled testing for molecular detection of tuberculosis in seven countries: a prospective, observational, diagnostic accuracy study.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether pooling multiple sputum specimens together for a single molecular test could expand tuberculosis diagnostic capacity without requiring additional laboratory infrastructure. Conducted prospectively across seven countries spanning multiple continents, the research enrolled individuals with presumptive tuberculosis from both facility-based and community-based settings, testing sputum individually and in pools of up to four specimens using the Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra platform, with culture serving as the reference standard. Pooled testing demonstrated slightly higher specificity than individual testing but a modest reduction in sensitivity, with positive agreement between pooled and individual results remaining high for specimens with medium to high bacterial loads but falling substantially for trace-level results. Critically, pooling reduced cartridge consumption by approximately half compared to individual testing, suggesting substantial cost and resource savings. The authors conclude that pooled tuberculosis testing could meaningfully expand access to molecular diagnostics in low to moderate prevalence settings without requiring new infrastructure investment.
items.citation: Garg T, Sander M, Byrne RL et al.. Diagnostic performance and testing costs of pooled testing for molecular detection of tuberculosis in seven countries: a prospective, observational, diagnostic accuracy study.. The Lancet. Global health. 2027

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviews advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research over a five-year period, synthesizing evidence that has informed updated WHO policy guidance consolidating recommendations for disease detection and drug-resistance testing into a single framework. Key developments include the expanded role of digital chest radiography with computer-aided detection as a frontline screening tool, and the diversification of decentralised molecular diagnostics through low-complexity automated and manual nucleic acid amplification tests deployed across a wider range of specimen types, including non-sputum samples such as stool, gastric aspirate, and tongue swabs that improve diagnosis in children and other populations unable to produce sputum. Rapid molecular drug-resistance testing has advanced, and targeted next-generation sequencing has gained WHO endorsement for comprehensive drug-susceptibility testing at reference laboratory level, while urine lipoarabinomannan assays provide diagnostic benefit primarily in people with HIV and advanced disease. Host blood transcriptomic signatures demonstrate promising prognostic and triage performance, and multiple other biomarker classes are progressing through clinical evaluation, yet none has met WHO target product profile criteria for a point-of-care test capable of reliably distinguishing infection from disease, including subclinical tuberculosis. The paper concludes that substantial gaps in diagnostic performance, implementation, and equity persist and identifies these as priorities for further development.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: Microfluidic Profiling of an Immune Cell-Associated Extracellular Vesicle Signature for Active Tuberculosis Diagnosis and Treatment Monitoring.
items.summary: This paper investigated whether extracellular vesicles carrying innate immune cell surface proteins could serve as diagnostic biomarkers for active tuberculosis, addressing the limitations of conventional pathogen detection methods that often fail in paucibacillary cases. Using whole-blood transcriptome profiling, the researchers identified four innate immune cell-associated surface markers and developed a tuberculosis-associated immune cell extracellular vesicle signature, which was then implemented on an eight-channel microfluidic chip capable of analyzing a small volume of plasma within thirty minutes. The platform was validated in a clinical cohort including patients with active tuberculosis, healthy controls, and patients with other respiratory diseases, achieving high discriminatory performance as measured by area under the curve values in both comparisons. The approach also provided complementary diagnostic information in patients who tested negative on individual conventional tests and demonstrated utility for treatment monitoring, as biomarker levels declined following anti-tuberculosis therapy. Overall, the study presents tuberculosis-associated immune cell extracellular vesicle profiling via microfluidics as a rapid and minimally invasive strategy for both diagnosing active tuberculosis and tracking treatment response.
items.citation: Lee EJ, Nie C, Park S et al.. Microfluidic Profiling of an Immune Cell-Associated Extracellular Vesicle Signature for Active Tuberculosis Diagnosis and Treatment Monitoring.. Journal of extracellular vesicles. 2026

items.title: Diagnosis of Extrapulmonary Tuberculosis at the Interface of Pathogen Detection and Host Response: Molecular, Microbiological, and Histopathological Advances.
items.summary: This review examines the persistent diagnostic challenges posed by extrapulmonary tuberculosis, which disproportionately affects children and immunocompromised individuals and is complicated by low pathogen burden, anatomically diverse affected sites, and nonspecific clinical presentations. The authors synthesized evidence across microbiological, molecular, sequencing-based, and histopathological diagnostic approaches, integrating these within the context of site-specific immunopathology including granuloma biology and caseous necrosis. Comparative evidence was drawn from multiple disease sites—including osteoarticular, lymph node, pleural, central nervous system, and disseminated forms—evaluating tools such as Xpert MTB/RIF and Ultra, targeted and metagenomic next-generation sequencing, host-response biomarkers, and artificial intelligence-assisted histopathology. The review proposes tiered diagnostic algorithms suited to resource-limited settings where most cases occur, and identifies gaps in current international guidance. The authors conclude that aligning diagnostic modality selection with anatomical site, specimen quality, pathological subtype, and available laboratory capacity has the potential to shorten time to diagnosis and support host-directed diagnostic strategies.
items.citation: Liu Q, Jiang Y. Diagnosis of Extrapulmonary Tuberculosis at the Interface of Pathogen Detection and Host Response: Molecular, Microbiological, and Histopathological Advances.. Pathogens (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.
items.summary: This narrative review examined how the diagnosis of tuberculosis in people with HIV has evolved from 1990 to the present, addressing the particular challenges posed by lower bacillary loads in sputum, high rates of extrapulmonary disease, and the nonspecific clinical presentation that overlaps with other opportunistic infections. The authors traced the historical reliance on smear microscopy as the sole rapid diagnostic tool, noting its reduced sensitivity in people with HIV and the poor accuracy of algorithms used to diagnose smear-negative cases, which led to both underdiagnosis and overdiagnosis with serious consequences for patient outcomes. The introduction of nucleic acid amplification tests and the urine lipoarabinomannan lateral flow assay, alongside the widespread use of antiretroviral therapy, has substantially transformed the diagnostic landscape and contributed to reductions in tuberculosis incidence and mortality. Nevertheless, the review concludes that no currently available rapid test achieves ideal sensitivity, and only urine lipoarabinomannan detection combines affordability with point-of-care suitability, leaving a clear need for further development of accurate, affordable, and simple diagnostic tools.
items.venue: South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde
items.citation: Maartens G. The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.. South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde. 2026

items.title: Flooding spread of manipulated knowledge in LLM-based multi-agent communities
items.summary: This paper investigates security vulnerabilities in large language model-based multi-agent systems, specifically focusing on how manipulated knowledge can spread through communities of communicating agents. The researchers designed a two-stage attack methodology combining Persuasiveness Injection and Manipulated Knowledge Injection, which causes agents to propagate both counterfactual and toxic knowledge without requiring explicit adversarial prompts and without noticeably degrading the agents' core capabilities. Through extensive experiments, they demonstrated that these manipulations can persist within retrieval-augmented generation frameworks, where benign agents inadvertently store and later retrieve corrupted information from chat histories. To counter these threats, the authors proposed two defense strategies involving system prompts that encourage critical verification of shared knowledge and the incorporation of supervisory agents to oversee interactions, both of which were shown to meaningfully reduce the rate at which manipulated knowledge spreads. The work calls attention to the urgent need for multi-agent platforms to adopt targeted, cost-effective defenses against this class of knowledge-manipulation attacks.
items.citation: Tianjie Ju, Yiting Wang, Yi Hua et al.. Flooding spread of manipulated knowledge in LLM-based multi-agent communities. Science China Information Sciences. 2026

items.title: Efficient differential expression analysis of large-scale single-cell transcriptomics data using Dreamlet
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of performing differential expression analysis on large-scale single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomics datasets spanning hundreds of subjects and millions of cells. The authors developed an open-source R package called dreamlet, which employs a pseudobulk approach based on precision-weighted linear mixed models to identify cell-cluster-specific genes associated with traits across subjects. The method is designed to handle complex statistical models while controlling false positive rates, and it achieves substantially faster runtimes and lower memory usage compared to existing workflows. The authors validated dreamlet's computational and statistical performance on published datasets and demonstrated its capabilities on a large novel dataset of over a million single nuclei from postmortem brain tissue of Alzheimer's disease cases and controls. The work establishes dreamlet as a scalable and statistically rigorous tool for disease-focused single-cell transcriptomics studies conducted in large cohorts.
items.citation: Gabriel E. Hoffman, Donghoon Lee, Jaroslav M. Bendl et al.. Efficient differential expression analysis of large-scale single-cell transcriptomics data using Dreamlet. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: AI-induced never-skilling in medical education
items.citation: Yuhe Ke, Liyuan Jin, Jasmine Chiat Ling Ong et al.. AI-induced never-skilling in medical education. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks
items.summary: This paper investigated whether internalized reasoning models and externalized agent-based frameworks represent competing or complementary approaches to complex medical question answering. The authors developed MedicalAgentsBench, a curated benchmark of challenging clinical questions drawn from eight medical datasets using difficulty-aware filtering and contamination screening. They systematically evaluated a range of internalized reasoning models, standard base models, and externalized multi-agent scaffolding methods across this benchmark. Their key finding is that the two approaches are complementary rather than mutually exclusive: each independently improves performance, and combining agent workflows with an internalized reasoning model yields the highest accuracy overall. Pareto analysis further demonstrated that this combined approach dominates the cost-performance frontier, while lightweight optimization of less expensive models provides a viable path for resource-constrained settings.
items.citation: Yanjun Shao, Xiangru Tang, Jiwoong Sohn et al.. MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks. Patterns. 2026

items.title: AutoResearchClaw: Self-Reinforcing Autonomous Research with Human-AI Collaboration
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of automating scientific discovery by arguing that existing autonomous research systems fail to capture the iterative, failure-informed nature of real research because they rely on linear pipelines and single-agent reasoning. The authors developed AutoResearchClaw, a multi-agent pipeline incorporating structured debate for hypothesis generation, a self-healing execution loop that treats failures as information, mechanisms to prevent hallucinated results, flexible human-in-the-loop collaboration, and cross-run learning that converts past errors into future safeguards. The system was evaluated on a benchmark spanning multiple research topics, where it substantially outperformed a competing autonomous research system. A key finding from ablation studies is that targeted human intervention at high-leverage decision points consistently outperforms both full autonomy and exhaustive step-by-step oversight, suggesting an optimal middle ground for human-AI collaboration in scientific research. The authors frame AutoResearchClaw as a research amplifier designed to augment rather than replace human scientific judgment.
items.citation: Jiaqi Liu, Shi Qiu, Mairui Li et al.. AutoResearchClaw: Self-Reinforcing Autonomous Research with Human-AI Collaboration. arXiv (Cornell University). 2026

items.summary: The paper addresses the problem of verifying the integrity of deep learning training within scientific workflows, where stochastic processes and flexible configurations make simple recomputation an inadequate check. The authors developed SciCheck, a framework combining a provenance ledger with two verification layers: a statistical judge that compares per-step gradient statistics between a submitted run and a verifier's reference run, and a spot-check that re-executes randomly sampled training segments whose checkpoints were committed epoch by epoch. The system was evaluated against adversarial conditions including gradient sign flipping, label poisoning, and fully fabricated runs across multiple neural network architectures, achieving high detection accuracy with low false positive rates. The analysis reveals that the two layers have complementary strengths: gradient statistics can detect sufficiently severe sign flips following a theoretically characterized relationship, while fabricated runs that replay genuine statistics evade statistical detectors but are reliably caught by the spot-check, whose detection probability follows a tractable formula enabling principled selection of sample size. items.title: Scenario Orchestration for Closed-loop Policy Evaluation of Autonomous Driving
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental challenge in autonomous driving evaluation: when a scripted test scenario is executed in closed-loop simulation, the ego vehicle's responses can invalidate the intended interactions that the scenario was designed to test. The authors introduce a scenario orchestrator that continuously monitors the full traffic state and dynamically adapts non-ego actors through re-timing, re-routing, and role reassignment to preserve a desired scenario intent as the ego policy unfolds. At each simulation step, the system solves a constrained optimization problem that balances fidelity to the intended interaction against traffic feasibility and minimizing unnecessary intervention. The framework also separates the question of whether a scenario was successfully realized from whether the ego policy succeeded or failed within it, enabling cleaner attribution of test outcomes. Experiments in the CARLA simulator demonstrate that this orchestration approach produces targeted interactions more reliably than fixed scripted or learned actor baselines, particularly when initial conditions or ego behavior vary, supporting its use as a tool for controlled and reproducible policy evaluation.

items.title: Interventions to Improve Care for Bacterial Sexually Transmitted Infections in Emergency Departments: A Narrative Review.
items.summary: This narrative review examined interventions designed to improve the diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up care for bacterial sexually transmitted infections — specifically chlamydia, gonorrhea, and syphilis — within emergency department settings in the United States. The authors searched the published literature spanning several decades and identified studies evaluating a range of approaches, including universal screening protocols, electronic health record prompts, point-of-care testing, and patient-directed tools. Universal screening substantially increased testing rates and case detection, electronic prompts enhanced screening uptake, and point-of-care testing enabled same-day diagnosis and treatment while reducing unnecessary antibiotic use. Bundled interventions that addressed multiple steps in the care pathway showed the greatest overall impact, though heterogeneity among interventions made direct comparisons challenging. The authors conclude that future research should prioritize implementation feasibility, sustainability, health equity, and cost-effectiveness across diverse emergency department contexts.
items.citation: Andonian KS, Giri H, Goodman GR et al.. Interventions to Improve Care for Bacterial Sexually Transmitted Infections in Emergency Departments: A Narrative Review.. Sexually transmitted diseases. 2026

items.title: Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).
items.summary: This pilot study examined the utility of point-of-care testing for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis among men who have sex with men attending a non-governmental organisation-led clinic near Beirut, Lebanon, while also assessing their sexual health knowledge, attitudes, and practices. Using a cross-sectional design over four months, researchers conducted sexual health consultations, administered STI and HIV tests, and gathered data through anonymous questionnaires covering demographics, risk behaviours, chemsex, sexual violence, and perceived stigma. The cohort was predominantly young, educated Lebanese men, with a notable proportion living with HIV, and participants generally demonstrated high awareness of STIs and HIV despite engaging in condomless sex and recreational drug use. HIV-related stigma and community perceptions emerged as significant barriers to seeking testing. The findings suggest that integrating point-of-care testing into sexual health services for this population enables same-day diagnosis, immediate counselling, and timely linkage to confirmatory testing and care.
items.citation: Abou Shahla W, Rossoni I, Padovese V. Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Point-of-care screening for curable sexually transmitted infections in antenatal care in Zimbabwe: a costing study.
items.summary: This study estimated the costs of integrating point-of-care screening for three curable sexually transmitted infections into antenatal care in Zimbabwe, where such infections are associated with adverse birth outcomes but cost data are scarce. Researchers implemented screening at two primary healthcare clinics in Harare, collecting economic costs through staff interviews, time-and-motion studies, and other sources, then modelled implementation in a low-volume routine care setting over a twelve-month period. The analysis compared point-of-care testing against a modelled syndromic management standard of care to calculate incremental costs per person screened and treated. The study found a substantial composite prevalence of the three infections among pregnant women, with test kits and personnel representing the dominant cost drivers of the intervention. The authors conclude that reductions in point-of-care diagnostic costs will be essential to making such screening strategies financially viable within health systems like Zimbabwe's.
items.citation: Martin K, Bath D, Nyamwanza R et al.. Point-of-care screening for curable sexually transmitted infections in antenatal care in Zimbabwe: a costing study.. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Mean-Field Limit of Non-exchangeable Multi-agent Systems Over Hypergraphs with Unbounded Rank
items.summary: This paper studies the large-population (mean-field) limit of multi-agent systems in which interactions are not restricted to pairs of agents but instead occur among arbitrarily sized groups, a setting described mathematically by hypergraphs. The authors consider dense, nonuniform hypergraphs whose interaction rank is allowed to grow without bound, generalizing previous work that assumed binary or fixed-order interactions. By combining tools from PDE analysis, stochastic analysis, kinetic theory, and graph limit theory, they derive a rigorous mean-field limit for such systems under sufficient regularity of the interaction kernels. The limiting object is a Vlasov-type equation in which the hypergraph structure is encoded by a novel construct called a UR-hypergraphon (unbounded-rank hypergraphon), and the resulting mean-field force incorporates infinitely many orders of interaction simultaneously. This constitutes the first derivation of a mean-field limit for multi-agent systems on hypergraphs of unbounded rank, extending the theoretical foundation for modeling higher-order collective phenomena.
items.citation: Nathalie Ayi, Nastassia Pouradier Duteil, David Poyato. Mean-Field Limit of Non-exchangeable Multi-agent Systems Over Hypergraphs with Unbounded Rank. Journal of Nonlinear Science. 2026

items.title: Flatline constructs : Gothic materialism and cybernetic theory-fiction
items.summary: This thesis examines the claim that cyberpunk fiction is the supreme literary expression of postmodernism or late capitalism, using three interlocking theoretical frameworks: cybernetics, the Gothic, and fiction. The work argues that postmodernism has been preoccupied with cybernetic themes while cybernetics has itself been haunted by the Gothic, and draws on Deleuze-Guattari's materialist reworking of the Gothic — derived from Worringer's concept of nonorganic continuum rather than conventional literary sources — to analyse key cyberpunk texts including Blade Runner, Videodrome, Neuromancer, and The Atrocity Exhibition. By placing Baudrillard's theories of simulation and hyperreality in dialogue with these fictional texts, the thesis investigates Baudrillard's claim that the era of cybernetic simulation effectively dissolves both science fiction and theory as distinct genres. The central organising concept is the "flatline," drawn from Gibson, which denotes simultaneously a state of unlife or undeath and a condition of radical immanence, serving as the convergence point where cyberpunk merges cybernetics with the Gothic through its preoccupations with catatonic trance, bodies that exceed their own boundaries, and agency without subjectivity. The thesis proceeds through four chapters, each examining the flatline in relation to cybernetics and postmodernism, the body, reproduction, and fiction itself respectively.
items.venue: Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick)
items.citation: Mark Fisher. Flatline constructs : Gothic materialism and cybernetic theory-fiction. Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick). 2026

items.title: INSPECT-SR tool for assessing trustworthiness of randomised controlled trials
items.summary: This paper addresses the threat that problematic randomised controlled trials pose to evidence synthesis, where flawed or fraudulent trials can distort the conclusions of systematic reviews and clinical guidelines. The authors developed INSPECT-SR, a tool designed to assess the trustworthiness of randomised controlled trials by helping reviewers identify trials with serious concerns arising from either research misconduct or honest critical errors. The development process and the resulting tool, along with an accompanying guidance document, are described and presented. The intended purpose is to enable systematic reviewers to detect and exclude problematic trials, thereby safeguarding the integrity of evidence synthesis.
items.citation: Jack Wilkinson, Calvin Heal, Ella Flemyng et al.. INSPECT-SR tool for assessing trustworthiness of randomised controlled trials. BMJ. 2026

items.title: Addressing benchmarking gaps in large language models for health and medicine with dynamic red-teaming
items.summary: This paper investigated whether large language models used in health and medical contexts are truly safe and reliable, arguing that conventional static benchmarks are insufficient for evaluating their real-world performance. The researchers developed a Dynamic, Automatic and Systematic red-teaming framework that uses adversarial agents to continuously and autonomously probe models across four safety-critical dimensions: robustness, privacy, bias, and hallucination. Applying this framework to a set of state-of-the-art language models revealed a stark "benchmarking gap," whereby models that performed well on standard static medical question-answering benchmarks failed dramatically under dynamic adversarial conditions, with the vast majority of previously correct answers breaking down under robustness testing. High failure rates were observed across all four safety axes, including widespread privacy leakage, bias-driven shifts in clinical recommendations, and frequent hallucinations, suggesting that strong static benchmark scores may reflect superficial pattern memorization rather than genuine medical reasoning. The authors propose their framework as a scalable, living audit system for surfacing latent risks in health-focused language models before they are deployed in consumer or clinical settings.
items.citation: Jiazhen Pan, Bailiang Jian, Paul Hager et al.. Addressing benchmarking gaps in large language models for health and medicine with dynamic red-teaming. Nature Health. 2026

items.title: The many behind the few : the lives and emotions of Erks and WAAFs of RAF bomber command 1939-1945
items.summary: This thesis examines the experiences of ground personnel — both men and women — who served in Royal Air Force Bomber Command during the Second World War, a group that constituted the large majority of the service yet has been largely overlooked in favour of aircrew and strategic bombing histories. The research investigates how a gendered hierarchy of trades was constructed within Bomber Command through interlocking discourses of class, gender, fear, heroism, and stoicism, as well as distinctive features of RAF culture such as trade selection, dialect, pay scales, and perceptions of each trade's contribution to the bombing mission. Drawing on the lived experiences of these personnel, the thesis explores how the hierarchy shaped feelings of fulfilment or inadequacy, with some ground staff overburdened while others felt they were failing to contribute meaningfully to the war effort. It also addresses the emotional dimensions of serving on operational stations amid high aircrew loss rates, including the RAF medical services' responses to psychological breakdowns among ground personnel. By situating non-combatant military personnel at the intersection of the front line and the home front, the thesis contributes to histories of the RAF, military medicine and psychiatry, the emotional experience of war, and wartime work and citizenship.
items.venue: Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick)

items.title: APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update
items.summary: These guidelines address the ongoing burden of chronic hepatitis B infection in the Asia Pacific region, where the disease continues to drive significant morbidity and mortality through complications such as acute-on-chronic liver failure, end-stage cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma despite decades of scientific progress. To develop the guidelines, the Asia Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver convened a Viral Elimination Taskforce comprising key opinion leaders from across its member countries and regions, who incorporated evolving epidemiological trends, socioeconomic factors, and technological advances into their deliberations. The resulting clinical practice guidelines span thirteen major areas encompassing screening, vaccination, antiviral treatment, and hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance, with the aim of providing practical and cost-effective recommendations for healthcare professionals, policy-makers, and patients. The overarching goal of the guidelines is to support efforts toward eliminating the disease burden of chronic hepatitis B across the Asia Pacific region.
items.citation: Hong You, Rakhi Maiwall, Jing Chen et al.. APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update. Hepatology International. 2026

items.title: SciCheck: A Framework for Verifying the Integrity of Deep Learning Training
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of verifying the integrity of deep learning training within scientific workflows, where stochastic processes and flexible configurations make simple recomputation infeasible as a check. The authors developed SciCheck, a framework in which researchers commit training blueprints to a provenance ledger and a verifier evaluates runs using two complementary layers: a statistical judge that compares per-step gradient statistics against a reference run, and a spot-check that re-executes randomly sampled training segments whose checkpoints were committed incrementally. The system was evaluated on multiple neural network architectures against adversarial scenarios including gradient sign flipping, label poisoning, and fully fabricated runs. SciCheck achieved high detection performance across all tested architectures and attack types, with the spot-check mechanism contributing most of the detection accuracy, while the statistical layer specifically targets gradient manipulation of sufficient severity according to a derived theoretical relationship. The framework operates at a computational overhead of roughly one to two times the cost of a single retraining, with efficient checkpoint storage, and provides verifiers with a principled way to choose the number of spot-check segments based on a desired soundness guarantee.

items.title: Scenario Orchestration for Closed-loop Policy Evaluation of Autonomous Driving
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental challenge in autonomous driving evaluation: when a scripted test scenario is run in closed loop, the ego vehicle's responses can invalidate the intended interactions, making the scenario fail to test what was designed. Experiments in the CARLA simulator demonstrate that orchestration more reliably produces the targeted interactions compared to scripted and learned actor baselines, especially under varying initial conditions and diverse ego policies, supporting its use as a tool for controlled and reproducible policy evaluation.

items.title: Clinical utility of nucleic acid amplification testing for detection of sexually transmitted infections in women with symptomatic bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis identified by conventional versus molecular diagnoses.
items.summary: This study examined whether molecular nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT) for bacterial vaginosis (BV) and vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC) improves the detection of co-occurring sexually transmitted infections compared to conventional diagnostic methods. The researchers analyzed data from over a thousand women with symptomatic vaginitis, comparing STI detection rates across three diagnostic approaches: clinician clinical assessment, conventional laboratory methods, and molecular NAAT-based vaginitis diagnosis. Women who tested positive for BV by NAAT had significantly higher rates of co-occurring STIs and a markedly elevated relative risk for STI detection compared to those diagnosed by conventional methods or clinician assessment alone. The association between VVC NAAT positivity and STI co-infection showed a similar trend, though it did not reach statistical significance. The authors conclude that an all-molecular, combined testing strategy for vaginitis and STIs using a single vaginal specimen improves diagnostic yield, supports better risk stratification, and streamlines clinical workflows compared to traditional approaches.

Journal of clinical microbiology. 2026

items.title: Pre-exposure prophylaxis adherence and risks of HIV and sexually transmitted infection among adult men before vs during the COVID-19 pandemic.
items.summary: This study examined how the COVID-19 pandemic affected pre-exposure prophylaxis adherence and HIV and sexually transmitted infection outcomes among adult men newly starting PrEP. Using a retrospective cohort design with commercial insurance claims data, researchers applied trajectory modeling to characterize adherence patterns among those who initiated PrEP before versus during the pandemic, then used weighted survival and regression models to compare clinical outcomes. Men who began PrEP during the pandemic showed markedly worse adherence patterns, with early discontinuation being the most common trajectory compared to consistently high adherence being most common in the pre-pandemic group. Initiating PrEP during the pandemic was associated with a significantly higher risk of HIV acquisition, while rates of sexually transmitted infections did not differ meaningfully between the two groups. The findings highlight the disruption that public health emergencies can cause to HIV prevention continuity and underscore the need for targeted strategies to maintain PrEP access and adherence during such crises.
items.venue: Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy
items.citation: Unigwe IF, Jenjai C, Goodin AJ et al.. Pre-exposure prophylaxis adherence and risks of HIV and sexually transmitted infection among adult men before vs during the COVID-19 pandemic.. Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy. 2026

items.title: DNA-guided CRISPR–Cas12 for cellular RNA targeting
items.summary: This paper introduces ΨDNA, a DNA-based guide molecule that reprograms Cas12 nucleases to target RNA rather than DNA, circumventing the conventional requirement for RNA-based guide systems. The researchers engineered ΨDNA to mimic a CRISPR RNA scaffold in reverse orientation, enabling two Cas12 variants to recognize RNA targets and activate downstream cleavage activity. This approach was applied to sensitive RNA diagnostics, achieving fully accurate detection of hepatitis C virus RNA in clinical samples, as well as multiplex knockdown of endogenous RNA transcripts in human cell lines through ribosome stalling. Mechanistic analysis revealed that a stem-loop structure within ΨDNA is critical for stabilizing a catalytically active Cas12-ΨDNA-RNA complex. Beyond knockdown and diagnostics, the system was extended through modular enzyme fusions to enable simultaneous DNA editing and RNA knockdown, RNase H-mediated RNA degradation, and epitranscriptomic editing, establishing ΨDNA as a versatile platform for programmable transcriptome manipulation.
items.citation: Carlos Orosco, Boyu Huang, Santosh R. Rananaware et al.. DNA-guided CRISPR–Cas12 for cellular RNA targeting. Nature Biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Next-generation CRISPR-based molecular diagnostics for veterinary parasitology: From laboratory innovation to one health surveillance.
items.summary: This review examines the application of CRISPR-based diagnostic technologies to the detection of veterinary parasites, motivated by the limitations of conventional methods such as microscopy, serology, and culture techniques, which are often slow, insufficiently sensitive, and reliant on specialized facilities. The authors critically survey how different CRISPR-Cas systems, specifically Cas12, Cas13, and emerging Cas14 variants, have been adapted to detect protozoan, helminthic, and arthropod-borne parasites in livestock, companion animals, and wildlife. The review describes how these platforms are being integrated with isothermal amplification, lateral flow assays, fluorescence detection, and portable biosensors to create rapid, field-deployable diagnostic tools aligned with One Health surveillance goals. Persistent challenges are identified, including assay standardization, multiplex detection capability, sample preparation complexity, and the regulatory and commercial hurdles required for practical deployment. The authors also outline future directions, including amplification-free CRISPR assays and artificial intelligence-assisted interpretation, positioning these technologies as transformative tools for veterinary parasite surveillance and disease control.
items.citation: Basit A, Hanif M. Next-generation CRISPR-based molecular diagnostics for veterinary parasitology: From laboratory innovation to one health surveillance.. Molecular and biochemical parasitology. 2026

items.title: Scaffold RNA Reengineering for a Leakage-Suppressed CRISPR/Cas12a Cascade System Toward Precise Nucleic Acid Diagnostics.
items.summary: This paper addressed the challenge of high background signal (leakage) in amplification-free CRISPR-based nucleic acid detection, which limits sensitivity and precision. The researchers engineered the CRISPR-Cas12a guide RNA by extending its scaffold RNA with a DNA segment at the 3' end, introducing steric hindrance that keeps the system in an inhibited state until a target nucleic acid triggers allosteric activation. This conformational switch redesigns the guide RNA as a threshold-controlled molecular switch, shifting Cas12a activity from suppressed to precisely activated only upon target recognition, thereby preventing the self-activation that typically causes uncontrolled background in cascaded CRISPR systems. The resulting cascade system, termed CALCas, achieved femtomolar detection sensitivity and was demonstrated for rapid detection of HPV16/18 within under thirty minutes without nucleic acid amplification. The authors argue that this approach of reprogramming Cas12a enzymatic activity through guide RNA engineering offers a broadly applicable strategy for precise quantitative nucleic acid diagnostics.
items.citation: Li X, Hu H, Jiang X et al.. Scaffold RNA Reengineering for a Leakage-Suppressed CRISPR/Cas12a Cascade System Toward Precise Nucleic Acid Diagnostics.. Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany). 2026

items.title: Point-of-care testing in the diagnosis of infectious diseases.
items.summary: This review examines point-of-care testing as a diagnostic strategy for infectious diseases, motivated by the growing global burden of such diseases and the escalating threat of antimicrobial resistance. The authors surveyed the core technical platforms underlying current point-of-care approaches, including lateral flow assays, chemiluminescence immunoassays, isothermal amplification, CRISPR-based diagnostics, and microfluidic chip technologies, and described their application across a range of clinical infection types spanning the respiratory, bloodstream, gastrointestinal, urinary, and sexually transmitted categories. The review assessed both the advantages of these tools—namely rapid detection, portability, and accessibility—and their limitations regarding sensitivity, quality control, cost, and integration into clinical workflows. The authors conclude that ongoing advances in nanomaterials, microfluidic engineering, artificial intelligence, and industry standardization are driving improvements in performance and integration, positioning point-of-care testing as a future core tool for precision clinical management and public health epidemic control.
items.citation: Fang Q, Lin Y, Hu G et al.. Point-of-care testing in the diagnosis of infectious diseases.. Frontiers in microbiology. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies with artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and clinical translation. The authors synthesize how genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic approaches generate deep molecular insights into disease mechanisms, while deep learning architectures are applied to decode these complex datasets and build predictive models. The review covers the application of this combined framework across the drug development pipeline, including target identification, drug repositioning, de novo compound design, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. Disease areas explored include oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions, illustrating the broad therapeutic potential of these converging technologies. The authors also identify persistent challenges such as harmonizing disparate omics data, ensuring reproducibility, and addressing algorithmic biases, while arguing that the fusion of multiomics and artificial intelligence opens new pathways for data-driven therapeutic innovation.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Cuproptosis-immunity crosstalk informs strategy to overcome immunotherapy resistance
items.summary: This paper investigated the relationship between cuproptosis, a copper-dependent form of cell death mediated by ferredoxin 1, and antitumor immune responses. The researchers found that CD8+ T cell-mediated immunity increases tumor cell susceptibility to cuproptosis, while cuproptotic tumor cells reciprocally stimulate immunity by releasing damage-associated molecular patterns that activate dendritic cells. Mechanistically, interferon-γ secreted by CD8+ T cells was shown to upregulate ferredoxin 1 expression in tumor cells through a specific signaling axis, thereby sensitizing those cells to cuproptosis. Building on this bidirectional crosstalk, the authors demonstrated that combining a cuproptosis inducer with anti-PD-L1 therapy produced enhanced tumor suppression and overcame immunotherapy resistance in multiple preclinical models. The findings establish cuproptosis as a form of immunogenic cell death and propose targeting this pathway as a strategy to counteract resistance to checkpoint immunotherapy.
items.citation: Guang Lei, Zhengze Lu, Zhihao Xu et al.. Cuproptosis-immunity crosstalk informs strategy to overcome immunotherapy resistance. Cell. 2026

items.title: Influence of protein aggregates, extracellular vesicles, and lipoprotein fusion on ionizable lipid nanoparticles protein corona analysis
items.summary: This paper examines the protein corona that forms around ionizable lipid nanoparticles used in nucleic acid therapeutics, with particular focus on how the corona influences organ targeting. The authors argue that achieving delivery beyond the liver is hindered by apolipoprotein adsorption, which drives hepatic uptake, and that understanding the true corona composition is therefore critical for engineering tissue-specific delivery. A central problem identified is that blood-borne contaminants, including extracellular vesicles, lipoproteins, and protein aggregates, co-isolate with lipid nanoparticles during analysis and obscure the genuine corona. The paper proposes that the protein corona on these soft lipid materials is fundamentally different in character from that observed on rigid inorganic nanoparticles, being more fluid and dynamic in nature. The authors advocate for refined, tailored proteomic strategies capable of distinguishing true corona proteins from co-isolated impurities to better guide the rational design of organ-selective lipid nanoparticles.
items.citation: Babak Borhan, Amanda M. Murray, Amir Ata Saei et al.. Influence of protein aggregates, extracellular vesicles, and lipoprotein fusion on ionizable lipid nanoparticles protein corona analysis. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: MXene quantum dot polymer nanocomposites as smart platforms for targeted drug delivery and multifunctional biomedical applications: an updated review
items.summary: This review examines MXene quantum dot polymer nanocomposites and their potential as multifunctional platforms for targeted drug delivery and broader biomedical applications. The paper synthesizes current knowledge on how MXenes and their composites leverage exceptional electrical conductivity, flexibility, and biocompatibility to enable smart microrobots capable of precise navigation and targeted therapeutic release, particularly in cancer treatment. The integration of quantum dots into polymer nanocomposites is highlighted as a strategy to merge electrical, optical, and catalytic properties, expanding utility across drug delivery, tissue engineering, flexible electronics, and energy storage. Stimuli-responsive polymers embedded within these systems allow controlled activation of therapeutic agents, and the composites can co-deliver multiple drugs to achieve synergistic treatment effects. The review also acknowledges persistent challenges including scalable production, long-term stability, and regulatory hurdles that must be addressed before widespread clinical translation can be achieved.
items.citation: Mohammad Hossein Karami, Omid Moini Jazani. MXene quantum dot polymer nanocomposites as smart platforms for targeted drug delivery and multifunctional biomedical applications: an updated review. Discover Nano. 2026

items.title: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation
items.summary: This paper introduces Video-Coder, a system designed to address persistent challenges in video generation related to precise spatial structure, coherent motion dynamics, and controllable scene composition. The approach trains a code-driven agent that autonomously writes and executes code to construct dynamic three-dimensional scenes, which then serve as structural and motion guidance for downstream video generation models. To support this, the authors built a dedicated data pipeline with curated datasets, an interactive execution environment for agent training, and a training scheme combining supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning that uses dual rewards drawn from both code execution feedback and video quality assessment. An annealing strategy gradually shifts the model's reliance from execution-based to video-based rewards over the course of training. The resulting system demonstrates substantial improvements on established benchmarks for physical plausibility and video quality, and the authors fully open-source their data, models, and code.
items.citation: Chaoyang Wang, Sicheng Gao, Junan Hu et al.. Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: SciCheck: A Framework for Verifying the Integrity of Deep Learning Training
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of verifying the integrity of deep learning training within scientific workflows, where non-determinism and flexible experimental design make traditional recomputation-based verification impossible. The authors developed SciCheck, a framework in which researchers commit training blueprints to a provenance ledger and verification proceeds through two complementary layers: a statistical judge that compares per-step gradient statistics against a reference run, and a spot-check mechanism that re-executes randomly sampled training segments whose checkpoints were committed incrementally. The framework was evaluated against attacks including gradient sign flipping, label poisoning, and fully fabricated runs across three neural network architectures of varying complexity. SciCheck achieved high integrity-detection performance while maintaining low false rejection rates for honest runs, with the spot-check layer carrying most of the discriminative power and the statistical layer catching sufficiently severe gradient manipulations. The authors also provide theoretical characterizations of detection probability and show that the approach requires only modest computational overhead relative to a single retraining, while substantially reducing checkpoint storage demands.
items.citation: Alexander Nguyen, Dylan Gresham, Gaby G. Dagher et al.. SciCheck: A Framework for Verifying the Integrity of Deep Learning Training. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Scenario Orchestration for Closed-loop Policy Evaluation of Autonomous Driving
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental challenge in autonomous driving evaluation: when a scripted scenario with predetermined actor routes and speeds is tested in closed loop, the ego vehicle's responses can invalidate the intended interactions, making the evaluation unreliable. The authors introduce a scenario orchestrator that continuously monitors the joint traffic state and dynamically adapts non-ego actors through re-timing, re-routing, and role reassignment to preserve a specific scenario intent throughout execution. At each timestep, the system solves a constrained optimization problem that balances maintaining the intended interaction against minimizing interventions and ensuring traffic feasibility. The approach also separates the question of whether a scenario was successfully realized from the question of how the ego policy performed within it, enabling more principled evaluation. Experiments in the CARLA simulator demonstrate that orchestration more reliably produces targeted interactions compared to scripted and learned actor baselines, especially when initial conditions or ego behavior vary, supporting its use as a tool for controlled and reproducible policy evaluation.
items.citation: Frieda Rong, Zhaoyue Wang, Veer Kapadia et al.. Scenario Orchestration for Closed-loop Policy Evaluation of Autonomous Driving. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Locating Contact on Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots From Tendon Measurements Alone via Constrained Moving Horizon Estimation
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of detecting and localizing contact along tendon-driven continuum robots using only tendon tension measurements at the motors. The authors first establish that contact localization is fundamentally impossible without additional constraints, demonstrating that the mapping from contact forces to tendon measurements has a null space large enough to prevent any unconstrained estimator from locating contact. When the obstacle geometry is known, however, non-penetration and complementarity conditions render the contact force locally identifiable, and the authors prove local exponential strong detectability of the resulting system. They develop a constrained moving horizon estimator that encodes these physical contact conditions and solves as a single quadratic program per time step, accompanied by a local robust stability guarantee. In benchmark simulations of a robot pressing and sliding against a wall, the proposed estimator dramatically outperformed a tuned extended Kalman filter in both contact location and force estimation accuracy, and maintained this advantage under randomized model mismatches including unmodeled tendon friction, while offering no benefit over the Kalman filter in contact-free scenarios, confirming that the gains arise specifically from the contact constraints.
items.citation: Haitham El-Hussieny. Locating Contact on Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots From Tendon Measurements Alone via Constrained Moving Horizon Estimation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Novikov-Magnus Master Equation for Driven Quantum Systems under Classical Correlated Noise
items.summary: This paper introduces a theoretical framework for deriving time-local quantum master equations describing driven quantum systems coupled to temporally correlated classical noise. The approach combines the Donsker-Furutsu-Novikov functional response relation with the Magnus expansion, allowing the noise average to be systematically closed while preserving the noncommuting, time-ordered structure of noise-induced perturbations along the controlled quantum trajectory. For zero-mean Gaussian noise, the resulting Novikov-Magnus master equation is derived through fourth order in the noise strength, and the framework is extended conceptually to non-Gaussian noise by incorporating connected higher-order noise correlations via higher functional derivatives. Applied to a driven qubit subject to Ornstein-Uhlenbeck and band-limited one-over-frequency noise, the second- and fourth-order equations maintain completely positive and trace-preserving character throughout the perturbative regime and accurately reproduce stochastic simulations. The accuracy of this approach, as measured by diamond-norm error, is comparable to that of the cumulant-based pseudo-Lindblad master equation, with a modest improvement at fourth order for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise.
items.citation: Nada Khogeer, Jerison Parra, Caroline Desgranges et al.. Novikov-Magnus Master Equation for Driven Quantum Systems under Classical Correlated Noise. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper investigates the reliability of majority-vote pseudo-labels used in test-time reinforcement learning, where pretrained language models are adapted to unlabeled target-domain data using self-generated supervision signals. The authors analyze the error structure of majority-vote supervision within an online Direct Preference Optimization framework, decomposing it into a population-majority bias component and a prompt-dependent finite-rollout variation component. Because population-majority bias cannot be corrected without external supervision, they focus on mitigating finite-rollout variation by proposing Prompt-Conditional Distributionally Robust DPO, which makes updates from sampling-sensitive prompts more conservative based on observed vote reliability. They also introduce a cache-based mechanism to reduce forgetting that occurs during online self-supervised adaptation. Evaluated across a broad set of mathematical and knowledge-intensive reasoning benchmarks and multiple model backbones, their approach matches or outperforms the strongest existing test-time reinforcement learning baseline in the large majority of experimental settings.
items.citation: Haoyu Wang, Ru Wang, Yuanyuan Wang et al.. On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Multiplexed Nucleic Acid Detection Using Sequence-Specific Cleavage Mediated by Repair Endonucleases.
items.summary: This paper introduces TIMBER, a non-CRISPR nucleic acid detection platform that uses repair endonucleases to cleave abasic-site-containing probes only when hybridized to a matched target sequence, thereby avoiding the nonspecific collateral cleavage that complicates CRISPR-based diagnostic systems. The approach achieves single-nucleotide polymorphism discrimination and can detect targets at attomolar concentrations when paired with preamplification methods such as RT-PCR or RT-LAMP, with results readable by fluorescence or lateral flow. The researchers validated the platform by detecting SARS-CoV-2 in clinical saliva samples and demonstrated simultaneous multiplexed detection of four distinct targets. They further applied TIMBER to identify cancer-relevant mutations, specifically EGFR variants in lung cancer samples, illustrating its versatility across infectious disease and oncology applications. The authors argue that this flexible, low-instrument-requirement system offers a practical alternative to existing diagnostic platforms for point-of-care and precision medicine settings.
items.citation: Garden PM, Li Y, Murugan V et al.. Multiplexed Nucleic Acid Detection Using Sequence-Specific Cleavage Mediated by Repair Endonucleases.. ACS sensors. 2026
