items.title: Beyond blood: a narrative review of advancements in saliva-based diagnostics.
items.summary: This narrative review examines the potential of human whole saliva as a noninvasive diagnostic biofluid capable of reflecting systemic and oral health, positioning it as an alternative to conventional blood-based testing. The authors surveyed salivary biomarkers across a broad range of clinical domains, including metabolic, cardiovascular, infectious, oncological, and neurodegenerative conditions, while also evaluating analytical technologies from immunoassays and mass spectrometry to wearable electrochemical biosensors. The review distinguishes between diagnostics that have already received regulatory clearance and those still in discovery phases. Despite promising advances, the authors identify persistent barriers to mainstream clinical adoption, including unstandardized collection protocols, interference from the oral matrix, and the absence of validated normative reference intervals. They conclude that translation into routine diagnostics will require universal sampling standardization, matrix-matched biosensor engineering capable of sub-picomolar detection, and large multicenter prospective trials to establish clinical cutoffs and validate blood-saliva correlation dynamics.
items.citation: Mondal S, Das Sharma A, Mandal SK et al.. Beyond blood: a narrative review of advancements in saliva-based diagnostics.. Expert review of molecular diagnostics. 2026

items.title: Consented Universal Newborn Screening for Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection Using Dried Blood Spot and Dried Saliva Spot Specimens: Implementation and Relative Programmatic Accuracy.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy and practical implementation of two specimen types — dried blood spots and dried saliva spots — for universal newborn screening of congenital cytomegalovirus infection. Using a prospective paired-sample design across multiple birthing centers, researchers applied quantitative PCR assays to both specimen types from tens of thousands of consecutive newborns, with confirmatory urine testing offered to those screening positive. Dried saliva spots did not significantly improve sensitivity for detecting congenital cytomegalovirus compared to dried blood spots, while producing a substantially higher false positive rate, with each additional true case identified by saliva but not blood accompanied by multiple false positives. Saliva-based screening also extended turnaround times, frequently failing to return results within the window required to offer confirmatory diagnostic testing that can distinguish congenital from postnatal infection. Based on this performance profile, the authors concluded that dried saliva spot screening did not support population-wide implementation within their program.
items.citation: Santander E, Reuvers E, Lacaria M et al.. Consented Universal Newborn Screening for Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection Using Dried Blood Spot and Dried Saliva Spot Specimens: Implementation and Relative Programmatic Accuracy.. International journal of neonatal screening. 2026

items.title: Vitamin D<sub>3</sub> oral rinsing reduces salivary SARS-CoV-2 antigen detectability: a clinical trial with public health implications.
items.summary: This clinical trial investigated whether rinsing the mouth with a Vitamin D₃ solution could affect the accuracy of saliva-based rapid antigen tests for SARS-CoV-2. Adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection provided paired saliva samples immediately before and after a one-minute Vitamin D₃ oral rinse, with samples analyzed by both rapid antigen test and rapid RT-PCR under blinded conditions. The rinse converted the majority of antigen-positive samples to antigen-negative results, substantially reducing antigen test positivity, while RT-PCR positivity and viral RNA levels remained largely unchanged. This discordance between antigen and molecular results indicates that the oral rinse interfered specifically with antigen detection rather than reducing actual viral load. The findings identify Vitamin D₃ oral rinsing as a pre-analytical variable that could compromise the reliability of saliva-based rapid antigen testing, with implications for infectious disease screening and public health surveillance.
items.citation: Feteih SMN, Heaphy ELG, Aljagthmi A et al.. Vitamin D<sub>3</sub> oral rinsing reduces salivary SARS-CoV-2 antigen detectability: a clinical trial with public health implications.. Frontiers in oral health. 2026

items.title: Sample-to-answer automated centrifugal microfluidics with computer-vision readout for point-of-care molecular diagnostics
items.summary: This paper addressed the need for decentralized, automated molecular diagnostic tools that became critically apparent during the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly in resource-limited settings where centralized laboratory infrastructure is strained. The researchers developed a fully automated centrifugal microfluidic platform that integrates loop-mediated isothermal amplification with a computer-vision-based optical readout system, capable of running a complete sample-to-answer assay at the press of a single button without user intervention. The platform was demonstrated using SARS-CoV-2 detection as a model application, processing multiple samples in a single run within approximately forty minutes. Testing with RNA fragments spiked into water and artificial saliva showed consistent detection down to a low copy number per reaction volume. The authors propose that this platform architecture is broadly generalizable and could serve as a template for rapid, point-of-care molecular diagnostics in future infectious disease outbreaks.
items.citation: Akhtar AS, Lapins N, Moura JM et al.. Sample-to-answer automated centrifugal microfluidics with computer-vision readout for point-of-care molecular diagnostics. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Molecular Testing on Saliva and Oral Swabs for Pulmonary Tuberculosis.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether molecular testing on saliva and oral swabs could serve as accurate, non-sputum alternatives for diagnosing pulmonary tuberculosis. Using a nested case-control design within a prospective cohort of adults and children at primary care centers in Colombia, the researchers tested paired saliva and nylon-flocked oral swab samples using Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra, comparing results against sputum liquid mycobacterial culture as the reference standard. Saliva demonstrated higher sensitivity than oral swabs, with saliva surpassing the World Health Organization's minimum sensitivity target for a low-complexity non-sputum diagnostic test, while both specimen types showed high specificity for culture-confirmed pulmonary tuberculosis. Participant acceptability of both collection methods was also high. The findings support saliva in particular as a promising non-sputum specimen type that could help close gaps in tuberculosis detection.
items.venue: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
items.citation: Vargas DA, Fuertes-Bucheli JF, Sanchez-Hidalgo A et al.. Diagnostic Accuracy of Molecular Testing on Saliva and Oral Swabs for Pulmonary Tuberculosis.. Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America. 2026

items.title: Andes virus outbreak linked to expedition cruise ship travel, multi-country investigation and response, April to June 2026
items.summary: The abstract describes an ongoing outbreak investigation of Andes orthohantavirus linked to an expedition cruise ship, involving cases among passengers and crew of multiple nationalities. Investigators conducted coordinated international contact tracing, medical evacuations, repatriations, and clinical and laboratory follow-up across affected countries. The outbreak resulted in confirmed and probable cases with a notable case fatality rate, affecting both passenger and crew populations aboard the vessel. The source of the outbreak and specific risk factors had not yet been fully determined at the time of reporting, with monitoring continuing to prevent further spread. The abstract is sufficiently detailed to summarize the event, though it reflects an active and still-evolving investigation.
items.citation: Oda E. van den Berg, UKHSA ANDV Team, Ettore Severi et al.. Andes virus outbreak linked to expedition cruise ship travel, multi-country investigation and response, April to June 2026. Eurosurveillance. 2026

items.title: Human infection with Andes hantavirus: an update for the general physician
items.summary: Andes virus (ANDV) is a hantavirus with the unusual capacity for sustained human-to-human transmission via respiratory droplets and close contact, distinguishing it from other orthohantaviruses that spread only from infected rodents to humans. This review synthesizes current knowledge of ANDV infection for general physicians, covering its transmission dynamics, clinical spectrum, and management. The most severe manifestation, hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, is characterized by acute respiratory failure, hemodynamic instability, kidney injury, hepatic involvement, and dysregulated cytokine release, with disease severity linked to specific hematological and biochemical markers. No approved antiviral treatment or vaccine exists, leaving supportive care as the only intervention, and case fatality rates remain high. A recent cruise ship outbreak involving passengers of multiple nationalities illustrates how ANDV can achieve rapid international spread in the era of mass travel, highlighting the need for clinician awareness, contact tracing, and coordinated global outbreak preparedness.
items.citation: Emanuele Durante‐Mangoni, Iolanda Cafarella, Silvia Mercadante et al.. Human infection with Andes hantavirus: an update for the general physician. European Journal of Internal Medicine. 2026

items.title: Extracellular vesicle biomarkers: current status and future perspectives as novel tools in liquid biopsy
items.summary: This review examines the emerging role of extracellular vesicles as a source of biomarkers for liquid biopsy in human disease. Because these nano-sized vesicles are shed by living cells into body fluids and carry proteins, nucleic acids, and lipids that reflect the state of their parent cells, they represent a potentially powerful window into physiological and pathological processes. The authors systematically survey biomarker discovery and application of extracellular vesicles across cancer, neurological disorders, and cardiovascular diseases, while critically analyzing technical bottlenecks in vesicle isolation, characterization, and detection. They also address ongoing challenges surrounding standardization and clinical translation of these approaches. The review concludes by highlighting future directions, including multi-omics integration, and the potential of extracellular vesicle-based tools for early diagnosis, real-time treatment monitoring, and prognostic evaluation.
items.citation: Wenlong Huang, Ming Zhao, Ling Li et al.. Extracellular vesicle biomarkers: current status and future perspectives as novel tools in liquid biopsy. Frontiers in Immunology. 2026

items.title: Hantavirus: A Comprehensive Contemporary Review of Virology, Global Epidemiology, Clinical Variants, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Intensive Care Management
items.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive narrative review of hantaviruses, negative-sense RNA viruses responsible for two serious zoonotic syndromes: hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome. The authors conducted a systematic literature search across major medical and public health databases spanning several decades to synthesize current knowledge on taxonomy, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical features, diagnosis, treatment, and intensive care management. The review identifies over fifty recognized hantavirus species divided broadly into Old World and New World categories, with distinct geographic distributions and causative agents, notably highlighting that the Andes virus is unique in its capacity for person-to-person transmission. Diagnostically, the paper outlines a time-dependent approach using molecular and serological methods, while therapeutically it notes that ribavirin shows benefit in hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome but no antiviral is definitively proven for the cardiopulmonary syndrome, and that extracorporeal membrane oxygenation has meaningfully improved survival in severe cases. The authors conclude that clinical vigilance, prompt diagnosis, evidence-based intensive care, and rodent control remain the essential pillars of managing hantavirus disease, while emerging therapies such as favipiravir and monoclonal antibodies continue under investigation.
items.venue: Indian Journal of Critical Care Medicine
items.citation: Anoop Kumar AS, Joshua John. Hantavirus: A Comprehensive Contemporary Review of Virology, Global Epidemiology, Clinical Variants, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Intensive Care Management. Indian Journal of Critical Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness
items.summary: This review examines hantaviruses, rodent-borne pathogens responsible for hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, in the context of a rapidly changing global environment. The authors synthesize current knowledge spanning virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical presentation, diagnostics, and prevention, with particular attention to how climate change, urbanization, and land-use transformation drive shifts in rodent reservoir dynamics and increase spillover risk to humans. The review highlights significant surveillance and diagnostic gaps in tropical and Caribbean regions where hantavirus transmission may be substantially underrecognized. Advances in molecular diagnostics, genomic surveillance, vaccine candidates, monoclonal antibody therapies, and climate-informed early warning systems are discussed as promising tools for improving outbreak detection and response. The authors argue that integrated One Health frameworks combining human, animal, and environmental monitoring, alongside strengthened laboratory capacity and regional collaboration, are essential for reducing the global burden of hantavirus disease and enhancing preparedness for future zoonotic threats.
items.citation: Maria E. Ramos‐Niño, Nicolette Chiem, Prakash V. A. K. Ramdass. Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in terahertz-based bound states in the continuum metasurfaces for 6G communications and MedTech
items.summary: This review examines the development of bound states in the continuum metasurfaces operating in the terahertz frequency range, with a focus on their potential for sixth-generation wireless communications and medical technology applications. The authors survey a decade of research progress, tracing the field from early symmetry-protected designs through to application-optimized quasi-bound states in the continuum, while covering the underlying physics including multipolar origins, topological robustness, and symmetry-breaking mechanisms that enable high quality-factor resonances. Key milestones highlighted include the development of dielectric metasurfaces with high quality factors, flexible biosensors capable of microgram-level detection, and gas spectrometers that dramatically reduce required optical path lengths. The review also evaluates emerging directions such as reconfigurable bound states in the continuum and chiral quantum photonics, while candidly identifying persistent barriers to practical deployment including nanofabrication tolerances, material loss trade-offs, and limitations in dynamic control. The authors conclude that terahertz bound-state-in-the-continuum metasurfaces represent critical enabling technologies for compact, high-efficiency systems bridging fundamental photonics research and the commercialization of terahertz-based platforms.
items.citation: Islam I. Abdulaal, A. Elsayed, Omar A. M. Abdelraouf. Recent advances in terahertz-based bound states in the continuum metasurfaces for 6G communications and MedTech. Journal of Optics. 2026

items.title: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation
items.summary: This paper addresses persistent challenges in video generation—namely precise spatial structure, coherent motion dynamics, and controllable scene composition—by introducing a code-driven agentic approach. The authors developed Video-Coder, a system that trains an agent to autonomously write and execute code to construct dynamic three-dimensional scenes that serve as structural and motion guidance for downstream video generation models. To support this, they curated two dedicated datasets, built a unified interactive environment for agent training and inference that integrates code execution and scene rendering, and trained the agent using supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning with dual rewards combining execution-based and video-based feedback. An annealing strategy was also employed to shift the model's reliance from execution rewards toward video quality rewards over the course of training. The resulting system achieves substantial improvements on established benchmarks for physical plausibility and video quality, demonstrating that agentic code-driven scene construction is a viable and effective paradigm for controllable video generation.

items.title: SciCheck: A Framework for Verifying the Integrity of Deep Learning Training
items.summary: SciCheck addresses the challenge of verifying the integrity of deep learning training within scientific workflows, where non-determinism and flexible configurations make simple recomputation infeasible as a check. The framework allows scientists to record training blueprints on a provenance ledger and employs a two-layer verification approach: a statistical judge that compares gradient statistics between a submitted run and a verifier's reference run, and a spot-check that re-executes randomly selected training segments whose checkpoints have been cryptographically committed. Testing across multiple neural network architectures and against attacks including gradient sign flipping, label poisoning, and fully fabricated runs, the framework achieves high integrity detection with very low false rejection of honest runs. The analysis reveals that the spot-check layer carries most of the detection power, particularly for fabricated runs that can mimic genuine gradient statistics and thus evade purely statistical detectors, while gradient statistics alone suffice for strong enough sign-flip attacks. Verification overhead is modest relative to a single retraining, checkpoint storage is substantially reduced compared to saving every checkpoint, and the framework provides verifiers with a principled way to choose the number of spot-check samples to meet a desired soundness guarantee.
items.citation: Alexander Nguyen, Dylan Gresham, Gaby G. Dagher et al.. SciCheck: A Framework for Verifying the Integrity of Deep Learning Training. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Scenario Orchestration for Closed-loop Policy Evaluation of Autonomous Driving
items.summary: This paper addresses a core challenge in autonomous driving evaluation: when a scripted simulation scenario is tested in closed loop, the ego vehicle's responses can invalidate the intended interaction, making assessment unreliable. At each step, the system solves a constrained optimization problem that balances fidelity to the intended interaction against traffic feasibility and intervention minimality. The approach also formally separates whether the intended scenario was realized from whether the ego policy succeeded or failed within that scenario, enabling cleaner evaluation logic. Experiments in the CARLA simulator demonstrate that the orchestrator more reliably produces targeted interactions across diverse scenario families and driving policies than scripted or learned actor baselines, especially under varying initial conditions and ego behaviors.

items.title: PhotoFinish: Portable Timerless Probing of Microarchitectural Latencies
items.summary: This paper investigates timerless probing primitives as a means of measuring microarchitectural latencies without relying on explicit high-resolution timers, which are commonly restricted as a defense against side-channel attacks. The authors developed PhotoFinish, a portable primitive that races an operation under test against a fixed reference across two parallel threads writing unique values to a shared memory location, converting latency differences directly into an architectural value using only parallel execution and shared memory. The approach was evaluated across a broad range of processors spanning multiple instruction set architectures, as well as in browser-based WebAssembly environments, demonstrating reliable cache state classification across diverse microarchitectures. Beyond cache timing, PhotoFinish was shown to be applicable to TLB and execution-engine latencies, and was used to conduct AES T-table and Evict+Reload attacks, as well as to identify last-level cache slice membership. The findings demonstrate that shared-memory races constitute a generic and precise substitute for explicit timing measurements, undermining the assumption that restricting timer access alone is sufficient to prevent fine-grained microarchitectural side-channel observations.
items.citation: Tristan Hornetz, Eduard Ebert, Lorenz Hetterich et al.. PhotoFinish: Portable Timerless Probing of Microarchitectural Latencies. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis
items.summary: This review examines the relationship between gut microbial-derived metabolites and kidney disease, including acute kidney injury, chronic kidney disease, diabetic kidney disease, and immune-mediated nephropathies. The authors synthesize current evidence showing that kidney injury disrupts intestinal barrier function and gut microbial balance, leading to reduced production of beneficial short-chain fatty acids while promoting accumulation of harmful uremic toxins such as indoxyl sulfate and trimethylamine-N-oxide. These metabolites exert their effects on renal tissue through multiple signaling pathways, with tryptophan metabolites identified as particularly important mediators of gut-kidney communication. The review maps the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms linking microbial metabolite dysregulation to renal fibrosis and disease progression. The authors also evaluate therapeutic strategies targeting the gut microbiota, including natural products, prebiotics, probiotics, and renal replacement therapy, as potential avenues for more precise treatment of kidney disease.
items.citation: Wan-Ying Zhang, Yu-Lu Zhang, Qing-Qing Yu et al.. Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis. International Journal of Biological Sciences. 2026

items.title: Editor's Choice – European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) 2026 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
items.summary: These guidelines from the European Society for Vascular Surgery address the clinical management of vascular graft and endograft infections, updating a previous version to reflect current evidence. The guidelines were developed by synthesising the best available scientific evidence and supplementing it with expert opinion, with recommendations graded by both strength and level of evidence. A substantial set of recommendations was produced covering definitions, diagnosis, multidisciplinary team management, antimicrobial therapy, management of both intracavity and extracavity infections, and follow-up care. The guidelines also incorporate shared decision-making principles and patient-facing information, as well as a discussion of unresolved issues in the field. The stated aim is to provide comprehensive, up-to-date guidance to clinicians and patients on managing this serious complication of vascular surgery.
items.venue: European Journal of Vascular and Endovascular Surgery
items.citation: Anne Lejay, Ben R. Saleem, Tara D. Barwick et al.. Editor's Choice – European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) 2026 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections. European Journal of Vascular and Endovascular Surgery. 2026

items.title: Antimicrobial-laden PerOssal beads display in vitro inhibition and killing of extensively drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria associated with conflict wounds in Ukraine
items.summary: This study investigated the potential of locally delivered antimicrobials to combat extensively drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria commonly found in conflict-related open fractures, particularly wounds sustained in Ukraine. The researchers tested antimicrobial-laden PerOssal hydroxyapatite and calcium sulphate beads—an established local drug delivery system for bone and joint infections—against clinical bacterial isolates using zone-of-inhibition testing and time-kill analysis. The bacterial isolates from Ukraine were resistant to multiple standard antimicrobials, rendering systemic prophylaxis potentially ineffective, and beads loaded with single agents such as gentamicin, tobramycin, or cefazolin showed only weak inhibitory activity. However, the combination of gentamicin and rifampicin achieved consistent broad-spectrum inhibition and bacterial killing, and co-amoxiclav-loaded beads also inhibited all tested strains. The authors conclude that local antimicrobial delivery via these beads holds promise for reducing infection risk in heavily contaminated open fractures when surgical wound excision is delayed, though in vivo validation is still required.
items.citation: Henry Adam Claireaux, Edward J. A. Douglas, Scott J C Pallett et al.. Antimicrobial-laden PerOssal beads display in vitro inhibition and killing of extensively drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria associated with conflict wounds in Ukraine. Bone and Joint Research. 2026

items.title: Gut Microbial Metabotypes Shape Polyphenol Bioactivity: Toward Precision Nutrition Strategies for Human Health
items.summary: This review examines how gut microbiota transform dietary polyphenols into biologically active metabolites and how differences between individuals in this capacity shape the health effects of polyphenol-rich diets. Because many polyphenols reach the colon largely unabsorbed, resident microorganisms convert them into smaller molecules such as urolithins, equol, and enterolignans, which may have distinct biological activities compared to their parent compounds. The paper introduces the concept of microbial metabotypes, which classify individuals by their ability to produce specific microbially derived metabolites, and critically evaluates the evidence linking these metabolites to outcomes including mitochondrial function, endothelial homeostasis, inflammation, and gut-brain communication, distinguishing human from preclinical evidence. The authors find that while urolithin, equol, and enterolignan metabotypes are relatively well characterized, translation of metabotype-guided approaches into clinical practice is hindered by inconsistent challenge protocols, unstandardized analytical thresholds, incomplete population validation, and limited long-term intervention data. They conclude that microbial metabotypes currently hold greater promise as research tools for stratifying participants in nutritional trials than as established frameworks for personalized dietary prescription.
items.citation: Pasquale Perrone, Stefania D’Angelo. Gut Microbial Metabotypes Shape Polyphenol Bioactivity: Toward Precision Nutrition Strategies for Human Health. Nutrients. 2026

items.title: ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
items.summary: This paper presents updated clinical guidelines from a major European gastroenterology organization on preventing, diagnosing, and managing infections in patients with inflammatory bowel disease. The guidelines were developed in response to the rapid expansion of immunosuppressive and biologic therapies used to treat Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, including newer small molecules and advanced biologics, each carrying distinct infection risk profiles. The document addresses opportunistic and other clinically significant infections — viral, bacterial, mycobacterial, and vaccine-preventable — that disproportionately affect immunocompromised patients. Building on prior consensus statements and a previous guideline, this update incorporates the most recent evidence on risk stratification and vaccination strategies tailored to the contemporary treatment landscape. The overarching aim is to provide clinicians with a structured, evidence-based framework for infection management that reflects the evolving complexity of IBD therapeutics.
items.venue: Journal of Crohn s and Colitis
items.citation: Henit A. Yanai, Pierre Ellul, Bram Verstockt et al.. ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease. Journal of Crohn s and Colitis. 2026

items.title: The Gut–Vagina Axis
items.summary: This review paper examines the emerging concept of the gut–vagina axis, focusing on how interactions between the gut and vaginal microbiomes may influence female health. The authors synthesize recent advances in microbiome research to explore the mechanisms underlying this relationship, including microbial migration between sites, hormonal and immune regulation, and metabolite exchange. They argue that communication between gut and vaginal microbial communities is bidirectional, with each site capable of influencing the microbial composition, immune responses, and metabolic activity of the other. The review highlights the potential implications of this axis for both local and systemic health outcomes in women.
items.citation: Lorenzo Agoni, Elena Roselletti, Giovanni Marasco et al.. The Gut–Vagina Axis. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Challenges for minimal warm inflation in the Standard Model and beyond
items.summary: The paper examines whether warm inflation can be minimally realised using the Standard Model, focusing on a scenario where the inflaton couples to gauge fields through an effective operator involving the gauge field strength and its dual. The authors demonstrate that Standard Model solutions face two fundamental problems: the energy released per sphaleron transition greatly exceeds the plasma temperature, undermining the plasma calculation, and the effective operator description itself breaks down. When the inflaton is embedded as the Goldstone boson of a renormalizable Peccei-Quinn theory, the required anomaly coefficient is so large that it drives QCD to a Landau pole, rendering the construction theoretically inconsistent. The authors find that these tensions can be alleviated by instead coupling the inflaton to a more strongly coupled dark gauge sector beyond the Standard Model.
items.citation: Anish Ghoshal, Alessandro Strumia. Challenges for minimal warm inflation in the Standard Model and beyond. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
items.summary: This paper investigates whether generalist AI models can serve as effective robot manipulation controllers, an approach the authors term agentic manipulation policies (AMPs), wherein a generalist model directly commands a manipulator and adapts its actions as tasks unfold. The authors developed a reference implementation called AMP1, designed to operate without modification across single-arm, bimanual, and mobile manipulation platforms, requiring no task-specific demonstrations or training. AMP1 was evaluated on multiple benchmarks and real-world trials spanning diverse tasks and robot configurations, where it substantially outperformed leading specialist approaches such as vision-language-action models and world-action models. Beyond following prescribed strategies, the agent autonomously developed its own manipulation behaviors—including searching for hidden objects, repurposing objects as tools, and self-calibrating cameras—and when augmented with a persistent memory store, it could improve further from accumulated experience across episodes. The authors conclude that agentic manipulation policies offer substantially greater generality and robustness than specialist manipulation policies, representing a promising direction for the field.
items.citation: Chen Chen, Omid Bagherieh, Naveen Nikamanth Appiah Balaji et al.. On Agentic Manipulation Policies. arXiv. 2026

items.title: SciCheck: A Framework for Verifying the Integrity of Deep Learning Training
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of verifying the integrity of deep learning training within scientific workflows, where non-determinism and flexible experimental design make traditional recomputation-based checks infeasible. The authors developed SciCheck, a framework in which researchers commit training blueprints to a provenance ledger and verification proceeds through two complementary layers: a statistical model comparing gradient statistics between the submitted run and a reference run, and a spot-check that re-executes randomly selected training segments anchored by committed checkpoints. The system was evaluated on multiple neural network architectures under adversarial conditions including gradient sign flipping, label poisoning, and fully fabricated runs, achieving high integrity detection while maintaining low false rejection rates for honest runs. The authors characterize the theoretical detection guarantees of each layer, showing that gradient statistics alone can catch sufficiently severe sign flips while being blind to fabricated runs that replay genuine statistics, and that the spot-check provides probabilistic soundness guarantees that scale predictably with the number of sampled segments. Overall, SciCheck achieves strong verification performance at a computational cost of roughly one to two times a single retraining, with efficient checkpoint storage through per-epoch commitments.
items.citation: Alexander Nguyen, Dylan Gresham, Gaby G. Dagher et al.. SciCheck: A Framework for Verifying the Integrity of Deep Learning Training. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Scenario Orchestration for Closed-loop Policy Evaluation of Autonomous Driving
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental challenge in autonomous driving evaluation: when a scripted scenario with fixed actor routes and speeds is tested in closed-loop simulation, the ego vehicle's responses can invalidate the intended interaction, making evaluation unreliable. The authors propose a scenario orchestrator that continuously monitors the joint traffic state and dynamically adapts non-ego actors through re-timing, re-routing, and role reassignment to preserve a specified scenario intent throughout execution. At each step, the system solves a constrained optimization problem that balances maintaining the intended interaction against limiting unnecessary interventions and ensuring traffic feasibility. The framework also separates the question of whether the intended scenario was successfully realized from the question of how well the ego policy performed, enabling cleaner evaluation logic. Experiments in the CARLA simulator demonstrate that this orchestration approach more reliably realizes targeted interactions compared to scripted and learned actor baselines, particularly when initial conditions or ego behavior vary, supporting its use as a tool for controlled and reproducible policy evaluation.
items.citation: Frieda Rong, Zhaoyue Wang, Veer Kapadia et al.. Scenario Orchestration for Closed-loop Policy Evaluation of Autonomous Driving. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Directed systems of A-spaces and weak cores
items.summary: The paper investigates a minimality property for weak homotopy equivalences defined on regular CW-complexes, drawing an analogy with Stong's classical theory of cores for finite topological spaces. The authors prove that for any regular CW-complex there exists a quotient map to an Alexandroff space — a topological space in which arbitrary intersections of open sets remain open — that is a weak homotopy equivalence and is minimal in the sense that any further quotient preserving weak equivalence must already be a homeomorphism. This minimal quotient is called the weak core of the space, and the paper establishes that it need not be unique in general. The authors also study which homotopy invariants are preserved under filtered colimits of Alexandroff spaces, developing a framework that extends finite topological space techniques to a broader setting.
items.citation: Jonathan Ariel Barmak, Juan Galotto. Directed systems of A-spaces and weak cores. arXiv. 2026

items.title: VLT and Keck recovery and characterisation of 2025 SC$_{79}$: linking 'Ayló'chaxnim and Atira asteroids
items.summary: The paper studied the asteroid 2025 SC₇₉, which orbits near the dynamical boundary between the Atira and 'Ayló'chaxnim asteroid classes, a region that is challenging to observe due to small solar elongations. The researchers recovered the object using two major telescopes, measuring its optical colors across four filters and combining these measurements with taxonomic comparisons, source region probability models, and large-scale orbital integrations of thousands of clonal trajectories spanning millions of years in both temporal directions. The optical colors most closely match a V-type taxonomic classification, and when combined with source region modeling, strongly favor an origin in the inner Main Belt. Dynamical integrations reveal that the asteroid's orbital clones transition repeatedly between the 'Ayló'chaxnim and Atira populations over hundred-thousand-year timescales, demonstrating a direct dynamical link between these two near-Sun asteroid classes. Forward integrations also show that a substantial fraction of clones ultimately collide with Venus or Mercury, tracing the eventual fate of objects in this orbital regime.
items.citation: Bryce T. Bolin, Leo Y. Alcorn, Davide Farnocchia et al.. VLT and Keck recovery and characterisation of 2025 SC$_{79}$: linking 'Ayló'chaxnim and Atira asteroids. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Revisiting the use of adenosine deaminase in cerebrospinal fluid analysis for infectious meningoencephalitis.
items.summary: This study investigated the diagnostic utility of adenosine deaminase levels measured in cerebrospinal fluid across a range of central nervous system infections, with particular attention to tropical diseases and HIV-infected patients, populations in which this marker had been insufficiently studied. Researchers analyzed cerebrospinal fluid adenosine deaminase levels from over two hundred patients with various microbiological diagnoses, comparing results against a non-infectious control group and examining correlations with other cerebrospinal fluid and blood laboratory parameters. Significantly elevated adenosine deaminase levels were found in patients with tuberculous meningitis and meningococcal meningitis compared to controls, with distinct cutoff values identified for tuberculosis and central nervous system coinfections. The sensitivity and specificity of the marker were modest for both conditions, and levels correlated positively with cerebrospinal fluid protein and negatively with cerebrospinal fluid glucose, while HIV status influenced results only in varicella-zoster virus infection. The authors conclude that cerebrospinal fluid adenosine deaminase can serve as a supportive, though not definitive, diagnostic tool in suspected tuberculous meningitis, meningococcal meningitis, and central nervous system coinfections.
items.citation: Farias LABG, Neto OMV, Sobrinho EPL et al.. Revisiting the use of adenosine deaminase in cerebrospinal fluid analysis for infectious meningoencephalitis.. Arquivos de neuro-psiquiatria. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic Performance of the FilmArray BCID2 Multiplex PCR Panel Applied to Excised Heart Valve Specimens from Patients with Infective Endocarditis.
items.summary: This study investigated whether the FilmArray BCID2 multiplex PCR panel, designed for blood culture identification, could be applied off-label to excised heart valve specimens as a diagnostic tool in infective endocarditis. Valve specimens from patients who underwent cardiac surgery for infective endocarditis were tested with the BCID2 panel, and results were compared against blood cultures and conventional valve cultures as reference standards. When benchmarked against blood cultures, the assay showed moderate sensitivity and high positive predictive value, but agreement between the two methods was low, and the negative predictive value was poor. Compared with conventional valve culture, specificity was perfect but sensitivity was very low, indicating the panel missed most culture-confirmed cases. The authors conclude that while the BCID2 panel may serve as a complementary tool in selected patients, a negative result cannot rule out infective endocarditis, and larger multicentre studies are needed to clarify its clinical utility.
items.citation: Bilewska A, Skrzeczyńska J, Dorota M et al.. Diagnostic Performance of the FilmArray BCID2 Multiplex PCR Panel Applied to Excised Heart Valve Specimens from Patients with Infective Endocarditis.. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Rapid identification of porcine bacterial pathogens using an artificial intelligence Raman microbial analyzer for biology.
items.summary: This study evaluated a commercial artificial intelligence-powered Raman spectroscopy system called AIRMAB for the rapid identification of bacterial pathogens isolated from diseased pigs. Bacterial isolates were collected from various tissues of diseased pigs and confirmed to species level using polymerase chain reaction before Raman spectral acquisition to establish accurate reference labels. The system combines Raman spectroscopy with deep learning to deliver label-free, isolate-level identification in approximately two minutes, covering fourteen clinically relevant swine bacterial pathogens. The AIRMAB system demonstrated high overall performance, achieving perfect recall for some of the most common species such as *Pasteurella multocida* and *Salmonella enterica* serovar Choleraesuis, and recall exceeding ninety percent for other important pathogens including *Escherichia coli*, *Streptococcus suis*, and *Glaesserella parasuis*. The authors conclude that this technology offers a rapid, accurate, and cost-effective alternative to conventional culture-based and molecular diagnostic methods, with practical utility for timely veterinary clinical decision-making and broader implications for zoonotic disease surveillance.
items.citation: Lu C-H, Ke N-J, Liu C-C et al.. Rapid identification of porcine bacterial pathogens using an artificial intelligence Raman microbial analyzer for biology.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: A Rapid Molecular Detection Method for Streptococcus agalactiae Based on Bacteriophage Lysin Lysis and Real-Time PCR.
items.summary: This study developed a rapid point-of-care molecular detection method for Group B Streptococcus, a major cause of neonatal infections, using bacteriophage lysin to achieve fast and efficient bacterial cell lysis. The approach combined lysin-based nucleic acid extraction completed within five minutes with real-time fluorescence quantitative PCR targeting the GBS cylA gene, bringing total turnaround time to approximately thirty-five minutes compared to the eighteen to forty-eight hours required for conventional culture. The assay was evaluated across two clinical cohorts using vaginal swab samples, where it demonstrated perfect sensitivity and high specificity in both phases, with specificity improving further after confirmatory sequencing of discordant samples. It also substantially outperformed antigen testing in sensitivity. The authors conclude that this bacteriophage lysin-based molecular assay shows strong diagnostic performance and potential utility for intrapartum or near-patient GBS screening, pending further validation in real-world clinical workflows.
items.venue: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
items.citation: Zhu H, Zeng X, Huang X et al.. A Rapid Molecular Detection Method for Streptococcus agalactiae Based on Bacteriophage Lysin Lysis and Real-Time PCR.. European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Temporal trends in pediatric group A streptococcal pharyngitis across the coronavirus disease 2019 era: A large retrospective cohort study.
items.summary: This study examined how the COVID-19 pandemic and its associated public health measures affected rates of Group A Streptococcus pharyngitis in children over time. Researchers conducted a large retrospective cohort study at a tertiary pediatric outpatient clinic, analyzing clinical episodes of suspected acute tonsillopharyngitis in patients aged zero to eighteen years spanning pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic periods. Group A Streptococcus positivity rates rose progressively across all three periods, with the lowest rates seen before the pandemic and the highest in the post-pandemic era. Multivariable analysis confirmed that the post-pandemic period was independently associated with greater odds of a positive test compared to the pandemic period, while older age and male sex were also independently associated with positivity. The authors conclude that this progressive increase likely reflects a combination of factors including changes in healthcare utilization, diagnostic practices, age distribution, and transmission dynamics, and that ongoing surveillance is warranted.
items.venue: The Journal of international medical research
items.citation: Nas Y, Gözüküçük S, Bayırlı H et al.. Temporal trends in pediatric group A streptococcal pharyngitis across the coronavirus disease 2019 era: A large retrospective cohort study.. The Journal of international medical research. 2026

items.title: Epidemiological surveillance reveals major pathogen dynamics in Brazilian Nile tilapia aquaculture from 2023 to 2025.
items.summary: This study examined the major bacterial and viral pathogens affecting Nile tilapia aquaculture across Brazil's three main producing regions over a two-year surveillance period. Researchers analyzed tens of thousands of diagnostic samples using bacteriological culture, real-time PCR, MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing, then applied generalized linear models, time-series analysis, co-detection network analysis, and pharmacological modelling to characterize pathogen dynamics. Rather than a single dominant threat, multiple pathogens were found to co-circulate at meaningful levels, with Infectious Spleen and Kidney Necrosis Virus, Lactococcus spp., and Streptococcus spp. representing the most widely detected agents, while Flavobacterium spp. showed the highest positivity rate on a smaller testing base. Most pathogens exhibited stationary, endemic dynamics consistent with stable regional presence, but Streptococcus spp. displayed non-stationary patterns suggesting active geographic expansion into the Northeast. These findings challenge the historically Streptococcus-centered view of Brazilian tilapia health and provide a baseline to support regionalized disease early-warning systems and more rational antimicrobial stewardship across the industry.
items.citation: Cardoso-Guimarães M, Fernandez-Alarcon MF, Correa R et al.. Epidemiological surveillance reveals major pathogen dynamics in Brazilian Nile tilapia aquaculture from 2023 to 2025.. Frontiers in veterinary science. 2026

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviewed advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research over a five-year period, synthesizing evidence to inform updated WHO policy guidance that consolidates recommendations for detecting tuberculosis disease and drug resistance into a single framework. Key developments included the expanded use of digital chest radiography with computer-aided detection as a frontline screening tool, broader deployment of decentralised molecular diagnostics such as low-complexity automated and manual nucleic acid amplification tests, and new specimen types like tongue swabs to improve testing in populations unable to produce sputum. Drug-resistance testing was enhanced through dedicated molecular platforms and next-generation sequencing at reference laboratory level, while urine-based lipoarabinomannan assays showed utility in people with HIV and advanced disease despite performance limitations. Host blood transcriptomic and other biomarkers demonstrated promise for prognosis and triage but no biomarker yet meets the WHO target product profile for a reliable point-of-care test distinguishing infection from active or subclinical tuberculosis disease. The authors conclude that despite meaningful progress, substantial gaps in diagnostic performance, implementation, and equity remain, underscoring ongoing developmental priorities in the field.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: Point-of-care testing in the diagnosis of infectious diseases.
items.summary: This review examines point-of-care testing as a diagnostic approach for infectious diseases, motivated by the growing global burden of such diseases and the escalating threat of antimicrobial resistance. The authors surveyed the core technical platforms underpinning current point-of-care technologies, including lateral flow assays, chemiluminescence immunoassays, isothermal amplification, CRISPR-based diagnostics, and microfluidic systems, as well as their application across respiratory, bloodstream, gastrointestinal, urinary tract, and sexually transmitted infections. The review discusses both immunochromatographic and molecular diagnostic modalities, weighing their technical characteristics against clinical applicability. While acknowledging persistent limitations in detection sensitivity, quality control, cost, and integration into clinical workflows, the authors identify advances in nanomaterials, microfluidic engineering, artificial intelligence, and industry standardization as drivers of improved performance. On this basis, they conclude that point-of-care testing holds strong promise as a central diagnostic tool for precision clinical management and public health infectious disease control.
items.citation: Fang Q, Lin Y, Hu G et al.. Point-of-care testing in the diagnosis of infectious diseases.. Frontiers in microbiology. 2026

items.title: Finger-actuated microfluidic device for point-of-care circulating cell-free nucleic acid extraction.
items.summary: This paper developed a fully finger-actuated microfluidic device designed to extract cell-free nucleic acids from plasma at the point of care without requiring external power or laboratory pipetting equipment. The device integrates finger-operated valves, a pump, and blister packs containing all necessary reagents, enabling a complete sample-to-eluate workflow encompassing lysis, binding, washing, and elution through manual actuation alone. Performance was benchmarked against commercial benchtop and automated robotic extraction methods using DNA-spiked aqueous samples and human pooled plasma, with the device achieving recovery rates comparable to or exceeding the manual benchtop control, particularly at lower input plasma volumes. Clinical utility was demonstrated using patient samples positive for cytomegalovirus, monkeypox virus, and chikungunya virus, with quantitative PCR amplification results closely matching those from standard protocols. The authors propose this instrument-free extraction tool as a scalable solution to bridge the gap between existing nucleic acid amplification technologies and decentralised diagnostic needs in resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Musaddaq G, Ehsan L, Yoga Y et al.. Finger-actuated microfluidic device for point-of-care circulating cell-free nucleic acid extraction.. Lab on a chip. 2026

items.title: Molecular point-of-care: technological evolution, clinical applications, and future perspectives
items.citation: Zhang D, Cui X, Zhang R et al.. Molecular point-of-care: technological evolution, clinical applications, and future perspectives. Frontiers in bioengineering and biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.
items.summary: This review paper examines the current landscape of molecular diagnostic technologies used to detect and characterize pathogens responsible for infectious diseases. The authors survey nucleic acid amplification approaches, including various polymerase chain reaction formats optimized for speed, quantification, automation, and point-of-care deployment, as well as isothermal amplification methods that operate without thermal cycling equipment. The review also covers CRISPR-based detection systems, which are frequently paired with isothermal amplification, and next-generation sequencing, which enables identification of novel pathogens, tracking of outbreak transmission, and microbiome analysis relevant to disease susceptibility. The authors conclude that the field is advancing toward hybrid platforms that integrate multiple technologies to overcome the individual limitations of each approach.
items.citation: Takata M, Chikumi H, Yoshifuji A. Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.. Yonago acta medica. 2026

items.title: QMini: A Portable Device for Infectious Disease Testing.
items.summary: The paper studied the development of a portable device for nucleic acid-based infectious disease testing that overcomes the size limitations of conventional laboratory equipment. The researchers built the QMini by simplifying the fluidic module through direct pump-to-chamber connections and shielding the optical module from ambient light using a three-dimensional printed enclosure. They applied the device to detect synthetic nucleic acid sequences from respiratory syncytial virus B, SARS-CoV-2, and influenza A using a bead-based assay with quantum dot barcodes. The device successfully detected low copy numbers of all three pathogens while showing limited cross-reactivity against nontarget viral sequences. The authors conclude that the QMini advances the portability of quantum dot barcode-based nucleic acid testing through device miniaturization, supporting its potential use in field settings.
items.citation: Mahbub N, Osborne M, Chen H et al.. QMini: A Portable Device for Infectious Disease Testing.. ACS nanoscience Au. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review paper examines the convergence of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence as a combined strategy for advancing precision drug discovery and clinical translation. The authors synthesize how multiomics approaches, spanning genomic association studies, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, generate detailed molecular portraits of disease that can be interrogated by deep learning architectures to uncover hidden biological patterns and build predictive models. The review covers applications across the full drug development pipeline, including target identification, drug repositioning, de novo compound design, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. Disease areas highlighted include oncology, neurodegenerative disorders, and cardiovascular conditions, with attention to the technological infrastructures supporting these efforts. The authors conclude that while this integration holds strong promise for accelerating and refining therapeutic development, significant challenges around harmonizing disparate data streams, ensuring reproducibility, and reducing algorithmic bias must still be addressed.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Loss-of-function mutation in Omicron variants reduces spike protein expression and attenuates SARS-CoV-2 infection

items.title: Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective
items.summary: This paper examined the regulatory landscape governing cell-derived extracellular vesicles as therapeutic and diagnostic products across major global jurisdictions. The authors critically reviewed how existing medicinal product frameworks in the European Union, United States, Japan, and other regions apply to extracellular vesicle-based products, noting that their acellular nature creates inconsistent regulatory classification depending on jurisdiction. A central focus was the tension between the recent European guidance clarifying that minimally modified extracellular vesicles fall outside advanced therapy medicinal product definitions and the approach taken by other regulators who treat such products as drugs or biological products subject to premarket requirements. The authors identified key operational grey zones including classification criteria, critical quality attributes, potency assessment strategies, and comparability requirements that need clarification to support coherent cross-regional clinical development. Rather than proposing new normative frameworks, the work offers a synthesis intended to foster regulatory dialogue among international agencies and scientific societies to advance extracellular vesicle therapies toward safe and internationally credible clinical use.
items.citation: Tania Limongi, Paola Milla, Barbara Stella et al.. Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective. Journal of Extracellular Vesicles. 2026

items.title: Lethal plague outbreaks in Lake Baikal hunter-gatherers 5,500 years ago
items.summary: This paper investigated the history of plague caused by *Yersinia pestis* among ancient hunter-gatherer populations near Lake Baikal in Siberia, examining skeletal remains from four cemeteries dating to approximately five and a half thousand years ago. The researchers recovered and analyzed ancient *Y. pestis* genomes and reconstructed kinship pedigrees from affected individuals to understand the nature and spread of these early infections. They found a strikingly high detection rate of plague infection and evidence that outbreaks spread within small family groups across a single generation, with acute mortality particularly affecting children. The newly identified strains diverge ancestrally from all previously known *Y. pestis* lineages and include functional differences at the ypm superantigen locus also found in the related bacterium *Yersinia pseudotuberculosis*, pushing back the estimated emergence of *Y. pestis* to before approximately five thousand seven hundred years ago. Crucially, the occurrence of lethal plague epidemics among low-density hunter-gatherer communities challenges the prevailing view that the dense populations and lifestyle changes associated with the Neolithic agricultural transition were necessary preconditions for plague outbreaks.
items.citation: Ruairidh Macleod, Frederik Valeur Seersholm, Bianca De Sanctis et al.. Lethal plague outbreaks in Lake Baikal hunter-gatherers 5,500 years ago. Nature. 2026

items.title: PhotoFinish: Portable Timerless Probing of Microarchitectural Latencies
items.summary: This paper investigates timerless methods for measuring microarchitectural latencies, motivated by the observation that restricting high-resolution timers is a common but potentially insufficient defense against microarchitectural side-channel attacks. The authors developed PhotoFinish, a portable primitive that races an operation under test against a fixed reference using two parallel threads that write unique values to a shared memory location, converting latency differences into an architectural value without ever reading or constructing a clock. PhotoFinish was evaluated across a broad range of processors spanning multiple instruction set architectures and was shown to reliably classify cache states across diverse microarchitectures, including when compiled to WebAssembly and run inside a browser. The primitive was demonstrated in realistic attack scenarios, including cache-based and TLB-based side channels, and proved precise enough to identify last-level cache slices. The findings show that shared-memory racing constitutes a generic and precise substitute for explicit timing, undermining the assumption that timer restriction alone can prevent software from observing fine-grained microarchitectural latency differences.
items.citation: Tristan Hornetz, Eduard Ebert, Lorenz Hetterich et al.. PhotoFinish: Portable Timerless Probing of Microarchitectural Latencies. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper investigates the reliability of pseudo-labels generated through majority voting during test-time reinforcement learning, where pretrained language models are adapted to unlabeled target-domain data using their own outputs as supervision signals. The authors theoretically decompose the error in majority-vote supervision into two components: a population-majority bias that cannot be corrected without external labels, and a prompt-dependent variation arising from finite sampling. To address the correctable component, they propose Prompt-Conditional Distributionally Robust DPO, a method that makes learning updates more conservative for prompts where vote reliability is low, combined with a cache-based mechanism to reduce forgetting during online adaptation. Evaluated across a broad set of mathematical and knowledge-intensive reasoning benchmarks with multiple model backbones, the proposed approach matches or outperforms the strongest existing test-time reinforcement learning baseline in the large majority of experimental settings.
items.citation: Haoyu Wang, Ru Wang, Yuanyuan Wang et al.. On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: An Empirical Study on Clustering-based Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm for Regression Test Case Selection
items.summary: This paper investigates the application of quantum computing to regression test case selection, a software engineering challenge where re-running entire test suites after every code modification is computationally prohibitive. The authors extend their previously proposed clustering-based Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm approach, called QAOA-TCS, by conducting a thorough empirical evaluation against both classical methods such as Additional Greedy and DIV-GA, and quantum competitors including SelectQA, BootQA, and IGDec-QAOA. The study assesses performance across single-objective and multi-objective problem formulations and explicitly examines robustness under realistic quantum noise conditions. QAOA-TCS was found to outperform state-of-the-art multi-objective approaches in most cases and remained stable even at high noise levels, while in the single-objective setting quantum approaches performed comparably to one another. In terms of efficiency, the quantum annealing-based SelectQA proved most efficient for large multi-objective problems, whereas QAOA-TCS offered the best effectiveness-efficiency trade-off in the single-objective formulation on noisy simulators, though comparisons were complicated by differing computational environments across methods.
items.citation: Antonio Trovato, Martin Beseda, Dario Di Nucci. An Empirical Study on Clustering-based Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm for Regression Test Case Selection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Geometric Pairwise Classification of Affine Constraints over Ellipsoidal Regions
items.summary: This paper develops a deterministic geometric method for classifying affine (linear) constraints with respect to fixed ellipsoidal regions, motivated by problems in chance-constrained optimization. For each individual constraint, analytical tests determine whether it is always violated, never violated, or cuts through the ellipsoid, while pairwise tests assess whether two constraints can be simultaneously and strictly violated at a common point, producing a compatibility matrix. The approach is grounded in quadratic optimization and Karush–Kuhn–Tucker optimality conditions, with careful handling of edge cases such as tangencies, parallel constraint normals, and degenerate inequalities. The method is applicable in any finite-dimensional setting and is intended to supply geometric information useful for bounding probabilities of simultaneous constraint violations and for approximating safe feasible regions.
items.citation: Igor M. L. Pataro, Martina Mammarella, Fabrizio Dabbene et al.. Geometric Pairwise Classification of Affine Constraints over Ellipsoidal Regions. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic performance of antigen-based rapid test kits for six respiratory viruses in children: comparison with a multiplex PCR panel and correlation with viral load.
items.summary: This study examined how well antigen-based rapid test kits perform for diagnosing six common respiratory viruses in children, and whether sensitivity depends on the amount of virus present in the specimen. In a prospective paired-specimen design, nasopharyngeal swabs from children with respiratory tract infections were tested simultaneously with antigen rapid tests and a multiplex PCR panel, with positive specimens further analysed by quantitative real-time PCR to determine viral load. Across more than fifteen hundred paired specimens, specificity exceeded ninety-nine percent for all six viral targets, while sensitivity varied considerably by pathogen and was strongly dependent on viral load—rising to near-complete detection at high viral loads and falling below fifty percent at low viral loads, consistently across all six viruses. These findings indicate that rapid antigen tests reliably identify children carrying the highest viral burdens, who are most likely to have acute, clinically significant infection, while their limitations at low viral loads reflect a biologically meaningful threshold rather than a simple diagnostic deficiency.
items.citation: Kitagawa D, Di Lorenzo A, Okamura T et al.. Diagnostic performance of antigen-based rapid test kits for six respiratory viruses in children: comparison with a multiplex PCR panel and correlation with viral load.. Journal of clinical microbiology. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic yield of reflex multiplex PCR after a negative rapid antigen test in children hospitalized with presumed viral acute respiratory tract infection: a prospective cohort study.
items.summary: This study investigated whether adding reflex multiplex PCR testing after a negative rapid antigen test improves viral detection in children hospitalized with presumed viral acute respiratory infections. In a prospective single-center cohort, children first underwent a five-target rapid antigen test, and those testing negative could then receive multiplex PCR at physician discretion. The study found that antigen testing alone identified fewer than a quarter of children with a detectable virus, while reflex PCR substantially increased diagnostic yield among antigen-negative children, with the large majority of those tested by PCR returning a positive result. Rhinovirus/enterovirus, which is not covered by standard antigen panels, was the most commonly identified pathogen overall, highlighting a key limitation of antigen testing alone. Antibiotic use was high across the cohort regardless of whether a virus was detected, though the authors note that the appropriateness of antibiotic prescribing could not be fully assessed without systematic bacterial testing.
items.citation: Bedir AZ, Saf C, Yörük MA. Diagnostic yield of reflex multiplex PCR after a negative rapid antigen test in children hospitalized with presumed viral acute respiratory tract infection: a prospective cohort study.. Irish journal of medical science. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of the RapidFor™ RSV/ADV Rapid Test Kit Compared with PCR for the Detection of Respiratory Syncytial Virus and Adenovirus in Nasopharyngeal Swab Samples
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of a point-of-care rapid antigen test, the RapidFor™ RSV/ADV Rapid Test Kit, for detecting respiratory syncytial virus and adenovirus in children presenting to a pediatric emergency department with acute respiratory symptoms. Using multiplex real-time PCR as the reference standard, researchers prospectively collected paired nasopharyngeal swabs from children aged eighteen years and younger during a defined respiratory season. The rapid test demonstrated very high sensitivity and specificity for both pathogens, with excellent agreement with PCR results for adenovirus and RSV alike. Age-related patterns in pathogen distribution were also identified, with RSV predominating in infants under one year and adenovirus more common in school-aged children, and distinct clinical predictors were associated with each infection. The authors conclude that this dual rapid antigen test offers clinically useful diagnostic performance and may support timely decision-making in pediatric emergency care settings.
items.citation: Ates B, Kacar A, Kok S et al.. Diagnostic Accuracy of the RapidFor™ RSV/ADV Rapid Test Kit Compared with PCR for the Detection of Respiratory Syncytial Virus and Adenovirus in Nasopharyngeal Swab Samples. 2026
