items.title: Mechanism-informed diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy: a systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis investigated the diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy, a severe form of acute brain dysfunction occurring in sepsis patients. The authors searched multiple databases and synthesized evidence from studies providing extractable diagnostic data, organizing candidate biomarkers along a biological axis spanning innate immune activation, blood-brain barrier dysfunction, glial response, and neuronal injury, while accounting for heterogeneity in how SAE was defined and when biomarkers were sampled. Pooled diagnostic test accuracy analyses indicated that blood-brain barrier and glial markers such as GFAP and S100β generally demonstrated more balanced discriminative performance than classic neuronal injury markers in the evaluated diagnostic settings. Bayesian comparative ranking identified upstream immune and alarmin candidates alongside timed S100β measurements as top performers, though several highly ranked biomarkers were supported by only single studies, and thresholds, sampling contexts, and platforms varied considerably across included work. The authors conclude that blood biomarkers reflect a biologically coherent immune-to-neuronal cascade in SAE, but that findings are hypothesis-generating rather than practice-changing, calling for prospective head-to-head validation using standardized phenotyping and anchor-based sampling to determine whether mechanism-staged biomarker panels offer incremental diagnostic value beyond established clinical predictors.
items.citation: Zhang Q, Zhu R, Li Y et al.. Mechanism-informed diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy: a systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis.. Frontiers in molecular neuroscience. 2026

items.title: Dynamic Changes of Neutrophil Nuclear Membrane CD63 as a Potential Biomarker for Early Adjunctive Diagnosis and Prognostic Evaluation of Sepsis in Critically Ill Patients: A Prospective Cohort Study.
items.summary: This study investigated whether neutrophil nuclear membrane CD63 (nmCD63), a marker of targeted nuclear degranulation during neutrophil extracellular trap formation, could serve as an early diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for sepsis in critically ill patients. The researchers developed a flow cytometry assay to quantify nmCD63 and validated it in a two-center prospective cohort with independent external validation. They found that nmCD63 levels rose progressively with disease severity and outperformed conventional biomarkers such as C-reactive protein and procalcitonin in distinguishing non-infectious systemic inflammation from infection. When combined with organ failure scoring, nmCD63 achieved strong discriminatory performance for identifying sepsis in patients with confirmed infection. Importantly, dynamic changes in nmCD63 preceded shifts in all conventional biomarkers, and tracking its trajectory over one week enabled reliable stratification of patient prognosis.
items.citation: Gao X, Zhang M, Li L et al.. Dynamic Changes of Neutrophil Nuclear Membrane CD63 as a Potential Biomarker for Early Adjunctive Diagnosis and Prognostic Evaluation of Sepsis in Critically Ill Patients: A Prospective Cohort Study.. MedComm. 2026

items.title: Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis
items.summary: This review examines the role of gut microbial-derived metabolites in the development and progression of kidney disease, including acute kidney injury and various forms of chronic kidney disease. The authors synthesize current evidence showing that kidney injury disrupts intestinal barrier integrity and promotes microbial dysbiosis, which in turn reduces beneficial short-chain fatty acids while allowing uremic toxins to accumulate. These metabolic shifts influence kidney pathology through multiple signaling pathways, with tryptophan metabolites highlighted as particularly important mediators of gut-kidney communication. The review maps the underlying pathophysiology of these associations across specific kidney conditions such as diabetic kidney disease, immunoglobulin A nephropathy, and membranous nephropathy. The authors also survey therapeutic strategies targeting gut microbiota dysbiosis, including natural products, prebiotics, probiotics, and renal replacement therapy, with the aim of informing more precise treatment approaches for kidney disease.
items.citation: Wan-Ying Zhang, Yu-Lu Zhang, Qing-Qing Yu et al.. Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis. International Journal of Biological Sciences. 2026

items.title: A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression
items.summary: This systematic review examined how different forms of exercise affect the expression of Toll-like receptors, a family of immune pattern recognition receptors implicated in inflammatory signalling and linked to sedentary behaviour and non-communicable disease. The authors searched multiple databases for studies in which exercise was used as an isolated intervention in human participants, ultimately including studies categorised by exercise modality and duration, spanning acute and chronic resistance, aerobic, and combined training protocols. Acute resistance exercise tended to upregulate TLR expression, while acute aerobic exercise more often produced neutral or downregulatory effects, particularly in healthy individuals. Chronic resistance and combined training programs predominantly left TLR levels unchanged or reduced them, whereas chronic aerobic training yielded mixed results with most measurements showing no significant change. The authors conclude that exercise interacts with TLR signalling in a manner dependent on exercise characteristics, but highlight that substantial heterogeneity in study designs limits firm conclusions and that further research is needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms and pathophysiological implications.
items.citation: Kasper Favere, Matthias Bosman, Peter Delputte et al.. A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support
items.summary: This review paper examines the application of federated learning as a privacy-preserving approach to training artificial intelligence models across diverse healthcare data modalities, including biomedical imaging, electronic health records, wearable sensor outputs, and clinical decision support systems. The authors conducted a broad literature review spanning multiple clinical domains such as chronic disease management, elder care, and diagnostics involving modalities like MRI, CT, ultrasound, and histopathology. The core premise is that federated learning enables multi-institutional AI training by sharing only model updates rather than raw patient data, thereby improving alignment with privacy regulations without requiring centralized data storage. However, the review emphasizes that privacy is not guaranteed by federated learning alone, as vulnerabilities such as gradient leakage, model inversion, and membership inference attacks necessitate additional safeguards. Beyond cataloguing successes, the authors identify persistent implementation challenges including system heterogeneity, data imbalance, communication bottlenecks, and fairness concerns, and offer actionable recommendations for regulators, developers, and healthcare systems to advance equitable and geographically distributed federated learning in medicine.
items.venue: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
items.citation: Shon G. Nemane, Vaishnavi M. Sarad, Dhiraj P. Tulaskar et al.. Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support. Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering. 2026

items.title: Stimuli-responsive nanocarriers for precision targeted and controlled antimicrobial drug delivery in drug-resistant infections
items.summary: This review examines stimuli-responsive nanocarriers as a strategy to overcome the limitations of conventional antibiotics, which fail to maintain therapeutic concentrations at infection sites and promote resistance by exposing microbiota to sub-inhibitory drug levels. The authors systematically analyze how nanocarriers engineered to respond to infection-specific microenvironmental cues—including acidic pH, elevated reactive oxygen species, pathogen-associated enzymatic activity, and hypoxia—can achieve spatiotemporally controlled, site-selective drug release. The review details the mechanistic basis of pH-, enzyme-, redox-, and multi-stimuli-responsive systems, explaining how trigger-induced physicochemical changes govern drug retention, activation, and penetration within drug-resistant infection environments. These platforms are further evaluated for their capacity to address resistance-associated barriers such as biofilm tolerance, intracellular pathogen persistence, efflux pump activity, and enzymatic antibiotic degradation, with a critical comparison made against passive nanocarriers and free antibiotics. The authors also identify key translational challenges—including microenvironmental heterogeneity, trigger variability, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory complexity—while arguing that stimuli-responsive nanocarriers represent a meaningful shift toward context-aware antimicrobial intervention capable of addressing drug resistance beyond the pace of conventional antibiotic discovery.
items.citation: Li Dai, Xiaoyan Sun. Stimuli-responsive nanocarriers for precision targeted and controlled antimicrobial drug delivery in drug-resistant infections. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: The Gut–Vagina Axis
items.summary: This review paper examined the emerging concept of the gut–vagina axis, focusing on how interactions between the gut and vaginal microbiomes may influence female health. The authors synthesized recent advances in microbiome research to explore the mechanisms underlying this relationship, including microbial migration between sites, hormonal and immune regulation, and metabolite exchange. They highlight that communication between gut and vaginal microbial communities appears to be bidirectional, with each site capable of influencing the microbial composition, immune responses, hormonal balance, and metabolic activity of the other. The review concludes that these interactions have meaningful implications for both local and systemic health outcomes in women.
items.citation: Lorenzo Agoni, Elena Roselletti, Giovanni Marasco et al.. The Gut–Vagina Axis. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Pulmonary inflammation in severe pneumonia is characterised by compartmentalised and mechanistically distinct sub-phenotypes
items.summary: This paper investigated the biological basis of severe pneumonia, which remains poorly understood despite being the leading infectious killer worldwide and a major driver of critical care admissions. The researchers performed comprehensive analyses of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, examining transcriptomic profiles, cytokine levels, microbiology, and clinical features in a cohort of patients with suspected severe pneumonia. They identified three distinct lung-restricted transcriptional endotypes, termed Pneumotypes, which share similar clinical presentations and severity of respiratory failure but differ markedly in their underlying immune biology and patient outcomes. The most common endotype is characterized by low alveolar cytokines, tolerogenic macrophages, and epithelial damage, a second endotype shows immature neutrophil infiltration and IL-6-STAT3 pathway activation associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation, while a third endotype resolves most rapidly and displays balanced immune activation alongside epithelial-endothelial repair signatures. The authors conclude that these mechanistically distinct pulmonary sub-phenotypes represent potential targets for personalized therapeutic strategies in severe pneumonia and acute lung injury.
items.citation: Mark Jeffrey, Josefin Bartholdson Scott, Shyamanova Mazumdar et al.. Pulmonary inflammation in severe pneumonia is characterised by compartmentalised and mechanistically distinct sub-phenotypes. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments
items.summary: This paper investigates intrinsic alignments of galaxies, which introduce systematic errors in weak gravitational lensing surveys and offer insights into galaxy formation and evolution. The authors developed model-agnostic tests to examine how density-weighting affects intrinsic alignment signals and to evaluate whether the standard tidal alignment paradigm accurately describes galaxy orientations. Using data from the IllustrisTNG cosmological hydrodynamical simulation and an observed galaxy survey, they found that density-weighting primarily amplifies alignment signals on large scales, while its effects on small scales depend on the specific galaxy sample. Additionally, by correlating galaxy shapes with the underlying tidal fields, they found that central galaxies align linearly with the non-linear tidal field even within the one-halo regime, supporting the tidal alignment paradigm down to small scales given their measurement precision.
items.citation: Paul Rogozenski, Sukhdeep Singh, Jonathan Blazek et al.. Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of integrating chain-of-thought reasoning into Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) for image generation, arguing that existing approaches fail because reasoning operates in discrete token space while image generation requires continuous space. To bridge this modality mismatch, the authors propose LARC, a Latent Reasoning framework in Continuous space, which shifts reasoning from token-level representations to continuous hidden states. The training framework proceeds in two stages: a curriculum supervised fine-tuning stage that gradually transitions token-level reasoning into latent reasoning, followed by an information-gain reinforcement learning stage that refines latent reasoning without requiring ground truth supervision. Evaluated across text-to-image generation benchmarks, LARC improves generation quality, prompt following, and compositional fidelity, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the GenEval benchmark and exhibiting test-time scaling behavior under both parallel and sequential strategies.
items.citation: Byungwoo Jeon, Yoonwoo Jeong, Hyunseok Lee et al.. Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of long-horizon planning for embodied agents, where cumulative errors and search complexity degrade performance in world model-based approaches. The authors introduce a hierarchical world model framework called ID-WM that separates high-level reachability planning from low-level action execution by combining a high-level model that samples feasible state transitions across the state manifold with a low-level inverse dynamics solver that translates those transitions into concrete actions. This decoupling allows the planner to identify viable subgoals without being constrained by low-level execution details, enabling the synthesis of novel long-horizon plans from short behavioral segments that generalize beyond training distributions. Evaluated across navigation and manipulation benchmarks, the framework substantially outperforms both state-of-the-art policy and diffusion-based planners, with particularly large gains over single-level world model approaches on complex, unseen long-horizon configurations.
items.citation: Gaoyue Zhou, Yvonne Wu, Zichen Jeff Cui et al.. Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Approximate Polynomial Satisfiability and Integral Closure Membership in the Counting Hierarchy
items.summary: This paper studies the computational complexity of two algebraic problems: approximate polynomial satisfiability (APS), which asks whether a polynomial system is nearly satisfiable, and integral closure membership, which asks whether a given polynomial is integral over a specified polynomial ring. The authors prove that both problems belong to the Counting Hierarchy for rational polynomials represented by arithmetic circuits, significantly improving the previously known upper bound of PSPACE for APS. Their approach to APS combines Noether normalization with a geometric analysis of how points in the image of a polynomial map approach the origin, reducing the problem to a test on multivariate resultants that can be solved within the Counting Hierarchy. For integral closure membership, they apply a global annihilator criterion together with an effective degree bound to reduce non-integrality to APS in polynomial time, thereby inheriting the Counting Hierarchy upper bound. These results complement concurrent independent work by other groups and have implications for geometric complexity theory, where APS had previously been used to construct hitting sets narrowing the so-called GCT chasm.
items.citation: Sanyam Agarwal, Archit Hari, Anurag Pandey et al.. Approximate Polynomial Satisfiability and Integral Closure Membership in the Counting Hierarchy. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Instance-dependent sequential limits as an exact information ledger
items.summary: This paper studies instance-dependent lower bounds for sequential decision-making problems including bandit regret, sequential hypothesis testing, best-arm identification, and Markov decision processes. The authors unify the derivation of these classical limits through a single chain of reasoning that proceeds from a divergence decomposition, through data processing inequalities, to a testing step and optimization over alternatives and allocations. A key contribution is formulating this chain as an exact "ledger" that tracks precisely where information is lost at each step, showing via the chain rule that data processing loses exactly a conditional divergence, which vanishes for natural exponential family reward distributions at sufficient statistics. The framework introduces a one-parameter family of martingale identities extending the decomposition across tilted instances, and identifies named, computable defects corresponding to each relaxation that converts the exact identity into a classical limit. Applying the ledger to seven published empirical datasets, the authors find that the gap between standard algorithms and classical limits is most often dominated by the uniform quantification term, particularly in model selection and Wald's sequential test settings.
items.citation: Akshay Balsubramani. Instance-dependent sequential limits as an exact information ledger. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Co-sufficient weighting: leveraging sparsity for more powerful variable selection in the linear model
items.summary: The paper addresses controlled variable selection in the Gaussian linear model, asking whether useful weights for weighted multiple testing procedures can be constructed from the data alone, without external information. The authors derive what they call co-sufficient weights, which are both informative and statistically independent of the p-values, by exploiting sufficient statistics and an assumption of sparsity. Applying these weights to weighted versions of Holm's procedure and the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure yields substantially greater statistical power than the unweighted counterparts when the true coefficient vector is sparse, while preserving the exact and robust error control guarantees of the original procedures regardless of whether sparsity holds. The approach is validated through extensive simulations and an application to HIV drug resistance data, where it outperforms competing methods across a wide range of settings.
items.citation: Souhardya Sengupta, Lucas Janson. Co-sufficient weighting: leveraging sparsity for more powerful variable selection in the linear model. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Rapid Diagnostics for Antimicrobial Resistance: From Bench to Bedside
items.citation: Mugisha N, Fawaz L, Noureddine R et al.. Artificial Intelligence in Rapid Diagnostics for Antimicrobial Resistance: From Bench to Bedside. Health science reports. 2026

items.title: Integrated evaluation of rapid diagnostic testing, genotypic-phenotypic resistance profiling, and AI-Assisted prediction models for antimicrobial stewardship and clinical outcomes in a resource-limited setting.
items.summary: This prospective observational study investigated whether combining rapid diagnostic testing, molecular resistance gene profiling, and an artificial intelligence prediction model could improve antimicrobial stewardship and patient outcomes in a resource-limited hospital setting. Adult patients with suspected bacterial infections were enrolled and evaluated using conventional antibiotic susceptibility testing alongside rapid diagnostics and genotypic resistance characterization, with an AI model trained on clinical and laboratory parameters to predict antimicrobial resistance. The integrated approach dramatically shortened the time to pathogen identification and effective therapy initiation compared with conventional testing alone, and was associated with substantially improved rates of appropriate antibiotic prescribing and reduced broad-spectrum antibiotic use. Patients managed with the integrated strategy also experienced shorter hospital stays and lower mortality, while genotypic and phenotypic resistance results showed substantial concordance and the AI model achieved strong discriminatory performance. The authors conclude that this combined diagnostic and predictive framework represents a potentially cost-effective and scalable strategy for combating antimicrobial resistance in settings with limited resources.
items.citation: Hammad M, Arif R, Fardoos S et al.. Integrated evaluation of rapid diagnostic testing, genotypic-phenotypic resistance profiling, and AI-Assisted prediction models for antimicrobial stewardship and clinical outcomes in a resource-limited setting.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Syndromic Testing in Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases: An Updated Review of Diagnostic Performance, Clinical and Healthcare Impact, and Emerging Developments.
items.summary: This review examines syndromic testing, an approach that uses nucleic acid amplification to simultaneously detect multiple pathogens and antimicrobial resistance determinants directly from clinical specimens, and how it has transformed infectious disease diagnostics over the past two decades. The authors surveyed the landscape of FDA-cleared multiplex panels across seven major clinical syndromes, including respiratory, bloodstream, gastrointestinal, and central nervous system infections, among others, summarizing their diagnostic performance, clinical applications, and limitations. Compared to traditional culture-based workflows requiring days for results, syndromic panels deliver comprehensive pathogen identification within hours, enabling faster and more targeted antimicrobial therapy. Evidence reviewed indicates that when syndromic testing is paired with antimicrobial stewardship programs, it can reduce time to optimal therapy, decrease unnecessary antimicrobial use, and shorten hospital stays, with mortality benefits observed particularly in bloodstream infection patients. However, the authors caution that rapid results do not automatically translate into improved outcomes, and challenges remain around panel utilization, evolving resistance epidemiology, and geographically variable pathogen distributions.
items.citation: Wang G, Chen F. Syndromic Testing in Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases: An Updated Review of Diagnostic Performance, Clinical and Healthcare Impact, and Emerging Developments.. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances and Future Perspectives in the Detection of Carbapenem-Resistant <i>Acinetobacter Baumannii</i>.
items.summary: This review examines the landscape of detection technologies for carbapenem-resistant *Acinetobacter baumannii*, a pathogen classified as a critical priority threat due to its multidrug resistance and limited treatment options. The authors surveyed a broad range of diagnostic approaches, spanning conventional phenotypic and culture-based susceptibility testing, nucleic acid amplification methods, whole-genome and metagenomic sequencing, mass spectrometry, AI-assisted diagnostics, and biosensor and CRISPR-integrated platforms. They found that while culture-based antimicrobial susceptibility testing remains the reference standard, its lengthy turnaround time limits early clinical decision-making, whereas molecular methods such as PCR, isothermal amplification, and biosensor platforms substantially reduce detection times and support point-of-care applications. Emerging genomic tools offer comprehensive resistance profiling and surveillance capabilities, and AI integration may improve resistance prediction, though challenges in standardization, cost, multiplexing, and clinical validation persist across newer platforms. The review concludes that the field is transitioning toward integrated, automated, and clinically adaptable diagnostics, with an emphasis on balancing analytical performance, speed, cost, and point-of-care suitability.
items.citation: Ye Q, Liu Y, Zhang K et al.. Recent Advances and Future Perspectives in the Detection of Carbapenem-Resistant <i>Acinetobacter Baumannii</i>.. Infection and drug resistance. 2026

items.title: Artificial intelligence in the diagnosis and identification of bacterial pathogens: Current advances and future perspectives.
items.summary: This review examines the growing role of artificial intelligence in the diagnosis and identification of bacterial pathogens, motivated by the global burden of bacterial infections and the limitations of conventional diagnostic methods such as culture, microscopy, and biochemical testing. The authors surveyed current applications of machine learning and deep learning algorithms, including Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, Artificial Neural Networks, and Convolutional Neural Networks, as applied to platforms such as automated microscopy, next-generation genomic sequencing, MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, and clinical data systems. The review finds that AI-assisted approaches can substantially improve the speed, accuracy, and automation of pathogen detection while enabling large-scale analysis of complex microbiological and clinical datasets. The authors also discuss current limitations of these technologies and argue that future integration of AI into microbiology laboratories, genomic surveillance systems, and clinical decision support tools holds strong potential to advance antimicrobial stewardship and global infection management.
items.citation: A Mohammed S. Artificial intelligence in the diagnosis and identification of bacterial pathogens: Current advances and future perspectives.. Diagnostic microbiology and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist
items.summary: This paper introduces Co-Scientist, a multi-agent AI system built on the Gemini architecture designed to augment scientific discovery by autonomously generating, critiquing, and refining research hypotheses. The system employs an asynchronous task execution framework for flexible compute scaling and a tournament-based evolution process for iterative hypothesis improvement, with automated evaluations confirming that increased test-time compute consistently improves hypothesis quality. Although designed as a general-purpose tool, its validation focused on three biomedical domains: drug repurposing, novel target discovery, and understanding mechanisms of antimicrobial resistance. Notably, Co-Scientist identified new drug-repurposing candidates and synergistic combination therapies for acute myeloid leukaemia that were subsequently confirmed through in vitro experiments. These real-world experimental validations support the authors' claim that AI systems of this kind have genuine potential to accelerate the pace of scientific discovery.
items.citation: Juraj Gottweis, Wei‐Hung Weng, Alexander Daryin et al.. Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist. Nature. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and translational medicine. The authors surveyed multiomics approaches—including genome-wide association studies, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics—alongside advanced AI methodologies such as deep learning, to assess their combined utility across the drug development pipeline. The review covers how these tools contribute to target deconvolution, drug repositioning, de novo compound discovery, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. The authors argue that this convergence accelerates target identification and lead optimization while enabling more precise clinical trial design, with illustrative cases drawn from oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions. They also identify persistent challenges, including harmonization of disparate omics data, reproducibility concerns, and the need to mitigate algorithmic biases, while framing the overall trajectory as the opening of a new era in bench-to-clinic medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: ANO6-mediated trogocytosis of cancer-associated fibroblasts promotes pancreatic cancer cell growth and immune suppression
items.summary: This study investigated how pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cells acquire essential lipids despite residing in a poorly vascularized tumor microenvironment dominated by fibroblastic stroma. The researchers discovered that cancer-associated fibroblasts transfer lipids from blood-borne particles to pancreatic cancer cells through a process called trogocytosis, in which the cancer cells bite off portions of the fibroblast plasma membrane at synapse-like contact points. This process is regulated by the phospholipid scramblase ANO6, which is activated in fibroblasts when calcium influx through Orai channels triggers phosphatidylserine exposure on the fibroblast membrane, enabling transfer of membrane lipids including cholesterol to tumor cells. Beyond fueling cancer cell growth, ANO6-mediated trogocytosis was found to support immune suppression by facilitating excessive cholesterol transfer that impairs cytotoxic T cell function. Blocking ANO6 disrupted exogenous cholesterol delivery to cancer cells and reversed immune suppression, suggesting it represents a potential therapeutic target in pancreatic cancer.
items.citation: Charline Ogier, Charles Solomon Akino Mercy, Elena Bondarenko et al.. ANO6-mediated trogocytosis of cancer-associated fibroblasts promotes pancreatic cancer cell growth and immune suppression. Nature Cancer. 2026

items.title: Arc mediates intercellular tau transmission via extracellular vesicles
items.summary: The paper investigated the mechanisms by which misfolded tau protein spreads between cells in neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia. The researchers focused on the neuronal gene Arc and its potential role in packaging tau into extracellular vesicles (EVs), using transgenic mouse models that either expressed or lacked Arc alongside human tau. They found that Arc is essential for loading tau into EVs through a pathway involving the I-BAR protein IRSp53, and that Arc directly binds tau to form a complex detectable in both mouse and human brain tissue. When Arc was knocked out, EVs contained far less tau and lost the ability to seed tau aggregation, while pathological tau instead accumulated intracellularly in neurons and was associated with accelerated hippocampal neuron loss. The authors conclude that Arc-mediated release of tau via EVs serves a dual function, facilitating both the clearance of intracellular tau and its intercellular transmission.
items.citation: Mitali Tyagi, Eric de Hoog, Matthew Grega et al.. Arc mediates intercellular tau transmission via extracellular vesicles. Cell. 2026

items.title: Synthesis and multilevel evaluation of benzimidazole-based anticancer compounds: DNA/serum albumin interaction, and in-depth theoretical insights
items.summary: Two novel benzimidazole-based compounds were designed, synthesized, and evaluated for anticancer potential against multiple cancer cell lines, including lung, breast, and liver cancer, alongside a healthy kidney cell line used as a control. One compound demonstrated particularly potent cytotoxic activity against breast and liver cancer cell lines, with its anticancer mechanism investigated through gene expression analysis of pro- and anti-apoptotic markers, oxidative stress measurements, and cellular senescence assays. The results showed that the compounds shifted gene expression toward apoptosis by downregulating anti-apoptotic genes and upregulating pro-apoptotic ones, while also elevating oxidative stress and inducing cellular senescence in breast cancer cells. Fluorescence spectroscopy revealed strong intercalative binding of both compounds to DNA, alongside moderate affinity for serum albumin suggesting favorable transport properties, and molecular docking studies corroborated these experimental observations. Complementary computational analyses including density functional theory calculations and reactivity mapping further supported the biological findings, collectively indicating these benzimidazole derivatives warrant further investigation as anticancer agents.
items.citation: Sevgi Kundu, Senem Akkoç, Yalçın Erzurumlu et al.. Synthesis and multilevel evaluation of benzimidazole-based anticancer compounds: DNA/serum albumin interaction, and in-depth theoretical insights. Molecular and Cellular Biochemistry. 2026

items.title: Delivering biomedicines with stimuli‑responsive biomaterials
items.summary: The abstract is too thin to summarize meaningfully, as it provides only a high-level description of the review's scope without detailing the specific systems studied, methodologies used, or key findings reported.
items.citation: Hemant Singh, Zenab Darban, Aliakbar Ebrahimi et al.. Delivering biomedicines with stimuli‑responsive biomaterials. Communications Materials. 2026

items.title: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking
items.summary: This paper addresses inefficiencies in running decision models — a class of lightweight language model agents designed for rapid categorical reasoning — on existing inference engines built primarily for text generation workloads. The authors identify two key failure modes in current systems: excessive recomputation of shared prefixes and distorted output probabilities that arise from batching approximations. To solve these problems, they propose Flide, an inference engine that separates the logical tree structure of a decision request from its physical execution by flattening it into a single token stream and using a mechanism called ForkAttention to track dependencies via GPU-resident indices, ensuring each branch produces results mathematically identical to an isolated forward pass. Flide supports both standard attention and recurrent Gated DeltaNet layers, uses pre-recorded GPU execution graphs to handle diverse request mixtures efficiently, and allows agent histories to resume from saved checkpoints. Evaluations on hybrid and decision models show that Flide substantially outperforms existing inference engines in query throughput while maintaining the closest fidelity to full-precision reference outputs.
items.citation: Bobo Li, Jiajia Song, Hao Fei et al.. Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Nova V1674 Her as a fast magnetic rotator
items.summary: This study investigated the post-nova quiescent state of V1674 Her using coordinated X-ray observatory observations taken more than two years after its 2021 outburst. The X-ray spectra were modeled with a multi-temperature thermal plasma, suggesting a very massive white dwarf, though a degeneracy between plasma temperature and metallicity prevents a definitive mass constraint. Timing analysis revealed a stable periodic modulation consistent with the spin period of an intermediate polar, with the modulation amplitude decreasing at higher energies, and phase alignment between post-outburst and quiescent observations indicates that accretion onto the same polar regions was rapidly re-established after the eruption. The system belongs to an emerging class of novae that are also intermediate polars, and is one of a small number in which rotational modulation was detected during the outburst supersoft X-ray phase. Based on these findings, the authors propose that the unusually fast rise of V1674 Her during outburst was driven by a fast or centrifugal magnetic rotator wind producing rapid mass loss, rather than the radiation pressure wind typically assumed for classical novae.
items.citation: G. J. M. Luna, M. Orio, A. Dobrotka et al.. Nova V1674 Her as a fast magnetic rotator. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Resolving the spinon hierarchy of the Heisenberg antiferromagnet
items.summary: The paper investigates how fractional spinon excitations collectively account for the full dynamical structure factor of the spin-½ Heisenberg antiferromagnet at zero temperature. Working directly in the thermodynamic limit, the authors decomposed the dynamical structure factor into contributions from successive even numbers of spinons, resolving the hierarchy through the six-spinon level. They found that two-spinon, four-spinon, and six-spinon contributions together account for approximately ninety-nine percent of both the total integrated intensity and the first-frequency-moment sum rule, demonstrating rapid convergence of the spinon hierarchy. The authors also derived a general upper-edge spectral law governing how intensity vanishes at the upper continuum boundary for any even spinon sector, with an edge exponent that grows quickly with spinon number, explaining why higher multiparticle continua carry negligible spectral weight at high energies even though they remain significant within lower-sector continua.
items.citation: Ian P. McCulloch, Jesse J. Osborne. Resolving the spinon hierarchy of the Heisenberg antiferromagnet. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Co-sufficient weighting: leveraging sparsity for more powerful variable selection in the linear model
items.summary: The paper addresses the problem of controlled variable selection in the Gaussian linear model, where the goal is to identify truly associated predictors while controlling error rates. The authors develop a weighting scheme called co-sufficient weights, derived entirely from sufficient statistics of the data itself without requiring external side information, exploiting only a prior belief in sparsity. These weights are constructed to be independent of the p-values used for testing, allowing them to be plugged into weighted multiple testing procedures such as weighted versions of Holm's procedure and the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure without invalidating their error control guarantees. The weighted procedures achieve substantially greater statistical power than their unweighted counterparts when the true coefficient vector is sparse, while maintaining exact or highly robust empirical validity even when sparsity does not hold. Superior performance of the proposed methods over competing approaches is demonstrated across a broad range of simulations and in an application to HIV drug resistance data.
items.citation: Souhardya Sengupta, Lucas Janson. Co-sufficient weighting: leveraging sparsity for more powerful variable selection in the linear model. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Onset of Radiatively Driven Convection in Ice-Covered Freshwater Lakes
items.summary: This paper investigates how radiatively driven convection begins in seasonally ice-covered freshwater lakes, focusing on the development of Rayleigh-Taylor instabilities triggered by solar heating beneath ice. The researchers combined two-dimensional direct numerical simulations with linear stability analysis to examine how thermal stratification, water clarity, and solar forcing influence the formation and growth of these instabilities. They found that strongly stratified lakes undergo a dormancy period before the water column becomes gravitationally unstable, while weakly stratified lakes can develop instabilities almost immediately. The linear analysis successfully captured key features of the instabilities, including their wavelengths, depths, and time-dependent growth rates, showing good agreement with the numerical simulations. When applied to field conditions, the framework predicts that weakly stratified lakes may experience convection onset within a few hours under clear-sky spring conditions, whereas strongly stratified lakes may not develop convection even over the course of a full day.
items.citation: Benjamin J. Smith, Bingfei Yan, Till J. W. Wagner et al.. Onset of Radiatively Driven Convection in Ice-Covered Freshwater Lakes. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Think in 360°: Benchmarking and Bootstrapping Panoramic Video Reasoning
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of understanding panoramic videos, where relevant visual evidence can appear in any direction and at any point in time, requiring models to integrate observations across the full viewing sphere and temporal dimension. The authors introduce a manually annotated benchmark comprising a thousand questions across multiple categories and question types, and use it to evaluate a range of proprietary, open-source, and panoramic-specialized models, revealing that cross-view tracking and sphere-time evidence integration are the most difficult capabilities for current systems. To address these weaknesses, they construct a reasoning dataset by converting verified panoramic observations and successful agentic explorations into question-answer chain-of-thought pairs grounded in real panoramic video. They then train a new model using a combination of panoramic chain-of-thought supervised fine-tuning and a self-distillation strategy in which a teacher with access to verified perspective views guides the student model's reasoning trajectories. The resulting model substantially outperforms its backbone and the previous state of the art on the new benchmark, demonstrating that grounded sphere-time supervision can effectively endow a general video model with panoramic reasoning capabilities.
items.citation: Lidong Lu, Lidong Zou, Xinyi Mao et al.. Think in 360°: Benchmarking and Bootstrapping Panoramic Video Reasoning. arXiv. 2026
