items.title: Translational Barriers and AI-Driven Challenges of Microfluidics-Enabled Wearables and Implantable Systems in Personalized Medicine.
items.summary: This review paper examines the translational pathway of wearable and implantable microfluidic systems from laboratory prototypes to clinical deployment, focusing on their capacity for continuous, minimally invasive biomarker monitoring across multiple biofluids. Rather than treating materials chemistry or device fabrication in isolation, the authors construct a unified framework spanning functional biomaterials, fabrication techniques, diagnostic performance benchmarking, and closed-loop theranostic platforms that combine sensing with autonomous therapeutic delivery. The review systematically analyzes how artificial intelligence is integrated across sensor self-calibration, multiplexed molecular decoding, and on-device decision-making to enable adaptive rather than merely passive health monitoring. A central concern raised is that heterogeneity in biofluid data and disparities in population baselines can propagate algorithmic bias, undermining equitable clinical application. The authors conclude that robust hardware interfaces, standardized validation benchmarks, and alignment with regulatory frameworks are necessary prerequisites for responsible translation of these technologies into personalized medicine.
items.citation: Huang K, Fong CY, Huang X et al.. Translational Barriers and AI-Driven Challenges of Microfluidics-Enabled Wearables and Implantable Systems in Personalized Medicine.. Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany). 2026

items.title: Integrated Microfluidic CRISPR-Based Diagnostic Device for Rapid Testing of HPVs.
items.summary: This study developed a compact, automated microfluidic diagnostic device called Ccard for detecting high-risk human papillomavirus strains associated with cervical cancer, targeting HPV16, HPV18, and an internal reference gene. The system uses a room-temperature nucleic acid release step that bypasses conventional extraction, after which a vacuum pump drives the sample through microfluidic channels into reaction chambers containing lyophilized reagents. Detection is achieved through a single-step combination of recombinase polymerase amplification and CRISPR/Cas13a chemistry, with results read in real time via an Internet of Things-connected device. The assay completes within thirty minutes and demonstrated a very low limit of detection for both viral targets, along with high sensitivity and complete specificity when validated against clinical swab samples. The authors conclude that the Ccard system offers a reliable and precise approach well suited for rapid HPV screening, particularly in resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Wang T, Li L, Wang Y et al.. Integrated Microfluidic CRISPR-Based Diagnostic Device for Rapid Testing of HPVs.. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: ANO6-mediated trogocytosis of cancer-associated fibroblasts promotes pancreatic cancer cell growth and immune suppression
items.summary: This study investigated how pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cells obtain essential lipids despite residing in a poorly vascularized, fibroblast-dense tumor environment. The researchers discovered that cancer-associated fibroblasts acquire lipids from blood-borne particles and transfer them to cancer cells through a process called trogocytosis, in which cancer cells bite off portions of fibroblast plasma membranes at synapse-like contact points. This process is regulated by calcium influx through Orai channels in fibroblasts, which activates the phospholipid scramblase ANO6, causing phosphatidylserine exposure on fibroblast membranes and enabling lipid—including cholesterol—transfer to cancer cells. Beyond fueling tumor growth, ANO6-dependent trogocytosis was found to promote immune suppression by facilitating excessive cholesterol transfer that impairs cytotoxic T cell function. Blocking ANO6 disrupted cholesterol delivery to cancer cells, inhibited tumor growth, and reversed immune suppression, identifying ANO6 as a potential therapeutic target in pancreatic cancer.
items.citation: Charline Ogier, Charles Solomon Akino Mercy, Elena Bondarenko et al.. ANO6-mediated trogocytosis of cancer-associated fibroblasts promotes pancreatic cancer cell growth and immune suppression. Nature Cancer. 2026

items.title: Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective
items.summary: This paper examines the regulatory landscape governing cell-derived extracellular vesicles as therapeutic and diagnostic products, with particular attention to how their acellular nature creates classification ambiguities across existing medicinal product frameworks. The authors surveyed current regulatory approaches in the European Union, the United States, Japan, and other jurisdictions, finding that EVs map inconsistently onto pre-existing categories such as advanced therapy medicinal products or biological drugs, generating jurisdiction-specific classification outcomes. Key technical and operational challenges identified include defining critical quality attributes, establishing potency strategies, and demonstrating comparability across manufacturing processes. The paper argues that EV-based products should be developed within existing medicinal product frameworks provided regulatory tools are applied consistently, and it calls for clarification of grey zones that currently impede harmonized global clinical development. Rather than prescribing new normative frameworks, the work offers a state-of-the-art synthesis intended to inform ongoing regulatory dialogue among international agencies, harmonization bodies, and scientific societies.
items.citation: Tania Limongi, Paola Milla, Barbara Stella et al.. Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective. Journal of Extracellular Vesicles. 2026

items.title: Delivering biomedicines with stimuli‑responsive biomaterials
items.summary: The abstract is too thin to summarize meaningfully beyond restating its own description of the review's scope.
items.citation: Hemant Singh, Zenab Darban, Aliakbar Ebrahimi et al.. Delivering biomedicines with stimuli‑responsive biomaterials. Communications Materials. 2026

items.title: Advances in Polydopamine-Based Nanoplatforms: Antioxidant Mechanisms and Applications in Oxidative Stress-Mediated Diseases
items.summary: This review examines polydopamine (PDA), a melanin-mimetic material with abundant redox-active functional groups, as an antioxidant platform for treating diseases driven by oxidative stress. The authors analyze how PDA-based nanoplatforms neutralize reactive oxygen species through hydrogen atom transfer and electron transfer mechanisms, with sustained activity maintained by dynamic cycling between catechol and quinone moieties. The review systematically describes design strategies for structurally diverse PDA architectures—including solid, mesoporous, hollow, doped, and coated forms—and evaluates how properties such as particle size, composition, and surface charge influence antioxidant performance. The paper further categorizes therapeutic applications according to core pathological challenges, including disrupting ROS-inflammation feedback loops, overcoming biological delivery barriers, remodeling regenerative microenvironments, and regulating programmed cell death. The authors conclude that PDA-based nanoplatforms offer distinct advantages over conventional antioxidant molecules, while identifying gaps in existing systematic knowledge that this comprehensive overview aims to address.
items.citation: Zhilin Wang, Zhu Liu, Luming Song et al.. Advances in Polydopamine-Based Nanoplatforms: Antioxidant Mechanisms and Applications in Oxidative Stress-Mediated Diseases. Nano-Micro Letters. 2026

items.title: Polymer-Based Flexible Wireless Sensors for Health Monitoring
items.summary: This review examines polymer-based flexible wireless sensors used for health monitoring, with a particular focus on an underexplored aspect of the field: the challenges of signal attenuation, noise accumulation, and data distortion within wireless transmission links. Rather than concentrating solely on materials, energy harvesting, or communication hardware as prior work has done, the authors construct a comprehensive framework that integrates signal sensing, wireless link transmission, and intelligent data processing. The review highlights the importance of channel compensation, noise suppression, feature extraction, lightweight artificial intelligence models, and edge computing as strategies for improving data quality and reducing power consumption. It also analyzes how wireless link stability and energy management collectively influence monitoring performance. The authors conclude by proposing design principles intended to guide the development of the next generation of high-reliability, low-power, intelligent flexible health monitoring systems.
items.citation: Heyuan Huang, Gang Xue, Jianning Zhan et al.. Polymer-Based Flexible Wireless Sensors for Health Monitoring. Nano-Micro Letters. 2026

items.title: Large-scale single-molecule analysis of tau proteoforms
items.summary: This paper introduces a method called Iterative Mapping of Proteoforms (IMaP) designed to characterize the full complexity of protein proteoforms at the single-molecule level through massively parallel, iterative probing with fluorescently labeled antibodies. The researchers applied this approach to tau, a protein central to neurodegenerative diseases, using a panel of antibodies targeting isoform-specific epitopes and multiple phosphorylation sites, enabling the simultaneous interrogation of thousands of potential proteoform combinations. IMaP demonstrated high sensitivity, reproducibility, and dynamic range, outperforming conventional methods in resolving closely related proteoform groups across neuronal cell models, organoids, mouse brain tissue, and human samples. The analysis revealed over a hundred distinct tau proteoform groups carrying up to six simultaneous phosphorylation events, with non-random co-occurrence patterns suggesting that tau phosphorylation proceeds through ordered, site-specific processes rather than stochastic accumulation. In human Alzheimer's disease tissue, a specific pattern of co-occurring phosphorylation events was observed, pointing toward a sequential pathway of pathological tau modification.
items.citation: James H. Joly, Vivekananda Budamagunta, Zhengjian Zhang et al.. Large-scale single-molecule analysis of tau proteoforms. Nature Methods. 2026

items.title: Think in 360°: Benchmarking and Bootstrapping Panoramic Video Reasoning
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of understanding panoramic videos, where relevant visual evidence can appear in any direction and at any point in time, requiring models to integrate observations across the full viewing sphere and temporal dimension. The researchers introduced a manually annotated benchmark with a thousand questions spanning multiple categories and question types, and evaluated a range of proprietary, open-source, and panoramic-specialized models, finding that cross-view tracking and sphere-time evidence integration were consistently the weakest capabilities. To address these gaps, they constructed a reasoning dataset by converting verified panoramic observations and successful agentic explorations into tens of thousands of question-answer chain-of-thought pairs grounded in real panoramic video. A new model was then trained on this corpus using a panoramic chain-of-thought supervised fine-tuning stage combined with a self-distillation approach in which a teacher with access to verified perspective views guides the student model's reasoning trajectories. The resulting system substantially outperforms both its backbone model and the previous state of the art, with improvements concentrated on the spatial, cross-view, and temporal reasoning capabilities identified as deficient by the benchmark.
items.citation: Lidong Lu, Lidong Zou, Xinyi Mao et al.. Think in 360°: Benchmarking and Bootstrapping Panoramic Video Reasoning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Knowledge Layer Model (KLM): Evidence-Visible AI Output, Routing Diagnostics, and Negative Results
items.summary: This paper introduces the Knowledge Layer Model (KLM), a specification designed to make the evidential basis of AI-generated answers inspectable, including versioned epistemic assessments, evidence relations, and explicit unknowns. The authors describe a reference implementation called SEDIM within an AI operating system, and report a series of internal experiments evaluating various components of this architecture. The empirical results are mixed and heavily caveated: a routing benchmark showed reasonably high classification accuracy, but a native-model configuration failed entirely on a corrected test, two diagnostic methods performed near chance on a key discrimination task, and a capacity-growth comparison was rendered inconclusive by data quality problems. A text-packing repair demonstrated complete retention of relevant content after fixing a legacy defect, though the authors emphasize this measures text presence rather than answer quality. The paper is notably self-limiting in scope, distinguishing internal author-reported findings from independently verified results and explicitly acknowledging that evidence visibility does not imply correctness, security, or regulatory compliance, with independent replication left as future work.
items.citation: Omer Asim Ozturk, Cihan Aydiner. The Knowledge Layer Model (KLM): Evidence-Visible AI Output, Routing Diagnostics, and Negative Results. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Current-driven transient dynamics of magnetic-octupole domain walls in noncollinear antiferromagnets
items.summary: This paper investigates the transient dynamics of magnetic-octupole domain walls in the noncollinear antiferromagnet Mn₃Sn driven by spin-orbit torques, a topic relevant to ultrafast spintronic device design. Using a multipole micromagnetic framework, the authors examined how domain walls behave both during and after current pulses, finding that the three symmetry-related wall types respond equivalently to current driving, in contrast to their distinct field-driven behavior. Post-pulse relaxation in a representative wall is dominated by the unwinding of current-induced rotations in the surrounding octupole domains, a process captured analytically, while composite walls exhibit an additional slower relaxation channel tied to the relative motion of their constituent walls. The response timescales depend systematically on material parameters such as exchange stiffness and magnetic anisotropy. Together, these findings establish the intrinsic relaxation channels and time scales that govern pulse-controlled positioning of domain walls in antiferromagnetic spintronic devices.
items.citation: Myoung-Woo Yoo, Axel Hoffmann. Current-driven transient dynamics of magnetic-octupole domain walls in noncollinear antiferromagnets. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Benchmarking Single-Photon Sources for Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution
items.summary: This paper investigates how the quality of photon sources affects the performance of Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution, a protocol that removes the need to trust measurement devices. The authors compared implementations using Weak Coherent Pulses, which suffer from Poissonian photon-number statistics and an inherent trade-off between single- and multi-photon emissions, against Quantum Dot single-photon sources, which exhibit sub-Poissonian statistics characterized by low antibunching. Applying a decoy-state security analysis to both source types, they found that Quantum Dot sources outperform optimized Weak Coherent Pulse configurations across all transmission distances, even at moderate mean photon numbers. The study also incorporated photon indistinguishability into the security analysis through Hong-Ou-Mandel interference visibility and demonstrated that both source types are highly sensitive to even small departures from perfect indistinguishability, with significant consequences for achievable key rates and maximum transmission distances.
items.citation: Janka Memmen, Yvonne Lasars, Tobias Heindel et al.. Benchmarking Single-Photon Sources for Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Less Loss, Fixed Weights: Logit Corrections for Forgetting
items.summary: The paper investigates whether the performance degradation that language models experience after fine-tuning or continued pretraining — commonly called "forgetting" — can be reversed through simple, fixed adjustments to the model's output token predictions, without modifying the model's weights. The researchers tested vocabulary-level biases and temperature scaling across a range of base and derived model pairs spanning different parameter scales, fitting these corrections on held-out text to estimate how much of the lost predictive performance could be recovered. They found that vocabulary bias alone recovers only a small fraction of the lost performance, while combining bias with temperature scaling improves recovery somewhat, though still leaving the majority of the loss out of reach. Models that underwent continued pretraining on mathematics showed the greatest forgetting and were the least amenable to correction by these methods. A controlled simulation in which models were randomly damaged — with no structured bias or temperature shift introduced — nonetheless showed partial recovery from the combined correction, suggesting the method captures some generic statistical regularities but cannot address most of the structural changes induced by real fine-tuning.
items.citation: Hanyu Yang. Less Loss, Fixed Weights: Logit Corrections for Forgetting. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ID2Pattern: Pretraining Generalizable Identity Behavior Patterns for Transaction Risk Foundation Models
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of incorporating high-cardinality identity fields—such as card, device, and account identifiers—into pretrained models for online payment transaction risk assessment. The authors argue that these fields carry valuable behavioral signals, but their ever-growing vocabularies and lack of semantic meaning make conventional encoding approaches inadequate. To address this, they propose ID2Pattern, a pretraining framework that introduces a Local Anonymous ID tokenizer to capture how identities appear and recur within a transaction sequence without relying on specific identity values, combined with a multi-scale pattern codebook that distills these tokenized sequences into discrete, reusable behavioral patterns. The framework was evaluated on a large industrial dataset and multiple public datasets, consistently outperforming strong baselines across both settings. Crucially, ID2Pattern maintained its effectiveness even when identity values were entirely unseen during training, demonstrating strong generalization to new users and markets.
items.citation: Ze Zhao, Haoyu Jiang, Weiyu Han et al.. ID2Pattern: Pretraining Generalizable Identity Behavior Patterns for Transaction Risk Foundation Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: 3D-printed architectures for (bio)sensing
items.summary: This perspective paper examines how three-dimensional printing technologies are transforming the design and fabrication of biosensing and chemical sensing devices by enabling fully integrated, all-in-one systems that consolidate sample preparation, fluid handling, and detection within a single manufacturing workflow. The authors surveyed recent advances across biomedical, environmental, and wearable sensing applications, analyzing the capabilities of additive manufacturing techniques such as fused deposition modeling, stereolithography, and digital light processing. A central theme is the relationship between materials and device function, with particular attention to conductive filament preparation, microchannel design, and surface functionalization strategies. The paper identifies key challenges including print resolution, material conductivity, biomolecule stability, and sustainability, and proposes solutions such as hybrid printing, low-temperature filaments, chemometrics-assisted design, and use of recycled materials. The authors conclude by outlining a development roadmap that emphasizes scalability, customization, and integration with artificial intelligence and the internet of things, positioning three-dimensional printing as a transformative platform for next-generation sensing systems.
items.citation: Panagiota M. Kalligosfyri, Gabriella Iula, Grazia Nota et al.. 3D-printed architectures for (bio)sensing. Biosensors and Biomolecular Electronics. 2026

items.title: Rapid visual and direct detection of Acinetobacter baumannii and carbapenem resistance by oligoDNA-gold nanoparticles biosensor in clinical samples.
items.summary: This paper addressed the urgent need for rapid identification of *Acinetobacter baumannii* and its carbapenem resistance genes in clinical settings, where conventional methods are slow and infrastructure-intensive. The researchers developed oligonucleotide-functionalized gold nanoparticle biosensors targeting a conserved region of the *nucAb* gene for species identification, along with separate biosensors for the carbapenem resistance genes *bla*OXA-23 and *bla*NDM, applied directly to clinical respiratory samples without requiring DNA purification or amplification. The *bla*NDM biosensor demonstrated broad utility by detecting multiple variants of the gene across several clinically important Gram-negative pathogens beyond *A. baumannii*. The biosensors produced visible colorimetric results within thirty minutes and achieved a low detection limit, supporting their potential use for rapid clinical decision-making and antimicrobial resistance surveillance.
items.citation: Chalana A, Gupta V, Sharma P et al.. Rapid visual and direct detection of Acinetobacter baumannii and carbapenem resistance by oligoDNA-gold nanoparticles biosensor in clinical samples.. Diagnostic microbiology and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: Nanozyme-based biosensors for pathogenic microorganism detection: a mini-review
items.citation: Yang T, Ling Y, Zhang E et al.. Nanozyme-based biosensors for pathogenic microorganism detection: a mini-review. Frontiers in microbiology. 2026

items.title: Cross-validated SPR/SERS dual-mode fiber biosensor for rapid and accurate detection of Salmonella Typhimurium in foods.
items.summary: This paper developed a portable fiber-optic biosensor that simultaneously harnesses surface plasmon resonance and surface-enhanced Raman scattering to detect the foodborne pathogen Salmonella Typhimurium in real food matrices. The sensing platform uses gold-film-coated tapered optical fibers functionalized with bacteriophage capture probes, paired with sea-urchin-shaped gold/silver nanoparticles conjugated to a Raman reporter dye and a second phage, forming a sandwich complex around target bacteria. Both detection channels operate from a single binding reaction and the entire workflow is completed in under an hour, achieving very low limits of detection in the low tens of CFU/mL range for both modes. The biosensor was validated in fish, vegetable, and milk samples, demonstrating strong accuracy and resistance to matrix interference. Critically, the two independent signal channels provide mutual cross-verification that substantially reduces false-positive results, offering a more reliable platform for on-site food safety surveillance.
items.citation: Zhu S, Su Y, Wang Y et al.. Cross-validated SPR/SERS dual-mode fiber biosensor for rapid and accurate detection of Salmonella Typhimurium in foods.. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Rapid and visual detection of group B Streptococcus based on an ERA-CasMNPs colorimetric biosensor.
items.summary: This paper addressed the need for rapid, sensitive, and equipment-light detection of Group B Streptococcus, a pathogen linked to serious perinatal complications. The researchers developed a biosensor called ERA-CasMNPs by combining enzymatic recombinase amplification targeting the GBS-specific cfb gene, CRISPR/Cas12a-based sequence recognition and cleavage activity, and a colorimetric readout generated through horseradish peroxidase-functionalized magnetic nanoparticles. The integrated system produces a visible color signal, enabling results without complex instrumentation. Testing against cultured clinical bacterial isolates showed the biosensor achieved sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy comparable to quantitative PCR, with a low detection limit and a total assay time under ninety minutes. The authors conclude that ERA-CasMNPs offers a promising platform for rapid, visual GBS detection suitable for resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Guo H, Jiang Y, Li D et al.. Rapid and visual detection of group B Streptococcus based on an ERA-CasMNPs colorimetric biosensor.. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Advancements in biosensor Technologies for Pathogen Detection: Innovations and comparison with conventional diagnostic approaches.
items.summary: This review paper examines biosensor technologies as alternatives to conventional diagnostic methods for detecting pathogens across clinical, food safety, and environmental monitoring contexts. The authors surveyed and compared established diagnostic approaches such as culture-based methods, ELISA, and PCR against a range of biosensor platforms, including electrochemical, optical, nanoparticle, microfluidic, and paper-based systems. The review discusses the fundamental sensing principles, design strategies, and applications of each biosensor type, highlighting their advantages in portability, sensitivity, multiplexing capability, and suitability for point-of-care use. While advances in nanomaterials, biorecognition strategies, and signal-transduction mechanisms have expanded the potential of biosensors, the authors identify persistent challenges including sensor stability, reproducibility, fabrication complexity, scalability, and the need for rigorous validation. The review concludes by outlining future perspectives for integrating biosensor technologies into practical diagnostic settings where conventional methods face limitations in speed and accessibility.
items.citation: Singhal P, Misra S, Prakash A et al.. Advancements in biosensor Technologies for Pathogen Detection: Innovations and comparison with conventional diagnostic approaches.. Journal of microbiological methods. 2026

items.title: Development of a NiCoFe-LDH/Ketjenblack-enhanced electrochemical antibacterial peptide biosensor for Aeromonas hydrophila detection in seawater samples.
items.summary: This paper describes the development of an electrochemical biosensor designed to rapidly detect the fish pathogen *Aeromonas hydrophila* in aquaculture settings, including real seawater samples. The biosensor was constructed by modifying a screen-printed carbon electrode with a nanocomposite of ternary nickel-cobalt-iron layered double hydroxide combined with Ketjenblack carbon, synthesized via a one-pot precipitation method, and functionalized with an antibacterial peptide as the biorecognition element. The nanocomposite was characterized using multiple analytical techniques confirming its high-activity nanosheet structure and rapid electron transfer properties, which amplify the electrochemical signal. Under optimized conditions at room temperature, the sensor achieved detection within half an hour, demonstrated a wide linear detection range, an exceptionally low detection limit, high reproducibility, minimal cross-reactivity with other bacteria, and strong performance in spiked seawater samples. The authors report this as the first electrochemical antibacterial peptide-based biosensor for *A. hydrophila* validated in seawater, highlighting its potential for practical aquaculture monitoring.
items.citation: Kızılkurtlu AA, Arancı K, Gülyüz S et al.. Development of a NiCoFe-LDH/Ketjenblack-enhanced electrochemical antibacterial peptide biosensor for Aeromonas hydrophila detection in seawater samples.. Mikrochimica acta. 2026

items.title: Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support
items.summary: This review paper examines the application of federated learning as a privacy-preserving approach to training artificial intelligence models across diverse healthcare data modalities, including medical imaging, electronic health records, wearable sensor outputs, and clinical decision support systems. The authors conducted a broad literature review spanning multiple clinical domains such as chronic disease management, elder care, and biomedical imaging, surveying how federated learning enables collaborative model training across institutions without transferring raw patient data. The paper finds that federated learning substantially reduces direct exposure of sensitive clinical information and improves alignment with privacy regulations, though it does not guarantee confidentiality on its own, as vulnerabilities including gradient leakage, model inversion, and membership inference attacks require additional protective measures. Key implementation barriers identified include system heterogeneity across institutions, data imbalance, communication bottlenecks, and fairness concerns that can undermine model performance across diverse populations. Drawing on both research findings and practical considerations, the authors offer recommendations for regulators, developers, and healthcare systems aimed at advancing safe, equitable, and geographically distributed federated learning in medicine.
items.venue: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
items.citation: Shon G. Nemane, Vaishnavi M. Sarad, Dhiraj P. Tulaskar et al.. Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support. Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges
items.summary: This systematic review examined CRISPR-Cas systems as potential next-generation antimicrobials to address the growing crisis of multidrug-resistant bacteria, for which conventional antibiotics are increasingly ineffective. The authors synthesized preclinical and experimental evidence on the antibacterial mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational potential of various CRISPR effectors, including Cas9, Cas12, and Cas13, targeting resistant bacterial strains. The reviewed studies demonstrated that CRISPR-Cas systems can effectively kill or resensitize multidrug-resistant bacteria through mechanisms such as chromosomal double-strand break induction, resistance plasmid curing, and RNA-targeted cleavage. Among delivery platforms—including bacteriophages, conjugative plasmids, and nanoparticles—phage-mediated delivery showed the most consistent efficacy, and one CRISPR-enhanced engineered bacteriophage cocktail has progressed to clinical evaluation. Despite this promise, the review identified substantial barriers to clinical translation, including limited host range, physiological instability, emergence of escape mutations, and insufficient safety data, highlighting the need for optimized delivery systems, multiplex targeting strategies, and clearer regulatory frameworks.
items.citation: Maha S.I. Wizrah. CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Traditional fermented food microbial ecosystems oriented towards industrial standards: multi-dimensional characterization and artificial regulation
items.summary: This review examines the microbial ecosystems underlying traditional fermented foods, which are inherently variable due to spontaneous fermentation processes driven by complex interactions among microbes, substrates, and environmental conditions. The paper addresses how this variability poses challenges for quality control and standardization in industrial settings. The authors highlight how multi-omics approaches can be integrated to comprehensively characterize microbial composition, community dynamics, metabolite profiles, interactions, and phage activity within these ecosystems. They also survey regulatory strategies—including the use of functional strains, synthetic microbial communities, bacteriophage control, and physicochemical modulation—as means to guide fermentation toward consistent, predictable outcomes. The review concludes by identifying future directions and challenges in transitioning from empirical, tradition-based practice to scalable, industrially standardized fermentation.
items.citation: M T Wu, Jiayao Wang, Yu Wang et al.. Traditional fermented food microbial ecosystems oriented towards industrial standards: multi-dimensional characterization and artificial regulation. npj Science of Food. 2026

items.title: Personalized cancer vaccines: bridging immune-oncology and precision medicine for advanced therapeutics
items.summary: This review examines the current landscape and emerging directions of personalized cancer vaccines, which are designed to target patient-specific tumor antigens and mount tailored immune responses against cancer. The authors survey multiple vaccine platform types—including DNA, mRNA, peptide, dendritic cell, and whole-cell approaches—and discuss immunological barriers such as tumor heterogeneity, immunosuppressive microenvironments, and insufficient immune memory that have historically limited clinical translation. To overcome these challenges, the review highlights advances in nanotechnology-based delivery systems, including lipid-polymer hybrids, biomimetic membranes, and stimulus-responsive materials, which improve lymph node targeting, dendritic cell activation, and antigen presentation. The integration of artificial intelligence for neoantigen selection and multiomics for patient stratification is presented as a means to accelerate and refine vaccine design, while combination strategies with immune checkpoint inhibitors are shown to further enhance and sustain antitumor immunity. Clinical evidence, particularly in melanoma and pancreatic cancer with personalized mRNA vaccines, is cited as grounds for renewed optimism that these next-generation approaches can shift cancer care from reactive treatment toward proactive, precision-driven immunotherapy.
items.citation: Leiguang Ye, Guo Zhao, Jiaxiu Ma et al.. Personalized cancer vaccines: bridging immune-oncology and precision medicine for advanced therapeutics. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Novel Strategies Against Fungal Infections: Repurposing Existing Drugs and Advancing Nanotherapeutics
items.summary: This review examines the growing global burden of fungal infections, which has been exacerbated by expanding immunocompromised populations, antibiotic overuse, and the rise of multidrug-resistant fungi that undermine conventional antifungal treatments. The authors surveyed two broad emerging strategies: drug repurposing, which identifies non-antifungal agents with intrinsic antifungal activity or synergistic potential when combined with existing drugs, thereby bypassing the need for entirely new drug discovery; and nanomaterial-based approaches, encompassing polymeric and metallic nanomaterials designed to improve drug solubility, enable targeted delivery, penetrate biofilms, and reduce host toxicity. Together, these strategies are argued to offer multimodal fungicidal mechanisms that lower the likelihood of resistance developing. Although the evidence base remains largely preclinical, the authors conclude that the convergence of repurposing and nanotechnology presents a promising pathway toward safer and more effective antifungal therapies, and they call for continued interdisciplinary effort to advance these approaches into clinical use.
items.citation: Zimeng You, Kaiwen Zhuang, Takashi Sugita et al.. Novel Strategies Against Fungal Infections: Repurposing Existing Drugs and Advancing Nanotherapeutics. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Dittany: Contribution-Guided Repair Framework for MAS Applications
items.summary: The paper investigates runtime repair of large language model-based multi-agent system applications, which often produce partial or flawed results that fail to fully satisfy task requirements. The authors developed a framework called Dittany that constructs a contribution graph by deriving expected contributions and acceptance conditions from task requirements and method specifications, then uses this graph at runtime to identify unmet conditions and determine which intermediate results remain valid. When failures are detected, the framework applies either action-level correction when sufficient inputs are available or graph-level recovery when prerequisites need revision, in both cases preserving validated contributions and verifying repaired outputs before downstream use. Evaluation across a large set of applications and tasks showed that the framework achieved substantially higher task accuracy than both native execution and competing recovery baselines, while keeping token consumption considerably lower than comparable repair approaches. Ablation studies confirmed that combining both repair scopes outperforms using graph-level repair alone in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
items.citation: Hanqi Sun, Yuchen Shao, Hanyi Si et al.. Dittany: Contribution-Guided Repair Framework for MAS Applications. arXiv. 2026

items.title: SATFRONT: Detecting Atmospheric Fronts with Satellite Data using Machine Learning
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of automatically detecting atmospheric fronts, which are major drivers of high-impact mid-latitude weather, without relying on the gridded reanalysis or forecast data that most existing deep learning approaches require. The authors developed SATFRONT, a machine learning framework that identifies cold, warm, and occluded fronts over Europe using geostationary satellite observations as its primary input, with reanalysis data available as an optional supplement. The model was trained on frontal analyses from multiple European national meteorological services and validated against independent analyses from the UK Met Office. Using satellite data alone, SATFRONT achieves detection skill that falls within the range of inter-agency agreement among human analysts and substantially outperforms an existing operational rule-based satellite-based front detector; incorporating reanalysis data further improves performance, particularly for the precise placement of individual fronts. The study demonstrates that automated, high-temporal-frequency frontal analysis directly from satellite imagery is feasible, opening pathways for near-real-time frontal detection in time-critical forecasting applications.
items.citation: Ioannis Dravilas, Miruna Stoicescu, Roope Tervo et al.. SATFRONT: Detecting Atmospheric Fronts with Satellite Data using Machine Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Soft X-Ray Detection Down to the Nitrogen K-Edge Using a Pixelated iLGAD Sensor
items.summary: This paper investigated inverse low-gain avalanche diode sensors designed to extend hybrid pixel detector technology into the soft X-ray energy regime, where achieving adequate quantum efficiency and signal-to-noise ratio has remained a longstanding challenge. The researchers integrated iLGAD sensors with thin entrance windows and systematically compared two gain layer designs — a standard gain layer and a shallow gain layer — evaluating their spectral response across photon energies and operating temperatures. Single-photon resolution was demonstrated at energies as low as the nitrogen K-edge region with a signal-to-noise ratio sufficient for practical detection. A notable double-peak feature was observed in the energy spectra, attributed to the dependence of charge multiplication on the depth at which photons are absorbed within the sensor. The study also developed a phenomenological spectral fitting model that allows quantitative extraction of key structural parameters, providing a foundation for scaling this technology into large-area, high-frame-rate detectors suitable for soft X-ray applications such as ptychography, spectroscopy, and resonant scattering at synchrotron and free-electron laser facilities.
items.citation: Shuqi Li, Anna Bergamaschi, Ashish Bisht et al.. Soft X-Ray Detection Down to the Nitrogen K-Edge Using a Pixelated iLGAD Sensor. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Tests of equivalence principle violation in doubly coupled dark energy
items.summary: This paper investigates a class of dark energy models in which dark matter couples to a scalar field while baryons do not, thereby violating the weak equivalence principle, and asks whether such violations can be detected using galaxy surveys. The authors generalize an existing coupled dark energy framework by introducing an additional nonminimal coupling between the scalar field and gravity, calling the result "doubly coupled dark energy," and define a parameter that quantifies equivalence principle violation on cosmological scales in a model-independent manner. Using forecasting methods applied to current and upcoming spectroscopic surveys, they assess the ability of these instruments to constrain the relevant coupling strengths while keeping the initial power spectrum shape and galaxy bias flexible across multiple bins. Among the surveys considered, the most futuristic radio telescope array is found to deliver the tightest constraints on the coupling strength, though the constraints degrade when both couplings are simultaneously varied and can be recovered by increasing the number of detected galaxies. The work demonstrates that large-scale structure surveys offer a viable route to testing equivalence principle violation in the dark sector.
items.citation: Yannick Kegel, Ziyang Zheng, Luca Amendola. Tests of equivalence principle violation in doubly coupled dark energy. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Proof-Carrying Evolution: Black-Box Search, White-Box Flight
items.summary: This paper investigates whether large language models can assist in designing control systems whose correctness can be formally verified. The authors introduce proof-carrying evolution, a framework in which a search process proposes controllers paired with mathematical certificates of their properties, with selection guided by whether candidates pass certificate checks and only certified designs deployed. Four language models were compared against classical search and synthesis methods across three control problems: spacecraft docking under a speed constraint, pursuit of a maneuvering target, and attitude control on a nonlinear manifold, with formal proofs generated in Lean 4 for the best solutions found. The strongest language models outperformed standard classical baselines on the linear problems, though a classical optimizer that jointly selects certificates largely closed this performance gap, and rankings among pursuit solutions were not robust to changes in the underlying dynamics model. On the nonlinear attitude control problem, language models did not consistently outperform classical evolutionary search, and all automated methods remained below a hand-tuned controller, while experiments confirmed that retaining certified candidates during search was essential for producing any certified final designs.
items.citation: Amit Jain, Sergio Sanchez-Hurtado, Victor Rodriguez-Fernandez et al.. Proof-Carrying Evolution: Black-Box Search, White-Box Flight. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A richness-sensitive Acoustic Biodiversity Index from species-level detections: classifier benchmarking, false-positive control and validation against standard soundscape indices in an African savanna and an urban zoo
items.summary: The paper develops and validates a revised Acoustic Biodiversity Index built from species-level detections rather than raw sound energy, addressing a known weakness of conventional acoustic indices in tracking species richness. The authors benchmarked four classifier approaches on a labelled tropical bird call dataset and found that BirdNET embeddings combined with logistic regression performed best, while also demonstrating that naive recording splits substantially inflate apparent classifier accuracy. They applied the best-performing classifier with location and season filtering to recordings from an African savanna and an urban zoo, incorporating a post-hoc plausibility filter that removed a substantial number of high-confidence but geographically implausible detections. The revised index, which expresses Shannon diversity of detections normalised against a regional species pool, correlated strongly with observed species richness across recorded hours, substantially outperforming six standard soundscape indices including the Acoustic Complexity Index. The authors conclude that species-level indices with explicit false-positive control, a declared regional reference pool, and effort standardisation offer a more interpretable and ecologically meaningful biodiversity indicator than energy-based acoustic indices.
items.citation: Muhammad Saeed, Dmitry Mikhaylov, Mohamed H. Alhosani et al.. A richness-sensitive Acoustic Biodiversity Index from species-level detections: classifier benchmarking, false-positive control and validation against standard soundscape indices in an African savanna and an urban zoo. arXiv. 2026
